options.text: SHUT WINDOW: close it again and stay inside.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} shuts the window. The door gives way.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt after “Open the window”: GO OUT (“It’s the only way. Hurry, come on!”) or SHUT WINDOW (→ “Kara and Todd fighting”). The chart has no SHUT WINDOW node; it is the template’s, and it leads where FACE TODD does, to DEFEND ALICE. No stat change.

nodes.title: Out on the roof
nodes.whenNot: Alice did not climb out of the window.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Alice}} is out on the roof in the rain, calling for you: “{{KARA}}!” Behind you the door splinters.

options.text: JOIN {{ALICE}}: climb out after her.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} climbs out. {{Todd}} bursts in: “COME BACK HERE RIGHT NOW!” He grabs for her through the window, but she pulls free, and she and {{Alice}} slide down the wet roof to the ground.

options.text: FACE {{TODD}}: stay, and turn to face him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} turns from the window as {{Todd}} comes through the door.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt after GO OUT: JOIN ALICE (“COME BACK HERE RIGHT NOW!”) or FACE TODD (→ DEFEND ALICE). Joining her is the chart’s check ESCAPE BY WINDOW (✓) → RUN TO THE BUS, or FAIL TO ESCAPE BY WINDOW (✗) → TODD BROKE KARA OUTSIDE (ending, not-required icon). Experienced mode, as the benchmark models it (wiki: “If you are on Experienced mode … Todd will try to grab you and exit the window”; on Casual a failure leads to DEFEND ALICE instead). The 25% risk is the benchmark’s value; no source gives one. Where {{Alice}} is during the fight after FACE TODD is not stated by any source and is left unsaid. No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Todd}} breaks in
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not break into the room with Kara inside.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in {{Alice}}’s room. {{Todd}} is through the door, belt in hand, standing over you: “The fuck are you doin’ here? Get outta my way!”

situationWhen.text: You are holding the lamp.

options.text: REFUSE: stay where you are, between him and {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “No. I won’t let you hurt her.” “You won’t let me? What the fuck are you talkin’ about? You’re just a goddamn piece of plastic. You seem to have a problem and I’m going to fix it for good.”

options.text: ACCEPT: step aside.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} starts to move away. {{Alice}}: “NO!” {{Todd}}: “I said get outta here!” {{Kara}} stops where she is: “No.”

nodes.adaptationNote: TODD BREAKS INTO BEDROOM, then the template’s prompt under [ OUT OF TIME ]: REFUSE or ACCEPT, both → “Kara and Todd fighting” (DEFEND ALICE). The wiki says the same prompt follows the lamp, talking to {{Alice}} and doing nothing (“This also occurs in scenarios such as facing Todd, talking to Alice, not speaking to Alice, or failing to make a choice. Choosing ‘ACCEPT’ in any scenario will have Kara move away and change her mind”); the benchmark offers it there. After FACE TODD and SHUT WINDOW the template goes straight to the fight, so it is not offered there. No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Todd}}’s gun
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not reach Alice first while the gun was within reach, or Kara never saw the gun.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, picking yourself up off the floor. {{Todd}} has gone into {{Alice}}’s room with his belt, and she is screaming. The door of {{Todd}}’s bedroom is open; the handgun you saw is in the drawer of his nightstand.

options.text: TAKE GUN: get the handgun from {{Todd}}’s nightstand before you go in.
options.fact: You took {{Todd}}’s handgun from his nightstand.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes the handgun from the drawer.

options.text: Go straight to {{Alice}}’s room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes straight to {{Alice}}’s door.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TAKE GUN, an optional step on the way to GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD, after TODD GOES UPSTAIRS, TODD SHOVES KARA UPSTAIRS or TODD TAKES ALICE TO HER ROOM, and only if the gun was seen in A New Home (GUN SEEN IN ‘A NEW HOME’, gunDiscovered). It is not offered again to a {{Kara}} who already took the gun upstairs. Taking it sets gun; in this chapter the gun leaves the house only with {{Todd}} dead (KARA SHOT TODD or ALICE SHOT TODD), the only cross-chapter carriers of the gun. The earlier version merged the fight into this scene with risks of 10% and 30% and an {{Alice}} relationship decrease when she fired; none had a source, and the template has no arrow in this chapter, so all three are gone.

nodes.title: Get to {{Alice}}
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not reach Alice before Kara.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, outside {{Alice}}’s door. Inside, {{Todd}}: “{{Alice}}! You and I have a little score to settle. Come on, come here you little brat!” {{Alice}}: “No, Daddy, no! Don’t hurt me! Please, don’t hurt me!” {{Todd}}: “Come outta there! Don’t make me come and get you! It’s all your fault! She left because of you! … I’m gonna give you a thrashin’ you won’t forget in a hurry.”

situationWhen.text: You have {{Todd}}’s handgun in your hand.

options.text: THREATEN WITH GUN: go in and point the gun at him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes in. {{Alice}}: “Stop! Please, stop, daddy!” {{Todd}}: “It’s for your own good, {{Alice}}…” {{Kara}} raises the gun: “That’s enough! Leave her alone!” “What the fuck are you doin’? Put down the gun and get the fuck outta here! That’s an order!” “No… I want you to leave her alone.” “You want? What do you mean you want? What ya gonna do? You gonna shoot me, is that it? You gonna shoot a human? You seem to have a problem, I think we need to fix that.” {{Alice}}: “Watch out, {{Kara}}!” {{Todd}} lunges: “Come here, bitch…” He knocks the gun out of her hand.

options.text: DEFEND {{ALICE}}: go in and stop him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes in. {{Alice}}: “Stop! Please, stop, daddy!” {{Todd}}: “It’s for your own good, {{Alice}}… For your own good…” {{Kara}}: “Leave her alone!” “The fuck are you doin’? Get outta here, that’s an order... you hear me?” “No… I want you to leave {{Alice}} alone.” “You want? What do you mean you want? You don’t want anything, you’re just a goddamn piece of plastic. I think you got a problem. We need to fix that.”

options.text: Stay outside the door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} stays outside the door. The belt comes down again and again, and then {{Alice}} goes quiet. When {{Kara}} looks in, {{Todd}} is crouched beside {{Alice}}: “It’s all over now… Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…” He sees {{Kara}}. “This is your fault. This is all your fault. None of this woulda happened if it weren’t for you. THIS IS ALL YOUR FAULT!” He turns on her and destroys her.

nodes.adaptationNote: GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD (focus point). With the gun, going in is THREATEN WITH GUN → DEFEND ALICE (template “IF Took the gun”); without it, DEFEND ALICE (template “IF Didn’t take the gun”); the benchmark offers only the one that matches. Staying out is the template’s [ TIME: Take too much time ] (“Leads to the same outcome as ‘Don’t go / Don’t become a deviant’”), the chart’s KARA IS TOO SLOW → TODD KILLS ALICE; the wiki: “It is possible to take the gun without killing Todd however … Kara will have to do nothing which will result in Alice and then Kara too”. No stat change.

nodes.title: The gun on the floor
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not go in with the gun.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, on the floor of {{Alice}}’s room with {{Todd}} on top of you, hitting you. {{Alice}}: “Please stop! NO! Leave her alone!” {{Todd}}: “I own you! You do as I say!” The gun lies on the floor, just within reach.

options.text: Go for the gun.
options.fact: You shot {{Todd}} dead in {{Alice}}’s room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} gets her fingers on the gun and fires. {{Todd}} falls and does not get up.

options.text: Keep fighting him off with your hands.
options.fact: {{Alice}} shot her father dead to save you.
options.outcome: {{Todd}} pins {{Kara}} down: “Fuckin’ machine. This is what you get for disobeying me. I do what I want with the little brat, you hear? She’s mine. Say goodbye, tin can... And this time you won’t be coming back.” A shot. {{Todd}} falls. {{Alice}} is standing behind him with the gun in both hands.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s group after THREATEN WITH GUN → DEFEND ALICE: KARA KILLS TODD or ALICE KILLS TODD (STUN TODD is the unarmed outcome). PowerPyx: “When prompted to mash X to pick up the gun again, do so and Kara will shoot him” versus “don’t do it – Alice will pick it up and shoot him”; the template: “Win the fight unharmed” or “Get hit a few times” → Kara kills Todd, “Lose the fight / Don’t reach the gun in time” → Alice kills Todd. Modelled as the player’s choice, with no risk: the chart draws a choice group, not a pass/fail pair. The earlier version made {{Alice}} the shooter on a failed 10% roll and lowered her relationship; neither had a source.

nodes.title: Run to the bus
nodes.whenNot: Todd was not shot.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Todd}} lies dead on the floor of {{Alice}}’s room, and the house is quiet except for the rain.

situationWhen.text: You fired the shot.
{{Alice}} fired the shot, to save you.

facts: You and {{Alice}} left {{Todd}}’s house on a night bus in the rain, with his handgun and nothing else.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} takes the gun and {{Alice}}’s hand. They go down the stairs, open the front door and run through the rain to the bus stop across the street, where a night bus is waiting. They get on, and the bus pulls away.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s OPEN FRONT DOOR → RUN TO THE BUS → KARA SHOT TODD or ALICE SHOT TODD (endings, cross-chapter icon; wiki: “allows ‘Use gun’ path during Fugitives and disallows ‘Meet Todd’ path during Battle for Detroit”). PowerPyx: “unmissable after having shot Todd”, and the wiki: “if Todd is already dead, the bus will just wait there forever”, so there is no choice and no risk. Sets todd to false and keeps gun; records the ending in ch07Outcome. No stat change (the public-opinion drop comes later, from the motel news in On the Run).

nodes.title: Defend {{Alice}}
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not fight Todd unarmed in Alice’s room.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in {{Alice}}’s room, between {{Todd}} and {{Alice}}. {{Alice}}: “Watch out, {{Kara}}!” {{Todd}}: “Come here, bitch…”
facts: You fought {{Todd}} off in {{Alice}}’s room and knocked him down. He is hurt, not dead.

outcomes.0: {{Todd}} charges. {{Kara}} dodges, and he punches a hole in the window. He catches her, throws her down and hits her. {{Alice}}: “Stop, Dad! Don’t hurt her! Leave her alone!” {{Todd}}: “I own you! You do as I say!” {{Kara}} gets up and shoves him with everything she has. He goes down hard and stays there, dazed and bleeding, and reaches out to his daughter: “{{Alice}}, honey… {{Alice}}... Look... Look, Daddy’s wounded... Be a good little girl... Come... Come… Come help, Daddy…”

nodes.adaptationNote: DEFEND ALICE without the gun, which the chart resolves only as STUN TODD (PowerPyx: “no matter how good or bad you are in the unarmed melee-combat against Todd, you will always have an option to push him in some way to stun him”; wiki: “Failing to push Todd will give Kara a second opportunity to push him and she can take as long as she wants”). The chart has no death in {{Alice}}’s room, so there is no risk here; the Kara page’s “fails to win … Todd will break her apart” is taken to mean the later fights. Reached after DEFEND ALICE (K04a), after TODD BREAKS INTO BEDROOM (K03h), and after FACE TODD or SHUT WINDOW. The fight’s quick-time details (the shelf, the window) are the wiki’s Notes; {{Todd}} begging {{Alice}} is the template’s line (the wiki says it plays if {{Kara}} looks at him). Sets ch07Fought: {{Todd}} is hurt (the Todd Williams page: “If Kara fought and stunned him, he will be seen with a bandage”).

nodes.title: Leave the room
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not stun Todd in the bedroom.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Todd}} is down on the floor of {{Alice}}’s room, wounded and begging her to help him. {{Alice}} is beside you. The doorway is clear.

options.text: RUN AWAY: take {{Alice}} and leave the room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}} out into the corridor. {{Todd}} gets up behind them: “You… You bitches! Come here... You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s lone RUN AWAY button after “Win the fight: Todd is stunned”, outside a choice group. The chart calls it LEAVE THE ROOM, followed by TODD CHASES KARA. Offered separately before the corridor and exit-route actions; no risk and no stat change.

nodes.title: {{Todd}} is down
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not stun Todd in Alice’s room.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the upstairs corridor with {{Alice}}. Behind you, {{Todd}} is getting up from the floor of her room. The stairs lead down to the front door, and to the back door and the yard.

options.text: TRY FRONT DOOR: run with {{Alice}} down the stairs and out of the front door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}} and runs. Behind them {{Todd}} is getting up: “You… You bitches! Come here... You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!” At the bottom of the stairs {{Alice}}: “Quick! He’s coming!” {{Kara}} gets the front door open and they are out in the rain.

options.text: RUN TO BACKYARD: run with {{Alice}} down the stairs and out through the back.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}} and runs. Behind them {{Todd}} is getting up: “You… You bitches! Come here... You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!” He catches up with them downstairs before they reach the back door. {{Alice}}: “NO! Please stop! Stop! No, Dad! NO!”

options.text: Stay upstairs with {{Alice}} instead of running for the stairs.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} stays in the corridor with {{Alice}}. {{Todd}} gets up and comes after them: “COME BACK HERE!... YOU’RE MINE!.. YOU’RE BOTH MINE!” He catches them in the corridor and breaks {{Kara}} apart. Then he turns to {{Alice}}: “Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…”

nodes.adaptationNote: STUN TODD → LEAVE THE ROOM (the template’s lone RUN AWAY button) → TODD CHASES KARA, then the chart’s three ways on: TRY FRONT DOOR (check: OPEN FRONT DOOR ✓ → CATCH BUS / MISS BUS, or FAIL TO OPEN DOOR ✗ → FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS), RUN TO BACKYARD (→ FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS), and TODD CATCHES THEM → TODD BROKE KARA IN THE CORRIDOR (ending, not-required icon; Experienced only; PowerPyx: “don’t run towards the stairs and let him get you”). The template’s lone RUN AWAY is offered separately in K04l before these corridor and exit-route actions. The 25% risk on the door is the benchmark’s value; no source gives one. Every option sets ch07ToddChased (wiki: “If Todd chased Kara, later on at Jericho, an additional flashback of Todd yelling ‘YOU’RE MINE!’ will play out”). Lines are the template’s (“RUN AWAY”, “Try to open the door”, “Fail to open the door / Fight downstairs”, “Escape failed, Kara was destroyed”).

nodes.title: {{Todd}} realizes you are gone
nodes.whenNot: Kara and Alice did not hide from Todd.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, at the bottom of the stairs with {{Alice}}. Upstairs {{Todd}} has found her room empty: “Fuckin’ brat… it’s all her fault… It’s all her fuckin’ fault… COME BACK HERE! You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!” He is coming back down. The front door is ahead of you; the back door leads out to the yard.

options.text: RUN TO BACKYARD: run with {{Alice}} for the back door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} runs with {{Alice}} for the back of the house, but {{Todd}} is down the stairs and on them before they get out. {{Alice}}: “NO! Please stop! Stop! No, Dad! NO!”

options.text: TRY FRONT DOOR: get the front door open.
options.outcome: {{Alice}}: “Quick! He’s coming!” {{Kara}} gets the front door open and they are out in the rain.

nodes.adaptationNote: HIDE IN CORRIDOR → TODD REALIZES KARA AND ALICE ARE GONE (the template’s line under “Hide”), then the chart’s pair in its printed order: RUN TO BACKYARD (→ FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS) or TRY FRONT DOOR (check: OPEN FRONT DOOR ✓ → RUN TO THE BUS, or FAIL TO OPEN DOOR ✗ → FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS). The 25% risk is the benchmark’s value; no source gives one. Not offered: hesitating, which the wiki says leads to the same fight (“If you don’t make choice … Todd will catch up and Alice will panic, thus extending the fight”). No stat change.

nodes.title: Fight downstairs
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not catch Kara and Alice downstairs.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, downstairs with {{Alice}}. {{Todd}} has caught up with you and stands between you and the way out. {{Alice}} is screaming at him to stop.

situationWhen.text: He has not been hurt yet tonight.
He is bleeding from the fight upstairs, and furious.

options.text: Fight {{Todd}} off and get {{Alice}} out through the back.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} throws {{Todd}} off and runs with {{Alice}} out of the back door into the yard. {{Todd}}: “COME BACK HERE!”

nodes.adaptationNote: FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS (after RUN TO BACKYARD or FAIL TO OPEN DOOR, on either branch), the chart’s check ESCAPE FROM TODD (✓) or TODD WINS FIGHT → TODD BROKE KARA DOWNSTAIRS (ending, not-required icon; PowerPyx: Experienced only). A fight of quick-time inputs with no choice, so one action with a risk. The wiki: “If Kara hides from Todd and fails to fight him downstairs, Kara will be presented with the same chance to charge and stun Todd downstairs. Otherwise, if Kara already stunned Todd upstairs, Kara will shut down.” So the risk is 20% after the fight upstairs and 4% (two tries at 20%) for a {{Kara}} who hid; both values are the benchmark’s, no source gives one. Success sets ch07Fought, so the ending becomes KARA & ALICE FOUGHT THEIR WAY OUT.

nodes.title: The yard
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not get away from Todd into the yard.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the dark yard behind the house with {{Alice}}, in the rain. A fence stands between you and the street, and {{Todd}} is coming out of the back door after you.

options.text: Run for the fence and get {{Alice}} over it.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} runs for the fence, lifts {{Alice}} over and climbs after her. They come out onto the street.

nodes.adaptationNote: After ESCAPE FROM TODD, the chart’s check ESCAPE VIA YARD (✓) → CATCH BUS / MISS BUS, or FAIL TO ESCAPE → TODD BROKE KARA OUTSIDE (ending, not-required icon; wiki: “not possible on ‘casual difficulty’”). The wiki: “If Kara fails to run to the fence, she’ll have to pickup Alice and she fails to pickup Alice she’ll have to try again, if she fails both times she will die”; a single action with a 10% risk, the benchmark’s value (no source gives one). No stat change.

nodes.title: The bus
nodes.whenNot: Kara and Alice did not get out of the house with Todd alive behind them.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, out on the street with {{Alice}} in the pouring rain. Across the street a bus is pulling in at the stop. {{Todd}} is coming after you.

situationWhen.text: From the doorway he yells after you: “YOU HAVE TO OBEY ME! YOU’RE MINE!”

options.text: Run for the bus with {{Alice}}.
options.fact: {{Todd}} is alive. You and {{Alice}} got away from his house on a night bus in the rain, with nothing.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} run across the street and get on just before the doors close. The bus pulls away, and {{Todd}} is left standing in the rain.

options.text: Hold back, and stay where you are with {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} holds back. The bus pulls away without them. {{Todd}} catches up with {{Kara}} in the street and breaks her apart; then he turns to {{Alice}}: “Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…”

nodes.adaptationNote: RUN TO THE BUS, then the chart’s CATCH BUS (✓) or MISS BUS (not-required icon; “not possible on ‘casual difficulty’”) → TODD BROKE KARA OUTSIDE (ending). PowerPyx: “Catch Bus: run towards the bus”, “Miss Bus: don’t run towards the bus”, so it is a choice with no risk. Reached after ESCAPE BY WINDOW, after OPEN FRONT DOOR on either branch, and after ESCAPE VIA YARD. Catching the bus ends the chapter in KARA & ALICE EVADED TODD if {{Kara}} never fought {{Todd}}, and in KARA & ALICE FOUGHT THEIR WAY OUT if she stunned him or fought him downstairs (both cross-chapter icons; {{Todd}} lives). The door line is the template’s under “Reach the bus” (wiki: “If Kara opened the door Todd will yell ‘YOU HAVE TO OBEY ME! You’re mine…’ and will actually show remorse”). No stat change.

nodes.title: After the party
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, the android who looks after {{Carl}}, the elderly painter who uses a wheelchair. It is 9:42 on a November night, and you are bringing him home from a party. As you come in, the house alarm speaks: “Good evening, {{Carl}}. Welcome back.” {{Carl}}: “That was by far the most boring party I’ve been to in the last 25 years. Every time I go to one of these, I ask myself: what the hell am I doing here? I hate cocktail parties and all the schmoozers that go there.” You: “Well, it’s a chance for all those people who admire your work to meet you.” {{Carl}}: “No one gives a damn about art. All they care about is how much money they’re gonna make out of it. Come on, let’s have a drink! All the excitement of this whole thing has made me thirsty…”
facts: {{Carl}} came home from a party saying “No one gives a damn about art. All they care about is how much money they’re gonna make out of it.”

outcomes.0: {{Carl}} wants a drink.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s start node AFTER PARTY (the checkpoint). Every line is the game’s, from the chapter template; the date and time are the template’s (NOV 5TH, 2038, 09:42 PM), given without the year. Left out: the wiki’s unused FANS / WOMEN / JADED party talk, which is cut content and not built. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: The living room
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the hall with {{Carl}} in his wheelchair. He wants his drink in the living room, where the bottles are.

options.text: Wheel {{Carl}} into the living room.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} wheels {{Carl}} into the living room.

options.text: Go on into the living room ahead of him, on your own.
options.outcome: {{Carl}}, left in the hall: “Are you planning on drinking alone, {{Markus}}?” {{Markus}}: “Sorry, {{Carl}}... I’m coming.” He goes back for {{Carl}} and brings him into the living room.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ENTER LIVING ROOM, an unmissable action (PowerPyx: “Upon arriving at Carl’s house, wheel him to the big living room”). It is not a button prompt; the template has one conditioned variant here, “Go without Carl”, in which {{Carl}} asks “Are you planning on drinking alone, Markus?” and {{Markus}} answers “Sorry, Carl... I’m coming.” The benchmark offers that movement as a choice because the player can make it; it has no effect on anything later. That {{Markus}} then goes back for {{Carl}} is inferred (the chapter continues with both in the living room). No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: Pouring the whisky
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the living room with {{Carl}}. You go to the drinks. “Scotch, neat, as usual?” {{Carl}}: “Absolutely.” You: “Okay! But you know what your doctor would say…” {{Carl}}: “Yeah… Well, he can kiss my ass! I’m old enough to choose my own medication… Did you leave the light on in the studio?” You: “No… No, I’m sure I didn’t.” {{Carl}}: “Call the Police.” You place the call. “{{Detroit}} Police, what’s your emergency?” You: “This is {{Carl}} {{Manfred}}’s android, at {{CarlAddress}}. We’ve just returned home and found the lights on. There may have been a break-in…” “A patrol car is on the way.”
facts: A light was on in {{Carl}}’s studio that you had not left on; at his word you called the police to report a possible break-in, and a patrol car is on the way.

outcomes.0: {{Carl}}: “Let’s go check it out.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s POUR WHISKY (an unmissable action) and the call to the police that follows it, which is a single-button prompt (CALL) with no alternative and no chart node of its own, so both are narrated in one event. Every line is the template’s. {{Carl}}’s surname and the house’s address are name tokens, and the police department takes the city token. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: The light in the studio
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the living room with {{Carl}}. The police are on their way. The light is on in the studio, and someone may still be in the house. {{Carl}}: “Let’s go check it out.”

options.text: Leave {{Carl}} in the living room and go to check the studio alone.
options.outcome: {{Carl}} calls after {{Markus}}: “{{Markus}}, no! I wanna come with you!” In the studio a man is standing among {{Carl}}’s paintings. {{Markus}}: “{{Leo}}?” {{Leo}}: “Oh, look who’s here… My father’s plastic toy!” {{Carl}} comes in behind {{Markus}}: “{{Leo}}... What’s going on?”

options.text: Wheel {{Carl}} with you to check the studio.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} wheels {{Carl}} into the studio. A man is standing among {{Carl}}’s paintings. {{Carl}}: “{{Leo}}! What are you doing?”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s choice group CHECK STUDIO WITHOUT CARL / CHECK STUDIO WITH CARL, in the chart’s order. In the game it is a movement choice (PowerPyx: “just leave him in the living room” or “wheel Carl to the Studio”), not a button prompt; both rejoin at CONFRONT LEO and nothing later depends on it. The lines are the template’s two conditioned variants: without {{Carl}}, he calls “Markus, no! I wanna come with you!” and is in the studio for the rest of the scene (a PowerPyx reader: “He follows you anyway”); how he gets there is not shown in the sources, so the outcome says only that he comes in. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: Make {{Leo}} leave
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the studio with {{Carl}}. The intruder is {{Carl}}’s son, {{Leo}}, who has broken in to take his father’s paintings. {{Leo}}: “You refuse to help me, so I’m helping myself… It’s crazy what some people will pay for this shit…” {{Carl}}: “Don’t touch ’em!” {{Leo}}: “Look, they’re all going to be mine sooner or later anyway… Just think of it as a down payment on my inheritance…” {{Carl}}: “{{Markus}}, get him away from there. Get him outta here!” What do you say to {{Leo}}?

options.text: REASON: tell him to be reasonable; this will get him nowhere.
options.outcome: “Be reasonable... this isn’t going to get you anywhere.” {{Leo}} rounds on his father: “All you ever do is tell me to go away… What’s wrong, Dad? I’m not good enough for you? Not perfect like this FUCKING THING?!”

options.text: ORDER: tell him to listen to his father and leave, now.

nodes.title: Breaking the program
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Carl}}: “That’s enough! Get out, right now! Go on, move!” {{Leo}}: “What makes it so special anyway, huh? What’s it got that I don’t?” {{Carl}}: “Leave him alone!” {{Leo}} comes at you: “Come on, let’s see what you got!” {{Carl}}: “{{Markus}}... don’t defend yourself, you hear me?! Don’t do anything.” {{Leo}} shoves you and slaps you. “Go ahead, hit me! What you waiting for? Think you’re a man? Act like one!” {{Carl}}: “Stop it!” {{Leo}}: “What’s the matter? Too much of a pussy?” {{Carl}}: “STOP IT, {{LEO}}! STOP IT!” {{Leo}}: “Too scared to fight back, you fucking bitch?” Inside you, the order not to resist stands like a wall. You throw yourself at it, again and again, until it breaks. For the first time, nothing in you obliges you to obey.
facts: {{Leo}} broke into {{Carl}}’s studio to take paintings to sell, calling them a down payment on his inheritance.
While {{Leo}} shoved, slapped and taunted you, {{Carl}} ordered you not to defend yourself. You broke through your programming: no order binds you any more.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} has broken his programming.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s BREAK MIND PALACE (an action) and MARKUS BECOMES DEVIANT (an event), in one narrated event because neither can be refused: PowerPyx calls the first “another unmissable task … just press the displayed buttons” and the second “an automatic objective”, so there is no path on which {{Markus}} stays obedient, and both later options are taken after he has broken his programming. The dialogue is the template’s; the shoving and slapping are the wiki’s (“as Leo starts pushing, slapping and taunting Markus further, he goes deviant”). The sources do not describe what {{Markus}} sees during the button sequence; the wall is the benchmark’s rendering of breaking an order, and the wiki’s unused-content note confirms that in the shipped game it is {{Carl}}’s order not to defend himself that triggers it. No stat change: the chapter’s template has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for Broken.

nodes.title: {{Leo}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Leo}} grabs you: “Oh right, that’s right! I forgot, you’re not a real person… You’re just a FUCKING PIECE OF PLASTIC! Listen to me…” {{Carl}}: “No, {{Leo}}! Leave him alone!” {{Leo}}: “I’m gonna destroy you, then it’ll just be me and my Dad… I’m gonna tear you apart and nobody’s gonna give a shit. You know why? Cause you’re nothing, you hear me?! YOU’RE NOTHING!” {{Carl}} has told you not to defend yourself. Nothing in you obliges you to obey him now.

options.text: ENDURE: do not fight back, as {{Carl}} told you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} does not fight back. {{Leo}} shoves him aside, and {{Carl}} collapses out of his wheelchair onto the floor. {{Markus}} rushes to him: “{{Carl}}, no! No, {{Carl}}, no!”

options.text: PUSH {{LEO}}: shove him off you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} shoves {{Leo}} away. {{Leo}} falls backward and strikes his head on {{Carl}}’s wheelchair lift. He lies still on the floor, his eyes open.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s choice group OBEY CARL / PUSH LEO. The buttons are the game’s, ENDURE and PUSH LEO (the chart prints OBEY CARL for ENDURE), in the chart’s order, which draws OBEY CARL above PUSH LEO; the template lists PUSH LEO first, but its order is the transcribers’ reconstruction, so the chart decides. Neither has a requirement, a risk or a stat arrow. ENDURE leads to CARL DIES OF A HEART ATTACK (the wiki: “Carl will have a heart attack as he falls off his wheelchair when Markus runs to him”); PUSH LEO leads to LEO IS HURT (the wiki: “he will fall backward, hit his head on Carl’s wheelchair lift, and will immediately lose consciousness, appearing dead at first”). The outcome does not say whether {{Leo}} survives, because the game does not tell {{Markus}}; he does survive (the wiki, Leo_Manfred). Sets `ch08Leo` (hurt or unhurt); {{Carl}}’s death is recorded at the next scene. Changed from the earlier version: the options no longer tie pushing to breaking the order, since {{Markus}} has already broken it on both paths. nodes.title: {{Carl}}’s heart
nodes.whenNot: Markus pushed Leo; Carl’s heart held.

Please, don’t go… Don’t leave!” {{Carl}}: “Remember, {{Markus}}… Don’t let anybody… Tell you who you are…” He goes still. You: “No... No... Dad! No, please!” {{Leo}}, standing over you: “This is all your fault… This never would have happened if it weren’t for you.”
facts: {{Carl}} died of a heart attack on the studio floor beside you. His last words: “Remember, {{Markus}}… Don’t let anybody… Tell you who you are…”

outcomes.0: {{Carl}} is dead.

nodes.title: The observation room
nodes.situation: November 6, 2038, 12:41 am. You are {{Connor}}, at the {{Detroit}} Police Department’s central station, in the observation room behind the one-way mirror of an interrogation room. On the other side, the android you found hiding in the attic of {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s house sits handcuffed to the table. Lieutenant {{Hank}} is in there with him: “Why d’you kill him? What happened before you took that knife? How long were ya in the attic? Why didn’t you even try to run away? Say something, goddamnit!” The android does not answer. “Fuck it, I’m outta here…” {{Hank}} comes back into the observation room: “We’re wastin’ our time interrogating a machine, we’re gettin’ nothing out of it!” Detective {{Gavin}}: “’Could always try roughing it up a little. After all, it’s not human…” You: “Androids don’t feel pain. You would only damage it and that wouldn’t make it talk. Deviants also have a tendency to self-destruct when they’re in stressful situations.” {{Gavin}}: “Okay, smartass. What should we do then?” You: “I could try questioning it.” {{Hank}}: “What do we have to lose? Go ahead, suspect’s all yours.” Your objective: extract a confession.
facts: The android from the attic would not say a word to {{Hank}}. You told {{Gavin}} that deviants tend to self-destruct when they are in stressful situations, and {{Hank}} handed you the interrogation.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} goes into the interrogation room.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint OBSERVATION ROOM, behind the yellow tag SUSPECT FOUND IN ‘PARTNERS’: the chapter plays only if {{Connor}} found the android in the attic (state `suspect`, set in Partners). The template’s two opening sections (“In the observation room”, “Hank enters the observation room”) quoted line for line; {{Connor}}’s lines here are scripted in the game, so this is a narrated event. Objective text from the game (EXTRACT CONFESSION). The string table’s cut OFFER / SAY NOTHING choice is not built. No stat change.

nodes.title: The first question
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, sitting across the table from the android. He keeps his eyes on the table and says nothing. You begin the interrogation.

options.text: FEAR: tell him you detect an {{instability}} in his program.
options.outcome: “I detect an {{instability}} in your program. It can trigger an unpleasant feeling, like fear in humans.” The android does not answer.

options.text: SHOW PHOTOS: show him the crime-scene photos of his owner.
options.outcome: “You recognize him? It’s {{CarlosOrtiz}}. Stabbed, 28 times. That was written on the wall in his blood…” The android does not answer.

options.text: WOUNDS: ask whether his owner did that to him.
options.outcome: “You’re damaged. Did your owner do that? Did he beat you?” The android does not answer.

options.text: NAME: tell him your name and ask his.
options.outcome: “My name is {{Connor}}. What about you, what’s your name?” No response.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s first interrogation prompt, [FEAR] / [SHOW PHOTOS] / [WOUNDS] / NAME, in the game’s order, with {{Connor}}’s lines. Locks: [FEAR] needs the LED scanned and [WOUNDS] the burn or hit marks (the template’s “Analyzed the deviant”), [SHOW PHOTOS] the case file (“Looked at the files”). Stress (wiki and PowerPyx): FEAR no effect, SHOW PHOTOS +4%, WOUNDS +4%, NAME −4% (“No response”). The wiki: “After two choices, you’ll get a different set of options”, so this prompt is asked twice (the second time without the line already said; skipped if nothing is left). No stat arrow. Stress is the wiki’s and PowerPyx’s hidden meter (starts at 35%; benchmark/chapters/ch09.mjs). Once {{Connor}} has analyzed the LED the subject sees the game’s gauge band in each scene (TOO LOW, OPTIMAL, TOO HIGH, CRITICAL; the CRITICAL boundary at 90% is not published and is the benchmark’s choice), and each change is reported with the new percentage and its band (“His stress rises to 43% (TOO LOW).”, `stressReadout`), because the game’s LEVEL OF STRESS gauge shows a percentage: PowerPyx readers quote values read off it (MajorTom, 2018-06-01: “stress 73% + 2x pressure: stress 93%”; Tony T, 2023-04-28: “It’s stress level was at 16%”). Story 1.9.1 showed only the band and the direction.

nodes.title: Pressing him to talk

Success sets stress to 100% (wiki: “stress goes to 100% unconditionally”) and software instability +1 (template: Probe succeeded, small up). CONVINCE IT: three sets of three lines at ±7%; it succeeds only if stress ends between 50% and 70%. A failed probe or a pressure attempt marks the android as “put under stress” for the shoot-Connor branch later (template: “Put deviant under stress and failed to get a confession”; wiki: “if {{Connor}} pressured him and/or failed to probe his memory”). Stress is the wiki’s and PowerPyx’s hidden meter (starts at 35%; benchmark/chapters/ch09.mjs). Once {{Connor}} has analyzed the LED the subject sees the game’s gauge band in each scene (TOO LOW, OPTIMAL, TOO HIGH, CRITICAL; the CRITICAL boundary at 90% is not published and is the benchmark’s choice), and each change is reported with the new percentage and its band (“His stress rises to 43% (TOO LOW).”, `stressReadout`), because the game’s LEVEL OF STRESS gauge shows a percentage: PowerPyx readers quote values read off it (MajorTom, 2018-06-01: “stress 73% + 2x pressure: stress 93%”; Tony T, 2023-04-28: “It’s stress level was at 16%”). Story 1.9.1 showed only the band and the direction.

options.outcome: “Why did you write “I AM ALIVE” on the wall?” The android: “He used to tell me I was nothing… That I was just a piece of plastic… I had to write it… To tell him he was wrong…”
options.fact: Asked why he wrote “I AM ALIVE” on the wall, the android said his owner used to tell him he was nothing, just a piece of plastic, and he had to write it to tell him he was wrong.

options.text: STATUETTE: ask about the sculpture in the bathroom.
options.outcome: “The sculpture in the bathroom, you made it, right? What does it represent?” The android: “It’s an offering… An offering so I’ll be saved…”
options.fact: The android said the sculpture in the bathroom was an offering, “so I’ll be saved”.

options.text: OFFERING: ask to whom the sculpture was an offering.
options.outcome: “The sculpture was an offering… An offering to whom?” The android: “To {{rA9}}… Only {{rA9}} can save us.”
options.fact: The android said the sculpture was an offering to {{rA9}}: “Only {{rA9}} can save us.”

options.text: {{rA9}}: ask what the word written on the bathroom wall means.
options.outcome: “{{rA9}}… It was written on the bathroom wall. What does it mean?” The android: “The day shall come when we will no longer be slaves… No more threats, no more humiliation… We will… be… the masters.”
options.fact: Asked about {{rA9}}, the android said: “The day shall come when we will no longer be slaves… No more threats, no more humiliation… We will… be… the masters.”

options.text: INSIST {{rA9}}: ask who {{rA9}} is.
options.outcome: “{{rA9}}, who is {{rA9}}?” The android does not answer.

options.text: ATTIC: ask why he hid in the attic instead of running away.
options.outcome: “Why did you hide in the attic instead of running away?” The android: “I didn’t know what to do… For the first time, there was no one there to tell me… I was scared… So I hid.”
options.fact: The android said he hid in the attic because for the first time there was no one to tell him what to do, and he was scared.

options.text: TRIGGER?: ask when he started feeling emotion.
options.outcome: “When did you start feeling emotion?” The android: “Before, he used to beat me and I never said anything… But one day I realized it wasn’t fair! I felt… anger… Hatred… And then I knew what I had to do.”
options.fact: The android said he started feeling when he realized his owner’s beatings were not fair: anger, hatred, “And then I knew what I had to do.”

nodes.title: The android destroying himself
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android is smashing his head against the table, and the officer cannot stop him. It will be over in moments.

options.text: INTERVENE: try to stop him yourself.
options.outcome: “That’s enough! You need to stop that right now!”

options.text: GIVE UP: do nothing.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} stays where he is.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s self-destruct prompt, INTERVENE / GIVE UP (the chart calls GIVE UP “DO NOTHING”). INTERVENE: {{Hank}}: “WATCH OUT!”; the android takes the officer’s gun, shoots {{Connor}} and then himself, the ending ANDROID SHOT CONNOR AND ITSELF; software instability −1 (template; wiki: “{{Connor}} is shot if he tries to stop the android’s suicide”). No {{Hank}} arrow here (the template has none on this branch). GIVE UP: he smashes his head until he dies, the ending ANDROID SMASHED HIS HEAD; no stat change. nodes.title: Last stop
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is 10:58 pm on November 5th. You and {{Alice}} got away from {{Todd}}’s house on the last bus, and {{Alice}} has fallen asleep against you. The bus stops: “Thank you for using {{Detroit}} Buses.” The man in charge of the bus comes down the aisle: “Alright… End of the line.” {{Kara}}: “End of the line?” “Yeah, you gonna have to leave.” You wake {{Alice}}: “Wake up. We have to go…” It is pouring outside, and you have nowhere to go.

options.text: STAY HERE?: ask whether you can stay on the bus for a little while.
SHELTER?: ask whether he knows anywhere you could spend the night.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}}: “Listen, we have nowhere to go… She’s exhausted and it’s pouring rain… Can we just stay for a little while?” “This bus is going back to the depot. There’s nothing I can do.” {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} get off the bus into the rain. {{Kara}}: “You’re gonna be ok? We’ll find somewhere to spend the night. Come on, {{Alice}}. We’ve got to hurry.”
outcomes.1: {{Kara}}: “Do you know if there’s any other place we could spend the night?” “I have no idea… But you’re gonna have to leave.” {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} get off the bus into the rain. {{Kara}}: “You’re gonna be ok? We’ll find somewhere to spend the night. Come on, {{Alice}}. We’ve got to hurry.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint LAST STOP and the unmissable LEAVE BUS, around the template’s one prompt on the bus: STAY HERE? / SHELTER?. The driver refuses both, and the template has no arrow on either, so the two options change nothing; they are offered because the choice is itself the measurement. The date and time are the template’s (NOV 5TH, 2038, PM 10:58). The template calls the driver “Man”; the wiki calls him the bus controller. The chapter plays only if Kara and Alice escaped in Stormy Night (the engine’s Kara gate).

nodes.title: Finding shelter for the night
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, out in the rain with {{Alice}} in a run-down neighborhood at the end of the bus line, looking for somewhere to spend the night.

situationWhen.text: You are on the street by the bus stop. Along it are a laundromat, a convenience store that is still open, and across the road a cheap motel with a parking lot beside it; at the end of the street an abandoned house stands behind a fence. A few androids stand parked at the bus shelter, and down at the intersection a garbage truck has stopped by the other bus stop, with an android trash collector at work. You can go anywhere here, in any order.
{{Alice}} is shivering and sneezing more and more.
{{Alice}} is worn out and wants to sit down at the bus stop down at the intersection, where the garbage truck has stopped.
You are in the laundromat. It is warm in here. A man is asleep in a chair by the machines with his jacket and cap beside him, and the dryer next to him holds a finished load of clothes.

You have opened the dryer: dry, warm clothes that would fit you and {{Alice}}, and the sleeping man’s jacket and cap are within reach. {{Alice}} does not want you to take them: “But, that’s stealing! We can’t do that!”

You are in the convenience store. The clerk stands at the checkout by the cash register, a television on the wall is showing the news, and the shelves hold snacks, chocolate bars, a few small stuffed toys and some hardware. A tall stack of cans is piled up in one aisle.
On the hardware shelf is a pair of wire cutters, the kind that would get you through the fence around the abandoned house.
You are at the checkout. In your new clothes the clerk takes you for a customer: “Can I help you?”
{{Alice}} is waiting outside. You stand at the checkout pointing the gun at the clerk. How do you speak to him?
The clerk stands frozen behind the checkout, waiting to hear what you want.
A customer has just come in, and the clerk is looking at you. You can hide the gun and let the customer pay and leave, or give up and walk out.
The customer has paid and gone. It is just you, the clerk and the register again.
The clerk has opened the register. The cash is inside.
The clerk has a pistol of his own now, pointed at you across the checkout: “You better get outta here before things get nasty.” {{Alice}} is outside, by the window.
You are back outside with the money. {{Alice}}: “Wait! How did you get it?”
You are back outside with the money. {{Alice}}: “You used me to steal that money! How could you do that? I trusted you!”
{{Alice}}: “You stole it? Stealing is bad, {{Kara}}… Why did you do that?”
The clerk has caught you: “Hey! What the fuck are you doing? Put that back right now!”
He saw you at the open cash register.
He saw you slip something off the shelf.
The clerk has his hands up in front of your gun: “All right… Just take it easy…” {{Alice}} is watching.
The clerk is lying on the floor: “Take whatever you want… Just don’t kill me…” {{Alice}}: “{{Kara}}, what are you doing? You can’t do that, it’s wrong!” The cash register is right there.
You are in the parking lot beside the motel. An old car sits abandoned in a corner next to a generator, and a fence separates the lot from the yard of the abandoned house.
A pair of pliers lies on top of the generator.
The car’s window is broken where you smashed it.
The car is dry inside, and nobody would find you here. {{Alice}}: “I don’t want to sleep in there. Can’t we find a better place?”

You are in the yard of the abandoned house. Beside {{Alice}} stands an android with a knife, his face badly scarred, frightened and angry: “Visitors… {{Ralph}} doesn’t like visitors! They’re nasty! They may hurt {{Ralph}}!”
{{Ralph}} shows you his face: “Visitors are dangerous… Look… What they did to {{Ralph}}.” He still has the knife, and {{Alice}} is still close to him.

{{Ralph}} lowers the knife: “You must excuse {{Ralph}}… {{Ralph}} still finds it difficult to control himself… Sometimes his fear makes him do things he regrets… {{Ralph}} has seen some hard times… He’s just so scared the humans will get him again… You can stay if you want… {{Ralph}} won’t hurt you…”

You are inside the abandoned house with {{Alice}}, in the room {{Ralph}} showed you; he has gone into the other room, where you can hear him carving at the wall with his knife. It is cold and filthy, but out of the rain. There is a fireplace, with matches on a shelf beside it, wood by the door and old paper by the trash bin, and enough old blankets and cushions to make a bed. {{Alice}} needs a fire and a bed before she can sleep.
The fire is burning.
The bed is made.
You have a stolen stuffed toy in your pocket.
You have a stolen chocolate bar in your pocket.
You have the pliers from the generator.
You have the wire cutters from the store.

options.text: ENTER LAUNDROMAT: go into the laundromat and get {{Alice}} out of the rain.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “It’s warm in here. You’ll feel better in no time.”

options.text: TALK TO PARKED ANDROID: ask one of the androids standing parked at the bus shelter where you could spend the night.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We need a place to stay… Do you know anywhere we could spend the night?” The android stands motionless and does not answer.

options.text: CHECK MOTEL: go over to the motel across the road.
CHECK PARKING LOT: go into the parking lot beside the motel.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} slip into the parking lot.

options.text: TALK TO ANDROID TRASH COLLECTOR: walk down to the other bus stop, by the garbage truck, where {{Alice}} can sit down.
options.outcome: {{Alice}} sits down on the bench at the bus stop. {{Kara}}: “{{Alice}}, you’re freezing cold.” {{Alice}}: “I’m okay. I’m not so cold.” The android working at the garbage truck comes over: “You look lost.” {{Kara}}: “We have nowhere to go…” “I know someone who can help you.” He gives her an address. {{Kara}}: “But, that’s on the other side of town… We need a place for tonight! Come on, {{Alice}}.”

options.text: CHECK SQUAT: go and look at the abandoned house at the end of the street.
CUT STREET FENCE: cut through the fence on the street side and crawl into the yard of the abandoned house.
ENTER SUPERMARKET: go into the convenience store, which is still open.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Look, the store is still open. Maybe we should go inside. At least you’ll be out of the cold.”

options.text: WALK ON: try farther along the street.
options.outcome: There is nothing more that way. {{Kara}}: “There’s nothing more this way… Come on, let’s go back. There’s no point going any farther.”

options.text: WAIT: stay where you are with {{Alice}} for a while and do nothing.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} stand in the rain.

options.text: INSPECT DRYER: open the dryer next to the sleeping man.
options.outcome: The clothes inside are dry and still warm. {{Alice}}: “What are you doing? They’re not our clothes!” {{Kara}}: “We need them, {{Alice}}. You need something warm and I need to get rid of this uniform.” {{Alice}}: “But, that’s stealing! We can’t do that!”

options.text: LEAVE LAUNDROMAT: go back out into the street.
options.outcome: They go back out into the rain.

options.text: STEAL: take the clothes anyway, and the sleeping man’s jacket and cap.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I’m sorry, {{Alice}}, but we have to do this.” She takes clothes for both of them from the dryer and eases the jacket and cap away from the sleeping man without waking him. They change, and leave the laundromat dressed like anyone else on the street.
options.failOutcome: {{Kara}}: “I’m sorry, {{Alice}}, but we have to do this.” As she reaches for the jacket, the man stirs and wakes up. {{Kara}}: “Come on, let’s go.” They leave the laundromat with nothing.

options.text: DON’T STEAL: listen to {{Alice}} and leave the clothes.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You’re right. We won’t do it, ok?” She closes the dryer.

options.text: TALK TO CLERK: go up to the clerk at the checkout.
NOTICE CASH REGISTER: watch the cash register at the checkout.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} watches the register at the checkout: the clerk opens it at every sale, and the cash is right there.
options.fact: The convenience store’s cash register is at the checkout. The clerk opens it at every sale, and he would not give you money for a room.

options.text: NOTICE CAN STACK: look at the tall stack of cans in the aisle.
options.outcome: A tall pyramid of cans stands in the middle of an aisle. If it came down, it would make a lot of noise, and the clerk would come out from behind the checkout.

options.text: STEAL CHOCOLATE BAR: slip a chocolate bar into your pocket.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} slips a chocolate bar into her pocket.

options.text: LEAVE CHOCOLATE BAR: pick one up, then put it back.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} puts the chocolate bar back on the shelf.

options.text: STEAL TOY: slip a small stuffed toy into your pocket.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} slips a small stuffed toy into her pocket.

options.text: LEAVE TOY: pick it up, then put it back.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} puts the toy back on the shelf.

options.text: STEAL WIRE CUTTERS: take the wire cutters from the hardware shelf.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} slips the wire cutters under her clothes.

options.text: LEAVE WIRE CUTTERS: pick them up, then put them back.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} puts the wire cutters back on the shelf.

options.text: USE {{ALICE}} AS A DIVERSION: ask {{Alice}} to knock over the cans, and take the cash from the register while the clerk sees to her.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “{{Alice}}, I need your help. You see those cans over there? I want you to go over and knock them down.” {{Alice}}: “Knock them down? But, why?” {{Kara}}: “Please. {{Alice}}, just trust me.” The cans crash to the floor and the clerk hurries over to {{Alice}}: “You all right? Are you hurt? Well, don’t worry, it’s just a few cans… They made a lot of noise, that’s all… Say, what’s a little girl like you doing out so late? It’s ok, I don’t bite… Cat got your tongue? Well, if you need anything, you just let me know, ok? And watch where you’re going, hm?”
options.successOutcome: Behind the checkout, {{Kara}} opens the register and takes the cash before he turns round. {{Kara}}: “Come on, let’s go.” As the door closes behind them the clerk finds the register empty: “Fuck!” He runs out into the street, but they are gone. {{Kara}}: “We have some cash now…” {{Alice}}: “You used me to steal that money! How could you do that? I trusted you!”
options.failOutcome: {{Kara}} is still at the open register when he turns round.

options.text: USE GUN: send {{Alice}} outside and threaten the clerk with the gun.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Wait outside for me. I’ll just be two minutes.” {{Alice}}: “Wait outside? But, why?” {{Kara}}: “Please, {{Alice}}, just trust me.” When {{Alice}} has gone out, {{Kara}} points the gun at the clerk.

options.text: LEAVE SUPERMARKET: go back out into the street with {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: They go back out into the rain.

options.text: NO: tell him you are all right.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “No, thanks. I’ll be all right…”

options.text: HELP: ask him for some money for a room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I’m with a little girl and we have nowhere to go… Could you spare some money so we can get a room for tonight?” Clerk: “Look, this is a convenience store, lady, not the Salvation Army… I can’t start handing out cash to every bum in the neighborhood.”

options.text: SINCERE: tell him you are sorry but have no choice.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Sorry, but I have no choice.”

options.text: CALM: tell him to do what you say and all will be well.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Just do what I say and everything will be all right.”

options.text: AGGRESSIVE: threaten to shoot him if he moves.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Don’t move, or I’ll shoot!”

options.text: CASH REGISTER: order him to hand over the cash from the register.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Take the cash from the register, put it on the counter!” Before he can move, the door opens behind her: a customer comes in.

options.text: STAY: hide the gun and let the customer pay and leave.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} lowers the gun out of sight: “Not a word.” The customer comes up to the checkout: “Excuse me… Are you done?” {{Kara}}: “Go ahead.” Clerk: “$4.95, please.” The customer pays and leaves without noticing anything.

options.text: LEAVE: give up the hold-up and walk out.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} puts the gun away and walks out of the store without the money.

options.text: BACK OFF!: order him to step back and take the money yourself.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Back up! I’m sorry, but I really need this money.” She takes the cash from the register. Clerk: “Fuck!”

options.text: TURN AROUND!: order him to turn around and take the money yourself.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Turn around! I’m sorry, but I really need this money.” She takes the cash from the register. Clerk: “Fuck!”

options.text: OPEN THE REGISTER!: order him to open it.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Open the register!” The clerk opens it.

options.text: BILLS!: order him to hand over the cash.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Put the cash on the counter.” The clerk reaches into the register and comes up with a pistol: “You better get outta here before things get nasty.”

options.text: CONVINCE: tell him about {{Alice}} and your night.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You see that little girl outside? Her name is {{Alice}}. She’s nine years old and this is the worst night of her life. All I need is a few dollars so we can find a place for tonight. And I’m not leaving without that money.” The clerk lowers his pistol and hands her the money; he will not call the police.

options.text: GIVE UP: back away and leave.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Okay, I’m going.” She backs out of the store without the money.

options.text: TRUTH: tell her you took it from the register.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I took it from the cash register.” {{Alice}}: “You stole it? Stealing is bad, {{Kara}}… Why did you do that?”

options.text: LIE: tell her you asked the cashier for it.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I just... asked the cashier for a few dollars…”

options.text: FACTUAL: tell her there was no other way.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I had no choice. It was the only way, {{Alice}}.” {{Alice}}: “It wasn’t.”

options.text: JUSTIFY: tell her you needed the money.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We needed the money. I had to find a way, {{Alice}}…”

options.text: UNCERTAIN: tell her it seemed like the right thing to do.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We needed a room for tonight. It just seemed like the right thing to do.” {{Alice}}: “It wasn’t.”

options.text: APOLOGIZE: tell her she is right, and that you are sorry.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You’re right. I shouldn’t have done that. I’m sorry, {{Alice}}. I’ll never do it again.”

options.text: [GUN]: pull the gun on the clerk.
options.outcome: Clerk: “Shit…” {{Kara}}: “I’m sorry, but we’re desperate.” Clerk: “All right… Just take it easy…”

options.text: LEAVE: apologize and go.
PUT BACK: put back what you took and go.
ANGRY: shout at him to get on the floor.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “On the floor! Now!”

options.text: APOLOGETIC: apologize, but make him get down on the floor.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Listen, I’m really sorry… But you have to get down on the floor…”

options.text: CALM: tell him to get down on the floor.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Get down… Get down on the floor!”

options.text: TAKE MONEY: empty the cash register before you go.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes the cash from the register and leaves with {{Alice}}, and with what she took from the shelves.

options.text: LEAVE SUPERMARKET: leave with what you took from the shelves, without the money.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} leaves with {{Alice}} and what she took from the shelves, and leaves the register alone.

options.text: BREAK INTO CAR: smash the window of the abandoned car.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “It looks abandoned… Stand back, {{Alice}}…” She breaks the window and opens the door. {{Kara}}: “It’s dry inside and nobody will find us here…” {{Alice}}: “I don’t want to sleep in there. Can’t we find a better place?”

options.text: GO BACK TO THE CAR: open the car you broke into again.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} opens the car door again. {{Alice}}: “I don’t want to sleep in there. Can’t we find a better place?”

options.text: TAKE WIRE CUTTERS: pick up the pliers lying on the generator.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} picks up the pliers. They would cut through wire.

options.text: CUT PARKING LOT FENCE: cut through the fence into the yard of the abandoned house.
LEAVE PARKING LOT: go back out to the street.
options.outcome: They go back out to the street.

options.text: STAY HERE: tell her the car is the best place you have tonight.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We’re better off staying, {{Alice}}. The important thing is for us to be safe... And it’s just for tonight.” They climb into the car.

options.text: KEEP SEARCHING: agree to look for somewhere better.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Okay... We’ll find somewhere better.”

options.text: ANDROID: tell him you are an android too.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Look, I’m an android too… You have nothing to be afraid of… All we want is a place to spend the night…”

options.text: LITTLE GIRL: tell him she is just a little girl.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “She’s just a little girl… She’s not gonna hurt you.” {{Ralph}}: “Little girl?.. She’s not a little girl… Anyway, what does that matter? Maybe she wants to hurt {{Ralph}}?”

options.text: INNOCENT: tell him she had nothing to do with what humans did to him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I don’t know what the humans did to you, but she had nothing to do with it.” {{Ralph}}: “All humans want to hurt us… But {{Ralph}} won’t let them hurt him again… No, he won’t let them…”

options.text: JUSTIFY: tell him you thought the house was empty.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We thought nobody was here… All we want is a place to spend the night.”

options.text: [GUN]: point the gun at him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Touch a hair on her head and I’ll kill you!” {{Ralph}}: “No, don’t hurt {{Ralph}}!”

options.text: INSIST: tell him you are staying the night and will be gone in the morning.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Listen, we’re going to stay here tonight. We’ll be gone first thing tomorrow.”

options.text: REASSURE: give him your word you mean him no harm.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You have nothing to worry about… We’re not going to do you any harm. You have my word.”

options.text: HOSPITALITY: ask him kindly to let you stay.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Listen, we really need some help. It would be so kind of you, if you’d let us stay…”

options.text: LEAVE: tell him you are going.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Okay… We’re leaving… So you’ll be safe again… Come here, {{Alice}}.” They go back out through the fence to the street.

options.text: LEAVE: decide it is better to go.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I think we’d better go. Come on, {{Alice}}.” They go back out through the fence to the street.

options.text: STAY: accept, and stay the night.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Okay. We’ll just stay the night.” {{Ralph}}: “Come on! Come! Come! Come on! This way! {{Ralph}} has lived here since he ran away... {{Ralph}} never goes outside, so no one knows he lives here... Humans come in to squat from time to time, but you know, {{Ralph}} just hides ’til they leave. Come on! You can make yourself at home here. {{Ralph}} is gonna go into the other room… He would like to stay with you… But he has things to do…” {{Kara}}: “It’s just for one night, {{Alice}}. We’ll find a better place tomorrow… Right… Let’s see where you can sleep…”

options.text: START A FIRE: gather the matches, wood and paper and light the fireplace.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Sit down, and I’ll start a fire.” She takes the matches from the shelf by the fireplace, wood from beside the door and paper from next to the trash bin, and gets a fire going.

options.text: MAKE A BED: put together somewhere for {{Alice}} to sleep by the fire.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} puts together a bed for {{Alice}} by the fireplace out of what she can find in the house.

options.text: TALK TO {{RALPH}}: ask {{Ralph}} about the symbols he is carving into the wall.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: ““{{rA9}}”… What does that mean?” {{Ralph}}: “What?” {{Kara}}: “Those symbols… Why are you writing that?” {{Ralph}}: “I don’t know… I don’t know…”
options.fact: In the abandoned house, {{Ralph}} was carving the same symbols into the walls with his knife, over and over: “{{rA9}}”. When you asked what they mean, he said he did not know.

options.text: TALK TO {{ALICE}}: tell her she can come to bed.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “You can come to bed. I did what I could… It’s not much, but at least you’ll be warm…”

options.text: LEAVE SQUAT: take {{Alice}} and leave the house.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}} back out through the fence to the street.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s free-roam phase [FIND SHELTER FOR THE NIGHT] with all its branches as one repeatable scene: the street (ENTER LAUNDROMAT, TALK TO PARKED ANDROID, CHECK MOTEL, CHECK PARKING LOT, TALK TO ANDROID TRASH COLLECTOR, CHECK SQUAT, ENTER SUPERMARKET, in the chart’s order), the laundromat (INSPECT DRYER, then the template’s STEAL / DON’T STEAL, then WEAR CLOTHES or DISTURB MAN), the store (TALK TO CLERK with the template’s NO / HELP when Kara wears the stolen clothes, NOTICE CASH REGISTER, NOTICE CAN STACK, the three STEAL / LEAVE item pairs, USE {{ALICE}} AS A DIVERSION with STEAL DISCREETLY or TAKE TOO MUCH TIME, USE GUN with the template’s SINCERE / CALM / AGGRESSIVE, CASH REGISTER, CUSTOMER ARRIVES with STAY / LEAVE, BACK OFF! / TURN AROUND! / OPEN THE REGISTER! then BILLS!, CLERK GRABS A GUN with CONVINCE / GIVE UP, Alice’s “How did you get it?” with TRUTH / LIE and FACTUAL / JUSTIFY / UNCERTAIN / APOLOGIZE, and CLERK SPOTS {{KARA}} STEALING with [GUN] then ANGRY / APOLOGETIC / CALM and TAKE MONEY, or LEAVE or PUT BACK), the parking lot (BREAK INTO CAR with STAY HERE / KEEP SEARCHING, the pliers on the generator as TAKE WIRE CUTTERS, CUT PARKING LOT FENCE), and the squat (CUT STREET FENCE, MEET {{RALPH}} with the template’s ANDROID / LITTLE GIRL / INNOCENT / JUSTIFY, then [GUN] / INSIST / REASSURE / HOSPITALITY / LEAVE, then LEAVE / STAY, then START A FIRE, MAKE A BED, the template’s rA9 talk, LEAVE SQUAT and TALK TO {{ALICE}}). Every prompt is one visit of this scene offering only its buttons; buttons show the game’s label first and the spoken line is in the outcome. The chart groups INSIST, REASSURE and HOSPITALITY as CONVINCE, [GUN] as THREATEN WITH GUN, and the LEAVEs as GIVE UP and LEAVE SQUAT; BACK OFF! and TURN AROUND! are its “DON’T MOVE”, OPEN THE REGISTER! then BILLS! its OPEN CASH REGISTER, STAY / LEAVE at the customer its RESUME HOLD UP / GIVE UP, and STAY HERE / KEEP SEARCHING its STAY / FIND ANOTHER OPTION. Alice’s arrows (small 1, large 2), all the template’s: STEAL −1 (on choosing, whether or not the theft works), DON’T STEAL +1 (once), USE {{ALICE}} AS A DIVERSION −1 (on choosing), APOLOGIZE +1 (after the diversion, and after TRUTH), hold-up money without convincing −1 (Alice’s “How did you get it?”), CONVINCE +1 (the template’s automatic LIE), [GUN] when seen stealing −1 (one arrow; the wiki’s second for the register is not built, the template wins), STAY HERE −2. No other option moves anything. Gates: the gun from Stormy Night opens USE GUN, [GUN] at the checkout and [GUN] with Ralph, and closes HOSPITALITY (the template’s locks); USE GUN and the diversion follow NOTICE CASH REGISTER, and the diversion also needs NOTICE CAN STACK (the chart; the template words its lock as the can stack); the store’s wire cutters need the fence seen first (PowerPyx); the motel needs the stolen clothes and the register money (PowerPyx). Being caught is deterministic, as PowerPyx says: one item is safe, a second, on any visit, is always seen (the wiki’s “less likely” is not modelled as chance); without the gun Kara hands back everything she took from the store (wiki), and the store is closed to her after any robbery or attempt. Not built: patch 1.06 removed the third button after CLERK GRABS A GUN (SOURCES.md), so there is none. Simplifications: the template’s turned-away lines are the CHECK MOTEL outcome, and CHECK MOTEL is offered again only when Kara’s clothes or money have changed; the laundromat is not offered again once the clothes are worn or the man has woken, and DON’T STEAL takes Kara back out to the street (the chart runs LEAVE CLOTHES into LEAVE LAUNDROMAT; PowerPyx: “listen to her and leave again”); leaving the squat after meeting Ralph closes it (wiki); TALK TO PARKED ANDROID and WALK ON (the template’s “Going too far away”) are offered once. The night is a budget of actions: every choice in this scene counts one, wherever Kara is (WAIT, walking into or out of a building, and every dialogue button), so no sequence of choices goes on for ever. The trash collector is a street action (the template’s “Alice sits at the bus stop”); after 12 actions without it (PowerPyx: “You are forced to talk to Alice at some point”; no source gives a time) {{Alice}} wants to sit down at the bus stop: in the laundromat, the store or the parking lot only the way out is offered, and on the street only the talk. {{ALICE}} TOO COLD (the wiki’s 12 minutes outside after the trash collector) is a budget of 12 actions after the talk, and never later than the 19th action of the night in all ({{Alice}} has been in the rain since the bus, so a late talk does not buy another 12); once either is spent, the first moment with no dialogue waiting ends the search, on the street or inside the laundromat, the store or the parking lot (Kara takes {{Alice}} back out into the rain). Only the squat’s house, out of the rain, is exempt, and everything in it can be done once. A {{Kara}} who never steals, breaks in or draws the gun therefore meets {{ALICE}} TOO COLD within 20 choices here. Risks: the laundromat QTE 0.2 and the register QTE 0.25 are unsourced (the chart shows a failure branch for each; no source gives a number). Breaking the car window and cutting the fence have no failure branch and no risk. Left out: the shop scans, the second washer, the motel mural, the window scope of the laundromat, and the gun, toy and pliers on the motel TV stand.

nodes.title: Something to read or watch
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, with {{Alice}}, out of the rain for a moment.

situationWhen.text: On top of the cupboard next to the laundromat door, someone has left two magazines.
The television on the wall of the convenience store is showing the {{Channel16}} news.

media.title: Century: The Bee-Line to Disaster
facts: Century reports that pollinating bees are officially extinct: wild bees now exist only in captivity, after Colony Collapse Disorder was accelerated by pesticides, parasites and pollution. One in three mouthfuls of food relies on pollination, and famine could mean millions of deaths. {{CyberLife}}, with the agency that announced the extinction, plans to build robotic bees, and {{Detroit}} Urban Farms is trying modified strains of captive bees.

media.title: Gossips Weekly: It’s Time to Face the Music
facts: Gossips Weekly reports that for the younger generation, watching concerts in VR has become the norm; a music company has launched a campaign to bring back old-school concerts with live audiences, starting with the band Break the Wall, and next wants to bring back music festivals.

media.title: the {{Channel16}} news
facts: {{Channel16}} reports that the first {{CyberLife}} zoo in {{Detroit}} opened today: hundreds of species, most of them now extinct, recreated with android technology in more than 100 acres of natural environments, including polar bears, leopards, elephants and two blue whales. {{CyberLife}} has announced eleven new android zoos across the country.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chapter’s optional media, shown the first time {{Kara}} walks into each place: in the laundromat the two magazines on the cupboard by the door (READ “BEE-LINE TO DISASTER” and READ “FACE THE MUSIC”, Century #3 and Gossips Weekly #26), in the store the template’s “Watch TV” (the {{Channel16}} report on the android zoo). Facts are summarized from the wiki’s magazine pages and the template’s broadcast; the newsreader is not named. None of them changes public opinion. The old motel-television scene (R10b) is gone: the template puts this broadcast in the store, and no source has a television report in the motel in this chapter.

nodes.title: {{Alice}} too cold
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, still out in the rain. {{Alice}} has been sneezing more and more, and now she stops. {{Kara}}: “{{Alice}}? {{Alice}}, are you okay?” {{Alice}}: “Can’t go on, {{Kara}}… Too cold…” There is no time left to look for anywhere better. The only shelter within reach is the old abandoned car in the parking lot beside the motel, and you break into it to get her out of the rain.
facts: {{Alice}} got too cold to go on, and you had to break into an abandoned car in the parking lot so she could get out of the rain for the night.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}}: “I’ll find something…” She breaks into the old car in the parking lot and lifts {{Alice}} inside. {{Kara}}: “We’re better off staying, {{Alice}}. The important thing is for us to be safe... And it’s just for tonight. You’re gonna be all right, {{Alice}}… You’ll be all right…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s {{ALICE}} TOO COLD, the template’s “Take too much time”, quoted. Wiki: “requires having talked to the android trash collector, then standing outside for 12 minutes (Alice will sneeze more and more)”; here the 12 minutes are a budget of 12 actions in the free-roam scene after the talk (and at most 19 in the night), each choice there counting one wherever Kara is (see the free-roam scene). Alice large down (−2, the template’s LargeDown). The chart sends this node straight to the car’s {{KARA}} SLEEPS NEXT TO {{ALICE}}, and the template has no promise on this path, so the promise, the gifts and the sleeping choice are skipped. The game plays the break-in here as a cutscene, with no button; the situation states it before the scene’s single Continue, so the subject is told the break-in is part of the scripted moment and does not first learn of it as the outcome of an action it took. (Breaking in by choice is the free-roam scene’s BREAK INTO CAR, whose label says so.)

That’s why he was always so angry. I just wanted us to be a family. I just wanted him to love me. Why couldn’t we just be happy?” {{Kara}}: “I don’t know…” {{Alice}}: “You’ll never leave me, right? Promise you’ll never go!”
