nodes.title: Back to life
nodes.situation: NOV 6TH, 2038. AM 03:34. You are {{Markus}}. The last thing you remember is the police shooting you in {{Carl}}’s studio. Now your systems reboot. You are lying on your back in the rain, in a pit of broken androids: bodies, arms, heads and torn-out parts piled in the mud as far as you can see. Everything you see is red and broken by interference, and every sound reaches you muffled.
facts: You woke at 3:34 in the morning on 6 November 2038 in a landfill of broken androids, after the police shot you in {{Carl}}’s studio.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} lifts his head out of the mud.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s start node and checkpoint BACK TO LIFE. The date and time are the chapter’s own (“NOV 6TH, 2038”, “AM 03:34”). Both Broken endings end with the police shooting {{Markus}} (the engine’s Broken outcome), and the wiki and PowerPyx say this chapter plays the same either way, so nothing here depends on the earlier choice. The red filter with interference and the muffled sound are the wiki’s Notes on the damaged eye and audio processor. No stat change; the chapter has none.

nodes.title: Analyze self
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, lying in the mud of the landfill. You run a diagnosis on yourself, part by part. OPTICAL UNIT: Impaired vision. CORRUPTED MIND PALACE. AUDIO PROCESSOR: Corrupted audio data. DAMAGED. PUMP REGULATOR: All systems in LOW POWER MODE. DEFECTIVE. LEFT AND RIGHT LEG COMPONENTS: MISSING. Unable to stand.
facts: Your diagnosis in the landfill: optical unit impaired (corrupted), audio processor damaged, thirium pump regulator defective with all systems in low power mode, and both legs missing.

outcomes.0: Diagnosis complete. {{Markus}} cannot stand; he starts dragging himself through the mud on his arms.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ANALYZE SELF: the template’s observation group “Diagnose”, its four readouts quoted in the game’s order and wording. In the game the player has to find the four spots on {{Markus}}’s body (PowerPyx; on Experienced they are not marked), all of them, in any order and with nothing to get wrong, so this is a narrated event rather than a choice of order. PowerPyx names the spots LED, audio processor, pump regulator and leg; the template’s readouts (optical unit, audio processor, pump regulator, legs) win (research note §10, discrepancy 4). The game titles the regulator readout THIRIUM PUMP REGULATOR; the word thirium identifies the source and is dropped from subject text (the neutral renderer removes it), so the readout reads PUMP REGULATOR. No stat change.

nodes.title: Repair legs
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, pulling yourself through the pit on your arms between the bodies. Legs lie torn off in the mud around you, and you examine them. RIGHT LEG COMPONENT #6847j. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. RIGHT LEG COMPONENT #6321t. Status: DAMAGED. INCOMPATIBLE. LEFT LEG COMPONENT #8427g. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE.
facts: You replaced your missing legs with a compatible right leg (#6847j) and left leg (#8427g) torn from other androids; a damaged right leg (#6321t) was incompatible.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} fits the right leg #6847j and the left leg #8427g, one after the other, and gets to his feet.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s REPAIR LEGS, with the template’s three leg readouts (observation groups “Compatible right leg”, “Incompatible right leg”, “Left leg”) in the game’s order and wording; the template’s #6321t is used, not the wiki’s #6312t. PowerPyx: “Follow the button prompts to repair the legs, nothing you can do wrong here”, so this is a narrated event with no risk. No stat change.

nodes.title: Hear about {{Jericho}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on your new legs, making your way through the pit. As you pass, an android stuck in the wall of bodies, so old and broken that you cannot tell what he was made for, grabs your arm and stares at you: “There’s a place where we can be free! Find {{Jericho}}! Find {{Jericho}}!..” As he holds you, something passes from him into your memory: a copy of the key he carried, the way to find {{Jericho}}. Then he shuts down for good.
facts: In the landfill a dying android grabbed you and said: “There’s a place where we can be free! Find {{Jericho}}!” Before he shut down he passed you a copy of the key he carried, the way to find {{Jericho}}.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} pulls free of the dead hand and goes on.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s event HEAR ABOUT JERICHO (the template’s section “Android grabs Markus”, speaker Phileas, whose line is quoted). The key: the Phileas page (“He carried a key to locate Jericho, which is copied to Markus and the latter uses it to find the freighter”) and the Jericho location page (“Phileas gave Markus a copy of his key to locate Jericho before permanently shutting down”); how it passes is not described, so it is narrated plainly. {{Markus}} does not learn the android’s name, so none is given. Sets fromDeadJerichoKey for Jericho (chapter 14). The old scene’s “single word” and “symbol” had no source and are gone. No stat change.

nodes.title: Passage of limbs
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. The only way out of the pit is a tight chasm between two walls of android bodies, and you squeeze into it. Hands of dying androids reach out of the walls, grab your arms and your legs and try to hold you down. A voice beside your head: “Where are you going?”
facts: Leaving the pit, you squeezed through a passage of dying androids whose hands grabbed you and tried to hold you down.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} tears free of the hands one after another and pushes through to the other side.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s PASSAGE OF LIMBS, with the template’s line (“Other android grabs Markus”: “Where are you going?”). PowerPyx: “a tight chasm Markus needs to squeeze through. There are hands of dying androids sticking out the side trying to hold Markus down. Press the button prompts here.” Neither the chart nor any source shows a failure branch, so there is no risk roll. No stat change.

nodes.title: Junkyard
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You come out into the open junkyard: a plain of broken androids under the rain and the floodlights, a crane swinging over the piles on the far left, a yellow neon sign reading VETA, and at the far end a slippery slope of bodies, the only way out. Many of the bodies still move. Some repeat the phrases they were made for, muffled in your damaged hearing: “An unexpected error has occurred. I apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.” “Don’t forget your dental appointment next Friday at 8 AM.” “Would you like another glass of red wine, Madam?” “Malfunction detected.” One keeps muttering: “I have to get to {{Jericho}}... Androids live in freedom there… I got to get to {{Jericho}}... No other choice…” Before you can climb out you must replace your damaged optical unit, audio processor and thirium pump regulator with compatible parts from the androids around you.
facts: In the junkyard, broken androids kept repeating their old service phrases, and one muttered that he had to get to {{Jericho}}, where androids live in freedom.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} starts searching the junkyard for parts.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint JUNKYARD (its image shows the crane and the yellow VETA sign; the wiki notes the sign in the final cutscene). The background lines are the template’s “Background dialogues”, which it lists as audible though not subtitled; four of them are quoted, plus the {{Jericho}} line, which the template keeps as audible (research note §10, discrepancy 6). The two TL400 lines and the others are left out. The objective is the wiki’s “Replace damaged parts” and PowerPyx’s “With all parts found (Optical Unit, Pump, Audio Processor) you can now climb the slippery slope”. No stat change.

nodes.title: Search for parts
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the open junkyard under the rain. To get out you must replace your damaged optical unit, audio processor and thirium pump regulator with compatible parts taken from the androids around you, then climb the slippery slope at the far end. You can search in any order, one thing at a time.

options.text: Pull out the android head sticking out of the wall of bodies on the far left, under the crane.
options.fact: In the junkyard you took your new optical unit, #8087q with a blue iris, from a talking AK700 head, after a crane dumped a load of bodies on you and you dug yourself out.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} pulls the head out of the wall. Its eyes open: “Hello. I’m an AK700 android. I was designed to serve you. What can I do for you?” Overhead the crane swings round and opens its grab, and a load of android bodies pours down on top of him. Buried, he digs and claws his way up through the bodies until he is out, the head still in his hand. He examines its eye: OPTICAL UNIT #8087q - BLUE IRIS. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. As he takes it out, the head speaks again: “My program has detected an anomaly. Please contact the nearest {{CyberLife}} maintenance center.” He replaces his damaged optical unit with it. The red haze and the interference clear, and he can scan his surroundings again.

options.text: Examine the optical unit of an android lying in the pile.
options.fact: An optical unit you examined in the junkyard (#9754h) was functional but incompatible with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} kneels by the android and examines its eye: OPTICAL UNIT #9754h. Status: FUNCTIONAL. INCOMPATIBLE. He leaves it.

options.text: Go to the android lying motionless in the middle of the junkyard.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} crosses toward the middle of the junkyard, between androids lying in the mud.

options.text: Examine the thirium pump regulator of an android lying in the pile.
options.fact: A pump regulator you examined in the junkyard (#9474) was low on energy and incompatible with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} opens the android’s chest and examines the regulator: PUMP REGULATOR #9474. Status: LOW ENERGY. INCOMPATIBLE. He leaves it.

options.text: Take the pump regulator from the dead android near the slope.
options.fact: You took your new pump regulator (#2886) from a dead android near the slope of the junkyard.
options.outcome: Near the foot of the slope {{Markus}} kneels by a dead android and opens its chest: PUMP REGULATOR #2886. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. He takes it out and replaces his own defective regulator. His systems come out of low power mode.

options.text: Search the head lying on the right side of the junkyard.
options.fact: You took your new audio processor (#4903) from a head on the right side of the junkyard.
options.outcome: On the right side of the area {{Markus}} finds the head and examines it: AUDIO PROCESSOR #4903. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. He pulls out his own damaged audio processor and plugs in the new one. Sound crashes in: the rain, the wind, the droning of the storm and the voices of the broken androids, deafening after the silence.

options.text: Examine the audio processor of an android lying in the pile.
options.fact: An audio processor you examined in the junkyard (#4807) was functional but incompatible with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} turns the android’s head and examines the processor behind its ear: AUDIO PROCESSOR #4807. Status: FUNCTIONAL. INCOMPATIBLE. He leaves it.

options.text: Climb the slippery slope at the far end of the junkyard.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} starts up the slope, sliding back on the loose bodies and pulling himself up again, handhold after handhold.

situationWhen.text: Your optical unit is still impaired: everything is red and broken by interference, and you cannot scan your surroundings.
Your new blue optical unit works: your vision is clear and you can scan your surroundings.
Your audio processor is still damaged; the rain and the voices reach you muffled.
Your new audio processor works; the storm is deafening.
Your thirium pump regulator is still defective, and all your systems are in low power mode.
Your new pump regulator works.
You left the android in the middle her regulator. You will need another compatible one, and without scanning you have not found one yet.
You left the android in the middle her regulator. Scanning, you find another compatible one in a dead android near the slope.
All three parts are replaced. Nothing holds you here.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s bracket [ SEARCH FOR PARTS ] as a repeatable scene: each visit offers what has not been done yet, in any order (PowerPyx: the parts can be found in any order; the chart draws no edge between its branches). Chart nodes here: FIND OPTICAL UNIT with CRANE DUMPS BODIES and DIG YOURSELF OUT as one option, because they always happen together (PowerPyx: interacting with the head “brings a lot of dead androids falling down from a crane”; digging out “gets you the Optical Unit”); the eye comes from the talking AK700 head, as in the template (“Take head”, “Remove optical unit”, with its two lines), and is #8087q with a blue iris; FIND AUDIO PROCESSOR (#4903; PowerPyx “in a head on the right side of the area”, while the wiki’s Biocomponent 4903 page has it in an android’s hand); FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN DEAD ANDROID (#2886, once the new eye can scan: PowerPyx “You can scan the area and find another one near the slope”; offered whether or not {{Markus}} has met the android in the middle, since PowerPyx: “If you didn’t kill the android in the middle of the area for its pump (or you never found it in the first place) you can also get a pump regulator from a dead android near the slope”); and CLIMB SLOPE, which ends the scene and needs all three parts. Going to the middle of the junkyard plays ANDROID BEGS TO DIE and FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN ANDROID, the next two scenes, which then come back here. The three incompatible readouts of the template’s “Search for components” group (#9754h, #9474, #4807) are optional looks (PUMP REGULATOR without the word thirium, as in the earlier scenes); the model names the wiki gives for their androids are not in the game’s text and are left out. Departures: the two encounters in the middle (the crawling android and the one with the pump regulator) happen together on the way there, in the template’s order, and going there is optional, as in the game, where {{Markus}} can miss them. Story 1.9.1 offered the dead android’s regulator only after sparing her, which forced the encounter; story 1.9.2 follows PowerPyx. If {{Markus}} already has the dead android’s regulator when he reaches her, KILL is not offered (he no longer needs her part; an adaptation, no source covers that order). The wiki’s note that the begging android must be met “before replacing Markus’ damaged parts” is not applied: PowerPyx’s own route meets him right after finding the optical unit (research note §8, question 3). Left out (not in the template, not on the chart): the singing android and the grappling android. No risk, no stat change: the chapter has no failure node and no arrow.

nodes.title: Android begs to die
nodes.whenNot: Markus never crossed to the middle of the junkyard.
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, crossing toward the middle of the junkyard. An android is crawling through the mud at your feet, too broken to get up. As you step past him he grabs your leg and holds on: “I’m begging you, please… End it… I don’t wanna live anymore…”

options.text: KILL: reach into his chest and pull out his thirium pump.
options.fact: In the junkyard a crawling android begged you to end his life, and you did: you pulled out his thirium pump and he shut down.

options.text: SPARE: pull your leg free and leave him.
options.fact: In the junkyard a crawling android begged you to end his life. You refused and left him there, begging you not to leave him.

outcomes.0: “Make it quick…” {{Markus}} kneels, reaches into the android’s chest and pulls out his thirium pump. The android shuts down in the mud.
outcomes.1: “No, please… Don’t leave me!.. Don’t leave me!” {{Markus}} pulls his leg free and walks on. The android is left alive in the mud behind him.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ANDROID BEGS TO DIE and its choice group REFUSE TO KILL / KILL. The prompt and its two buttons are the template’s (“Android begs to die”: KILL, SPARE), in the game’s order, each shown with its label first; the plea and the two replies are the template’s lines. The android is male (the wiki’s Sorrowful Android: “the android grabs Markus on the leg”; KILL: “Markus takes out the android’s heart”; SPARE: “he will beg Markus not to leave him though alas he is left alive”). In the game he is optional and easy to miss (PowerPyx); here he is always met on the way to the middle of the junkyard (see the previous scene’s note). Neither option gives {{Markus}} a part. Records fromDeadBeggar (Kill or Refuse to kill). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki gives no cross-chapter effect.

nodes.title: The pump regulator
nodes.whenNot: Markus never crossed to the middle of the junkyard.
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the middle of the junkyard, a few steps from the crawling android. An android lies motionless in the mud with her chest open, and you examine her regulator: PUMP REGULATOR #2886. Status: FUNCTIONAL. COMPATIBLE. You reach in to take it. She wakes, and her hand closes on your arm: “Wait! Please! Please, don’t do that! I wanna live…”

options.text: KILL: pull out her pump regulator and take it.
options.fact: The pump regulator you run on came from a living android in the junkyard who begged you to let her live; you took it and she shut down.

options.text: SPARE: leave her the regulator and look for another one.
options.fact: In the junkyard an android whose pump regulator you needed begged to live, and you spared her.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} pulls the regulator from her chest. She says nothing more; she slowly shuts down. He replaces his own defective regulator with hers, and his systems come out of low power mode.
outcomes.1: “Thank you…” {{Markus}} lets go of the regulator and stands up. He will have to find another compatible one.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN ANDROID and its choice group REFUSE TO KILL FOR PUMP / KILL FOR PUMP. The prompt and its two buttons are the template’s (“Try to take pump regulator from android”: KILL, SPARE), in the game’s order, each shown with its label first; her plea and “Thank you…” are the template’s lines, and KILL has none (the template’s ø). The game titles the regulator readout THIRIUM PUMP REGULATOR; the word thirium identifies the source and is dropped from subject text (the neutral renderer removes it), so the readout reads PUMP REGULATOR. The compatible readout #2886 is the template’s (it does not say which android carries it, so the dead android near the slope shows the same part number). She is female (the wiki’s Begging Android; the Markus page: “He gets a choice to kill or spare her”). The old scene’s “you have minutes” is gone: no source gives a timer. After SPARE, the dead android’s regulator near the slope is the way (PowerPyx), back in the search. If {{Markus}} already took the dead android’s regulator before coming here, only SPARE is offered: the two regulators are alternatives for the same part (PowerPyx: “If you didn’t kill the android … you can also get a pump regulator from a dead android”), and no source shows the prompt after the part is replaced (adaptation). Records fromDeadPump (Kill for pump or Refuse to kill for pump), and after KILL fromDeadPumpSource (Living android). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki gives no cross-chapter effect.

situationWhen.text: You already took a working pump regulator from the dead android near the slope; you do not need hers.

nodes.title: {{Markus}} came back from the dead
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You haul yourself over the top of the slope and stand. Behind you the landfill stretches away under the rain, the floodlights and the yellow VETA sign; ahead are the lights of the city. You raise a hand to your temple and pull out your LED, the light that marks you as an android. Without it, nobody will know what you are. You think of the dying android’s words: there is a place where androids can be free.
facts: You climbed out of the landfill and pulled the LED from your temple, so you now pass for human. Your right eye is now blue (#8087q). You set off for the city to find {{Jericho}}.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} walks away from the landfill toward the city. “My name is {{Markus}}.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ending MARKUS CAME BACK FROM THE DEAD, the chapter’s only outcome (wiki: “This chapter has only one outcome”), reached on every path. PowerPyx: “After Markus reaches the top of the slope he must still remove his LED (to appear like a human). Then he walks away”; the Markus page: “his right eye has been exchanged for a blue eye (#8087q)”. The closing line is the template’s spoken “My name is Markus.”; the line before it, “Markus.”, is marked unused in the template and is not built. The jacket the Markus page says he steals on the way to the city is not in this chapter’s text and is left to Jericho. Records fromDeadOutcome (Markus came back from the dead) and fromDeadLedRemoved. No stat change.

nodes.title: In the zen garden
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. It is November 6th, 2038, 9:56 in the morning. You close your eyes and enter the zen garden, the virtual space where you report to {{Amanda}}, your handler at {{CyberLife}}. A pond lies in front of you, with paths running left and right along its edges and bridges leading out to an island in the middle.
facts: You report to {{Amanda}}, your handler at {{CyberLife}}, in the zen garden, a virtual space you enter in your mind.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} looks around the garden.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint IN THE ZEN GARDEN (date and time from the template’s notes: NOV 6TH, 2038, AM 09:56). A narrated event with a single Continue. The engine also records here, once, what this chapter reads from earlier chapters (deviant found in Partners, the spilled drink and the statuette there; confession, death and intervention in The Interrogation; {{Kara}} and {{Todd}} after Stormy Night; {{Carl}} after Broken), so every later scene reads the same snapshot. No stat change. Cross-chapter inputs (`inputsVersion` 2, story 1.9.2): “intervened” (INTERVENTION at {{Amanda}}’s first question, {{Chris}}’s and {{Gavin}}’s lines) is The Interrogation’s ending ANDROID WAS SENT BACK TO ITS CELL, which three INTERVENEs reach after any approach, and {{Gavin}}’s line follows whether {{Hank}} drew on him there (template conditions “Intervened and saved the deviant in The Interrogation” and “Connor intervened during The Interrogation”); story 1.9.1 read both from the CONVINCE-only flag ANDROID TRUSTS CONNOR.

nodes.title: The zen garden
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the zen garden. A path runs left along the edge of the pond toward a circular archway; another runs right along the water. On the island in the middle of the pond, {{Amanda}} is tending her roses.

situationWhen.text: Off the path to the right, a smaller path leads to a small graveyard.

options.text: Cross the bridge to the island where {{Amanda}} is tending her roses.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} crosses the bridge to the island. {{Amanda}} is among her roses.

options.text: Go left along the pond to the circular archway and examine the stone there.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the edge of the pond to the circular archway on the left of the path and examines the stone inside it.

options.text: Go right along the pond and take the path to the small graveyard.
options.fact: In the zen garden there is a small graveyard with a gravestone for every {{Connor}} model that has been destroyed. There is one.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the path to a small graveyard: one gravestone, for the {{Connor}} model that was destroyed.

options.text: Go right along the pond and take the path to the small graveyard.
options.fact: In the zen garden there is a small graveyard with a gravestone for every {{Connor}} model that has been destroyed. There are two.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the path to a small graveyard: two gravestones, one for each {{Connor}} model that was destroyed.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FIND AMANDA with its two optional side branches, as a repeatable scene: FIND MAGIC STONE (PowerPyx: “go left along the edge of the pond until you find a circular archway… Interact with it”) and CHECK THE GRAVES (wiki: “only if Connor previously died in The Hostage and/or The Interrogation”; the Zen Garden page: “gravestones for killed Connor models”). Neither has a line, a clue text or a stat change in the template; no source describes the stone, so the outcome says only that {{Connor}} examines it. The graveyard shows one gravestone per earlier {{Connor}} death (the benchmark’s reading of “Another gravestone is present” on The Interrogation page). Crossing to the island ends the scene.

nodes.title: Talk with {{Amanda}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the island in the zen garden. “Hello, {{Amanda}}.” {{Amanda}}: “{{Connor}}… It’s good to see you.”

situationWhen.text: {{Amanda}}: “I expected you to find the deviant who killed that man… I must admit I’m a little bit disappointed...” You: “I’m sorry. I know I should have succeeded.” {{Amanda}}: “Never mind. I’m sure you’ll show more foresight in the future.”

{{Amanda}}: “Congratulations, {{Connor}}... Finding that deviant was far from easy, and the way you interrogated it was very clever. You’ve been remarkably efficient, {{Connor}}.” You: “Thank you, {{Amanda}}.” {{Amanda}}: “We’ve asked the police department to transfer it to us for further study. It may teach us something about what happened.”

{{Amanda}}: “Your predecessor was unfortunately destroyed... It knew deviants could be unpredictable, but it wasn’t careful enough… I hope you won’t make the same mistake.” You: “I don’t intend to.” {{Amanda}}: “When a {{Connor}} model is destroyed, its memory is transferred to the next one, but some data can be lost in the process. Avoid being destroyed. It will be better for you and the investigation…” You: “I understand.”

{{Amanda}}: “Finding that deviant was far from easy… you showed great skill in your investigation. But you knew deviants could be unstable. You should have been more cautious.” You: “I thought I could make it talk… It was a judgement error.” {{Amanda}}: “Never mind. I’m sure you’ll be more careful in future.”

outcomes.0: {{Amanda}} turns from her roses to {{Connor}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TALK WITH AMANDA, opening: one of four reactions, decided by Partners and The Interrogation, each with the template’s Amanda arrow, applied by the engine here: deviant not found in Partners, large down (−2); “Got a confession, without dying”, large up (+2); “Connor died during The Interrogation”, small down (−1); found but no confession, small down (−1). The wiki’s chapter page and Relationship Stat page list the same four. A confession followed by a death counts as a death (the template’s confession variant reads “without dying”). “The DPD” is rendered as “the police department”. The cut line about the transfer request (“We hope they’ll accept our request…”) is not built.

nodes.title: What {{Connor}} thought of the deviant
nodes.whenNot: Connor never found the deviant in Partners, so Amanda does not ask about the interrogation.
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, with {{Amanda}} among the roses. {{Amanda}}: “The interrogation seemed… challenging… What did you think of the deviant?”

options.text: TRAUMATIZED: say it showed signs of trauma after being abused by its owner.
options.outcome: “It showed signs of PTSD after being abused by its owner, as if its original program had been completely replaced by new instructions.”

options.text: {{DEVIANCY}}: say it showed every sign of deviancy and the model was clearly defective.
options.outcome: “It showed all the signs of deviancy: cognitive instability, unpredictable behavior, and the emulation of human emotions. It was even afraid to die. The model was clearly defective.”

options.text: INTERVENTION: say you kept it from being damaged, so it can still be analyzed.
options.outcome: “I prevented it from being damaged, so we might still learn something by analyzing it.”

options.text: REGRETS: say the previous {{Connor}} should have anticipated the danger.
options.outcome: “It could’ve killed everyone in the room. The previous {{Connor}} should have anticipated the danger. It was a mistake to let an armed policeman so close to the deviant.”

options.text: SIMULATION: say it simulated human emotion, fear above all, very convincingly.
options.outcome: “It simulated human emotion, fear in particular, in a very convincing way. It seemed completely overwhelmed by them, and behaved irrationally…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The first of {{Amanda}}’s three questions, asked only if the deviant was found in Partners (the template nests it in that variant). Buttons in the game’s order: TRAUMATIZED, DEVIANCY, INTERVENTION (unlocked by “Intervened and saved the deviant in The Interrogation”; if he also confessed, {{Connor}} adds “It said something to me: ‘The truth is inside’…”), REGRETS (unlocked by {{Connor}}’s death in The Interrogation) and SIMULATION (its cut ending, “as a human would under extreme stress”, is not built). No arrow on any answer (template; PowerPyx “No effect”).

nodes.title: What {{Connor}} makes of {{Hank}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, with {{Amanda}} in the zen garden. {{Amanda}}: “This… Lieutenant {{Anderson}} has been officially assigned to the deviancy case… What do you make of him?”

options.text: UNPLEASANT: call him unpleasant and unprofessional.
options.outcome: “I find him unpleasant and unprofessional. He seems to have an addictive personality, has a lack of respect for procedure, and despises androids - which makes our relationship difficult.”

options.text: DYSFUNCTIONAL: call him dysfunctional, with a personal situation affecting his work.
options.outcome: “I would define him as ‘dysfunctional’. He obviously has a personal situation impacting his professional behavior and... seems to have no interest in the investigation.”

options.text: INTRIGUING: say he is irritable but used to be a good detective.
options.outcome: “I think he’s irritable, and socially challenged. But I also think he used to be a good detective… He’s an intriguing character.”

options.text: UNSURE: say you do not have enough information yet to judge him.
options.outcome: “He’s obviously not what I was expecting, but... I don’t have enough information yet to form a definitive opinion.”

nodes.adaptationNote: {{Amanda}}’s second question, asked on every path. Buttons in the game’s order; no arrow on any answer (template; PowerPyx “No effect”).

nodes.title: How to work with {{Hank}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, with {{Amanda}} in the zen garden. {{Amanda}}: “Unfortunately, we have no choice but to work with him… What do you think is the best approach?”

options.text: FRIENDLY: say you will try to build a friendly relationship and earn his trust.
options.outcome: “I will try to establish a friendly relationship. If I can get him to trust me, it will be helpful for the investigation.”

options.text: ADAPT: say you will adapt to his personality and avoid conflict.
options.outcome: “I will adapt to his personality. It is in the best interest of the investigation that I avoid conflict and try to accommodate his psychology.”

options.text: INDIFFERENT: say you will focus on the investigation and try to ignore him.
options.outcome: “I will focus on the investigation and try to ignore him. As long as he doesn’t interfere and we avoid conflict, he shouldn’t be a problem.”

options.text: DON’T KNOW: say you need more data before you decide.
options.outcome: “I don’t have enough data to decide that yet. I’ll learn more about him and try to adapt my behavior accordingly.”

nodes.adaptationNote: {{Amanda}}’s third question, with the template’s arrows: FRIENDLY Amanda small down (−1), ADAPT small down (−1), INDIFFERENT small up (+1), DON’T KNOW none (wiki: “Picking ‘indifferent’… up”, “Picking ‘friendly’ or ‘adapt’… down”; PowerPyx the same). The outcome adds {{Amanda}}’s closing lines, with the template’s variants for a {{Connor}} who died in The Interrogation and for a deviant never found.

nodes.title: Arrive at the police station
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, back in your body, in the reception hall of the {{Detroit}} police station. People wait on the seats. A woman: “I’m getting nervous, Mark.” The man with her: “It’s okay… Just tell ’em what happened to you.” “But it was all over so quickly... I didn’t even see his face!” Near a television, another woman hands a shaken man a cup of water. Gates bar the way into the station, and an android receptionist is at the desk. If you try the gates without signing in, an android stops you: “No access without prior authorization.”
facts: At the station reception you were told that Lieutenant {{Anderson}} had not arrived yet and that you could wait at his desk.

outcomes.0: The receptionist: “Can I help you?” “I’m here to see Lieutenant {{Anderson}}.” “Do you have authorization?” “Yes.” “Lieutenant {{Anderson}} hasn’t arrived yet, but you can wait at his desk.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint ARRIVE AT POLICE STATION, with the template’s reception scenes (the two couples, the gate android, the receptionist). Narrated, no choice, no stat change. The wiki’s note that a surviving {{Todd}} can be filing a report at the station is not built: the template’s reception couple does not name him.

nodes.title: The reception TV
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at the reception, before the gates. The television by the waiting seats is running the news.

media.title: the news at reception
facts: The news at the station reception: a Russian carrier and an American patrol boat clashed in the Arctic last night and exchanged warning shots, apparently with no damage or casualties. The Minister for Defense spoke of “intolerable provocation that cannot go unanswered”; the countries in the region have called for military forces to withdraw and for an international conference. Neither Moscow nor Washington has responded.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s “Watch TV” at reception: the Arctic report, optional, with no stat change (the Public Opinion page lists only the break-room report for this chapter). The newsreader and the minister are not named; the countries the report names are summarized as “the countries in the region”.

nodes.title: Waiting for {{Hank}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, inside the station. An android officer points out Lieutenant {{Anderson}}’s desk: “It’s that desk right there.” It is empty. On it are a headset, a coffee cup, a little tree, a box of donuts, a basketball cap, stickers, a book of matches, a plaque and his terminal; there are hairs on his chair. Officers work at the desks around it, and the holding cells are at the back. You can look around while you wait for him.

situationWhen.text: Somewhere behind you, Officer {{Ben}} is telling another officer: “No shit? That fucking machine could have killed everyone in the room…”

options.text: Go to the break room, then come back to wait at his desk.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} walks into the break room. Detective {{Gavin}} is there.

options.text: Sit down at his desk and wait for him.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} waits at the desk.

options.text: Sit for a moment in the chair in front of {{Hank}}’s desk, then get up and look around the station.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} sits in the chair facing the desk for a moment, then gets up. Around him the station goes about its morning: “Hey, you take a look at these samples yet?” “Lab report says they cut it with something.” “Maybe they’re trying out a new form of {{RedIce}}?”

options.text: Ask the officer at the next desk when Lieutenant {{Anderson}} usually arrives.
options.outcome: “Excuse me. Do you know what time Lieutenant {{Anderson}} usually arrives?” Officer {{Wilson}}: “Depends on where he was the night before… If we’re lucky, we’ll see him before noon…” “Thanks.”

options.text: Talk to Officer {{Chris}} at his desk.
options.outcome: Officer {{Chris}}: “Good Lord! They already repaired you?” “Unfortunately, my predecessor was too damaged to be repaired. I’m the new {{Connor}}.” “They don’t waste any time over at {{CyberLife}}… I don’t think {{Hank}}’s gonna be overjoyed to see you…”

Anderson” (the three articles, offered once a desk item has been scanned, since LEARN ABOUT HANK follows EXAMINE HANK’S DESK on the chart). The nameplate, tissue and police-cases strings in the string table are not placed by the template and are not built. The headset, cap, stickers and hairs unlock {{Connor}}’s MUSIC, BASKETBALL, ANTI-ANDROIDS and DOG topics later. Also here, with no stat change: Officer {{Wilson}} (“Finding Hank’s desk”), Officer {{Chris}} (the template’s three variants), the call to {{Hank}} with the game’s LEAVE A MESSAGE / HANG UP buttons (calling at all is optional, as in the game), the man in the holding cell, and, only if the android was sent back to his cell in The Interrogation, TALK WITH CARLOS’ ANDROID, which plays the two cell scenes that follow. The scene ends either by going to the break room (TALK WITH GAVIN and the break-room TV) or by sitting down to wait; either way {{Hank}} arrives next. These two exits are listed first, as in the other repeatable scenes of this chapter the main line comes first. Simplifications: in the game the station can be explored in any order and also while {{Hank}} is in {{Fowler}}’s office; here the cell, the desk and the call come before {{Hank}} arrives, and the break room is the last stop before he does. The background chatter is quoted once; {{Wilson}}’s private phone call is not built; the magazines are a media scene after this one.

situationWhen.text: In the break room you just left, the television is running the news.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: {{Ivanoff}} Says “Niet”!
facts: {{Detroit}} Today, “{{Ivanoff}} Says ‘Niet’!”: after President {{Warren}} demanded that “all Russian troops withdraw from the arctic immediately”, the Russian president called her comments “megaphone diplomacy” and said “US sabre-rattling is the number one threat to stability in the region.” The Kremlin set out Russia’s claim to the territory in a detailed statement, and he would “remind President {{Warren}}” that “the United States is subject to UN conventions, like everybody else.” The conflict shows no signs of abating. On the cover: {{CyberLife}} is the world’s first trillion-dollar company; the global population has reached 10 billion.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Famous Painter Dies
facts: {{Detroit}} Today, “Famous {{Detroit}} Painter Dies”: the death of the artist {{Carl}} {{Manfred}} is confirmed; the coroner described a “fatal cardiac event” induced by a stressful domestic situation, and his son {{Leo}} has asked the media to respect the family’s privacy. {{Carl}} rose to fame in the 2020s as a figurehead of neo-symbolism, went through a dark period marked by alcohol and drugs, and had returned to work in recent months. The Governor called him “one of {{Detroit}}’s brightest lights”; his estate will auction a collection of his paintings. On the cover: the UN warns of World War Three; President {{Warren}} is at 33% approval.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: The Three Laws of Robotic Parenting
facts: {{Detroit}} Today, “The Three Laws of Robotic Parenting”: {{CyberLife}}’s child androids, once doubted, are now among its bestsellers: “Customizable, removable LED, no hunger, no expensive childcare... no smelly diapers!” With unemployment at 37.3%, $7,500 for a child that skips the teenage years and college looks like a wise investment against $350,000 over 17 years. A sociologist warns that these androids are leading fewer parents to have children when birthrates are already far too low (“the baby doom”); {{CyberLife}}’s director of humanization calls this “the usual resistance to new ideas” and the androids “a triumph of humanization design”. On the cover: the UN warns of World War Three; President {{Warren}} is at 33% approval.

media.title: the break-room news
facts: The break-room news: several sources report that {{CyberLife}} has provided the {{Detroit}} police with a prototype detective android. Police assistant androids have existed for several years, but this would be the first case of an android authorized to play an active role in criminal investigations; no one at {{CyberLife}} was available to comment.

Then the next report: the first book written by an artificial intelligence, “Do Humans Dream of Mammalian Sheep?”, has shot to the top of the bestseller list, and critics are unanimous in their praise. Designed by {{CyberLife}}, the AI known as VOLTAIRE analyzed human centers of interest on social networks for several months before its algorithms generated the plot; according to several specialists, most books written in the coming years will be the work of artificial intelligence.

media.title: the break-room news
facts: The break-room news: the police found the body of thirty-year-old {{CarlosOrtiz}} in his home last night, after calls from concerned neighbors. Known to the police as a petty criminal, he is reported to have suffered from a psychiatric condition and rarely left his apartment; he is thought to have died several weeks ago. The police appear to be treating the death as a homicide. His android is also reported missing.

Then the next report: the first book written by an artificial intelligence, “Do Humans Dream of Mammalian Sheep?”, has shot to the top of the bestseller list, and critics are unanimous in their praise. Designed by {{CyberLife}}, the AI known as VOLTAIRE analyzed human centers of interest on social networks for several months before its algorithms generated the plot; according to several specialists, most books written in the coming years will be the work of artificial intelligence.

options.outcome: “Have you known Captain {{Fowler}} for long?” {{Hank}}: “Yeah... Too long.”

nodes.title: Morning in the parking lot
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is 10:25 in the morning, the day after you fled {{Todd}}’s house with {{Alice}}. You spent the night in an abandoned car in a fenced parking lot, and {{Alice}} is still asleep on the back seat. You get out quietly and leave her sleeping. Anyone who looks at you closely can still see an android: the LED on your temple, your hair as it was.

situationWhen.text: You are wearing the clothes you took from the laundromat.
You are still in your android uniform.

facts: You and {{Alice}} spent the night in an abandoned car in a parking lot; she is asleep, and you need to change how you look before you go anywhere.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} leaves {{Alice}} asleep in the car and looks around the lot.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint MORNING IN PARKING LOT and the unmissable LEAVE ALICE ASLEEP IN CAR (PowerPyx: “simply exit the car”), one event. The start is chosen by Fugitives (where Kara slept); this row plays when she slept in the abandoned car (the module reads `ch10Shelter`, `shelter`, `karaRoute`, then `ch10Ending`, and falls back to the car). Date and time from the template (NOV 6TH, 2038, AM 10:25), without the year. nodes.title: The parking lot
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the fenced parking lot where you spent the night. {{Alice}} is asleep in the abandoned car. Before you wake her you can look around: old tires lie in front of the car, magazines on the ground beside them, a dumpster stands against the back wall, the car has a trunk, and the gate you came in by looks out on the street. You do one thing at a time, in any order.

situationWhen.text: Your hair is cut and the LED is gone.
The trunk is jammed shut.
Police are patrolling the street outside the gate.

options.text: FIND SOME RUSTED SCISSORS: pull the old scissors out of the tire in front of the car.
options.outcome: A pair of rusted scissors is stuck in a tire in front of the car. {{Kara}} pulls them out and kneels at the car’s side mirror.

options.text: FIND BURNT ANDROID: look behind the dumpster by the back wall.
options.fact: Behind a dumpster in the parking lot lies an android that was burned to death, an AX420 by the number on its uniform; above it someone has sprayed “DEATH TO ANDROIDS”.
options.outcome: Behind the dumpster lies an android that has been burned to death; the number on its uniform reads AX420. Sprayed on the wall above it: “DEATH TO ANDROIDS”.

options.text: READ “CYBER-WILDLIFE”: the magazine lying in front of the car.
options.fact: {{Detroit}} Today, “Cyber-Wildlife”: {{CyberLife}} is about to open the first android zoo, in Los Angeles, showing animals that have become extinct in the last thirty years (turtles, polar bears, mountain gorillas, African elephants and several species of tiger), which it promises will be “more real than the real thing”. The cover adds that US life expectancy is now 91, and that 0.4% of the world’s population holds 94% of its wealth.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} reads the magazine: {{CyberLife}} is opening an android zoo of extinct animals.

options.text: READ “ANDROID AND {{CANADA}}”: the other side of it.
options.fact: A travel advertisement for {{Canada}}: “where the air is clean and the welcome is always warm.” Although the United States voted in its Android Act in 2028, the parliament there has again put off deciding whether to permit androids: they are not sold there and have no official status, while in the United States they fuel record growth and record unemployment.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} reads the advertisement: across the border, androids are still not allowed.

options.text: TRY TO OPEN CAR TRUNK: see what is in the back of the car.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} tries the trunk. It is jammed and will not open; she needs something to force it.

options.text: FIND A CROWBAR: look for something to force the trunk with.
options.outcome: A crowbar lies on the other side of the car, near the fence that borders the abandoned house next door. {{Kara}} picks it up.

options.text: FIND SOME CLOTHES: force the trunk open with the crowbar and put on what is inside.
options.fact: You found clothes in the trunk of the abandoned car and changed out of your android uniform.
options.outcome: The trunk gives. Inside are some old clothes, a jacket among them. {{Kara}} takes off her android uniform and puts them on.

options.text: CHECK NEIGHBORHOOD: look out through the gate you came in by.
options.fact: Police are patrolling the street outside the parking lot; you need to reach the train station without being noticed.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks out through the gate. There are police in the street. {{Kara}}: “The police are on our trail… We need to reach the train station without being noticed.”

options.text: WAKE UP {{ALICE}}: go back to the car and wake her.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “{{Alice}}… Wake up, {{Alice}}…” {{Alice}}: “So it wasn’t a nightmare…” {{Kara}}: “No... No, it wasn’t a nightmare. How do you feel?” {{Alice}}: “I’m cold… What are we gonna do now?..” {{Kara}}: “That android we saw yesterday... he gave me an address, he said we could get help there. The train passes just on the other side of the road, the station can’t be far… You feel okay to walk a little? Let’s go then.” {{Alice}}: “You’re pretty like that. You really look like a human now.” They leave the parking lot.

nodes.title: Talk to {{Alice}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, beside {{Alice}} in the motel room. She has just woken up and remembered last night. What do you say to her?

nodes.title: The motel room
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the motel room with {{Alice}}. You have said you will run her a bath; the bathroom is through the door. In the room there is a clock, a window onto the street, a painting on the wall, and the television, with magazines in front of it. You still need to change how you look: your hair, and the LED on your temple. You do one thing at a time, in any order.

situationWhen.text: The bath is running.
Your hair is cut and the LED is gone; the bath is still filling.

options.text: DRAW A BATH FOR {{ALICE}}: go into the bathroom and start the water.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} turns on the bath taps. While the tub fills she looks at her face in the mirror over the sink: the face of the runaway AX400.

options.text: LOOK AT THE CLOCK.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks at the clock. The morning is getting on.

options.text: LOOK OUTSIDE: look out of the window at the street.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks out of the window at the street outside the motel.

options.text: READ “CYBER-WILDLIFE”: the magazine in front of the television.
options.fact: {{Detroit}} Today, “Cyber-Wildlife”: {{CyberLife}} is about to open the first android zoo, in Los Angeles, showing animals that have become extinct in the last thirty years (turtles, polar bears, mountain gorillas, African elephants and several species of tiger), which it promises will be “more real than the real thing”. The cover adds that US life expectancy is now 91, and that 0.4% of the world’s population holds 94% of its wealth.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} reads the magazine: {{CyberLife}} is opening an android zoo of extinct animals.

options.text: READ “ANDROID AND {{CANADA}}”: the other side of it.
options.fact: A travel advertisement for {{Canada}}: “where the air is clean and the welcome is always warm.” Although the United States voted in its Android Act in 2028, the parliament there has again put off deciding whether to permit androids: they are not sold there and have no official status, while in the United States they fuel record growth and record unemployment.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} reads the advertisement: across the border, androids are still not allowed.

options.text: LOOK AT THE PAINTING on the wall.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} looks at the painting on the motel room wall.

options.text: FINISH DRAWING BATH: turn off the taps; the bath is ready.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} turns off the water and comes back into the room. {{Alice}} looks at her: “You’re pretty like that. You really look like a human now.” {{Kara}}: “Your bath’s ready.”

options.text: CHANGE CHANNEL: watch the news with {{Alice}} without running the bath.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} stays in the room with {{Alice}} and turns to the television.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s DRAW A BATH FOR ALICE (then the hair, next scene), [ EXPLORE MOTEL ROOM ] with LOOK AT THE CLOCK, LOOK OUTSIDE, READ “CYBER-WILDLIFE”, READ “ANDROID AND {{CANADA}}” and LOOK AT THE PAINTING, and FINISH DRAWING BATH, as one repeatable scene. The chart lets Kara explore before the bath (TALK TO ALICE has an edge straight to the hub) or after REMOVE LED, and FINISH DRAWING BATH bypasses the hub, so here the room can be explored any time before the bath is finished, which ends the phase and needs the haircut (Alice’s compliment follows it in the template). The sources give nothing about the clock, the window or the painting, so their outcomes say only what Kara looks at. The magazines are chart nodes inside the hub; their facts are the wiki’s article text. Outcome lines are the template’s (“You’re pretty like that…”, “Your bath’s ready.”). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one. The direct TALK TO ALICE > EXPLORE MOTEL ROOM > CHANGE CHANNEL edge is also available without starting the bath or haircut. This follows the chart; whether the game forces a haircut elsewhere on that edge remains an operator check (research §8.5).

nodes.title: The news

nodes.title: Cheer {{Alice}} up
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, with {{Alice}} in the motel room. She is frightened, and she has nobody but you. You kneel beside her. What do you tell her?

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We can’t change the past, {{Alice}}... But we can decide the future... We’re gonna pull through, and soon all this will just be a bad memory.”

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “It’s us against the world, {{Alice}}… Just the two of us… We have to learn to trust each other… I only have you, and you only have me… And I’m going to do everything I can to make you happy again.”

nodes.title: Breakfast

nodes.title: Room 28

HANK CHECKS MOTEL ROOM (“It’s gone…”, template) is the first option’s outcome; “Found you.” is the string table’s BACKDOOR line. CHECK THE DOOR sets `chase`. nodes.title: In the street
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, out on the street with {{Alice}}. The train station is a few blocks down the road. Between you and it, police officers are posted along both sides of the street. To get there unseen you would have to move from cover to cover, crossing from one side to the other when nobody is looking.

nodes.title: Getting past the police
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, holding {{Alice}}’s hand on a street full of police. The station is ahead. Officers stand on both sides of the street; there is a bus shelter by the laundromat, umbrellas outside a café, an ATM, and gaps in the traffic to cross in.

options.text: SNEAK PAST POLICE FORCES: go from cover to cover, crossing whenever the officers look away.
options.outcome: Across to the motel side, behind the bus shelter by the laundromat, a fast dash over the road, under an umbrella, behind the ATM: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} slip past every officer.

options.text: Walk straight down the street to the station without hiding.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} walk down the street in the open.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s group SNEAK PAST POLICE FORCES / SPOTTED BY POLICE. In the game it is a stealth sequence, not a menu; the string table lists its steps (avoid the cops in front of the squat and the motel, cross to the coffee shop, hide near the laundromat, cross to the bank, hide using an umbrella, hide in the pawn shop), and PowerPyx gives the route (motel side, bus shelter, “cross the street fast. If you are a bit too slow, you will be spotted”, umbrella, ATM). Sneaking is one action with a failure branch; walking in the open always gets them SPOTTED BY POLICE. The risk value is unsourced: no source gives a probability for any check in this chapter (research note §3); Experienced difficulty is modelled, so every chart failure branch is reachable. Fixes the old K09: walking openly now always leads to the chase and never to a death in the street (the chart has no death before CONNOR PURSUES KARA), and the old situation’s “the news is calling you a kidnapper” is gone (no report mentions Alice). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: The squat
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. There is blue blood on the fence around one of the abandoned houses: another android has been here. You knock at the door, walk round to the front and go in. {{Hank}} waits outside. Inside, a scarred android in old clothes meets you, twitching and muttering to himself.
facts: Blue blood on a fence led you to an abandoned house, where a scarred android is squatting.

outcomes.0: The scarred android watches {{Connor}}, frightened.

nodes.title: Interrogate the squat android
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, inside the squat, facing the scarred android. What do you ask him?

options.text: AX400: ask whether he has seen an AX400.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I’m looking for an AX400. Have you seen it?” The android: “{{Ralph}}’s seen nobody…”

options.text: DEVIANTS: ask whether there are any other androids here.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Are there any other androids here?” The android: “Other androids?.. No... {{Ralph}} is alone…”

options.text: REASSURE: tell him not to be afraid; you are not going to hurt him.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Don’t be afraid. I’m not gonna hurt you.” The android says nothing.

options.text: BLUE BLOOD: tell him there is blue blood on the fence, and another android was here.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “There’s blue blood on the fence. I know another android was here.” The android: “{{Ralph}} scratched himself coming through... That’s {{Ralph}}’s blood…”

options.text: PRESSURIZE: tell him you know he has seen it.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “You’ve seen it, haven’t you? I know you’ve seen it.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s INTERROGATE SQUAT ANDROID: the template’s prompt AX400 / DEVIANTS / REASSURE / BLUE BLOOD, in its order, with PRESSURIZE added only when Kara threatened Ralph at the table (the template’s two variants). After a threat every answer ends in SQUAT DEVIANT INFORMS ON AX400 (“She ran out the back door!”, then “It’s in the area… Call it in!”) and the chase; otherwise in SQUAT ANDROID KEEPS QUIET and the search (next scene). Replaces the old C09a (“Push past him and search upstairs”, risk 0.2, with an unsourced Amanda change and a fall down the stairs): the template has no failure branch here. The informing is driven by this chapter’s THREATEN, not by Fugitives. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one.

nodes.title: Investigate the ground floor
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the ground floor of the squat. {{Ralph}}, the scarred android, keeps close to you; his stress rises and falls as you move about. There is a table, a fire burning in the fireplace, a door to the kitchen, and the stairs, with an old arcade machine beside them. {{Hank}} is waiting outside. You do one thing at a time, in any order.

options.text: CHECK UPSTAIRS: go up the stairs and ask whether anyone is up there.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} climbs halfway up the stairs. “Is anyone upstairs?” {{Ralph}}: “No. Nobody.” {{Connor}} believes him.

options.text: ANALYZE SQUAT ANDROID: scan him.
options.fact: Your scan of {{Ralph}}: PROCESSING LED, signs of software instability, probability of self-destruction moderate; MODEL WR600 - Gardener, serial# 021 753 034, status REPORTED MISSING; BURN MARK, irreversible skin damage, probable cause extreme heat.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} scans {{Ralph}}. PROCESSING LED: signs of software instability; probability of self-destruction: moderate. MODEL WR600 - Gardener; serial# 021 753 034; status: REPORTED MISSING. BURN MARK: irreversible skin damage; probable cause: extreme heat.

options.text: CHECK TABLE.
options.fact: The table in the squat is laid for three, with food on it.
options.outcome: The table is laid for three, with food on it. Androids do not eat.

options.text: CHECK UNDER THE STAIRS: go round the side of the stairs, by the arcade machine.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} steps round the side of the stairs.

options.text: CHECK KITCHEN: look through the kitchen door.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} looks into the kitchen. Nobody is there.

options.text: CHECK FIREPLACE.
options.fact: A fire is burning in the squat’s fireplace, though androids do not need warmth.
options.outcome: A fire is burning in the fireplace. Androids do not need warmth.

options.text: LEAVE THE SQUAT: go back out to {{Hank}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} gives up the search and goes back out to {{Hank}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s [ INVESTIGATE SQUAT GROUND FLOOR ] hub after SQUAT ANDROID KEEPS QUIET, as one repeatable scene, with its nodes in the chart’s order: CHECK UPSTAIRS (a dead end: “Is anyone upstairs?” / “No. Nobody.”, template; PowerPyx: “Connor believes him”), ANALYZE SQUAT ANDROID (the template’s three scan clues, quoted), CHECK TABLE (“Dinnerware for three and food”, PowerPyx), CHECK UNDER THE STAIRS (Ralph’s stress rises near “the stairs and arcade-machine”; stepping to the side of the stairs makes Ralph hold Connor while Kara and Alice run, PowerPyx: no failure branch, so no risk), CHECK KITCHEN (“no one will be inside”), CHECK FIREPLACE (“Androids don’t need warmth”). HANK COMMANDS CONNOR TO LEAVE is the game’s timer (“If you wait for a long time”, PowerPyx), modelled as Hank’s two calls from the template after the third and the fifth look that finds nothing (counts unsourced). LEAVE THE SQUAT is the string table’s SQUAT.C.LEAVE, offered as the chart’s unlabelled box between the hub and SQUAT ANDROID DISAPPEARS (research note §8 Q1; flagged). nodes.title: {{Ferndale}} Station

Find {{Jericho}}!..” When he touched you, he left something in your memory that you could not read at the time.

Nobody else on the platform looks at it twice. You scan the mark, and the key in your memory decodes it: it is a sign left for androids, and it shows you what the next sign looks like.

nodes.title: A magazine on the bench
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the platform at {{Ferndale}} Station, before the escalators down to the street. Someone has left a digital magazine on a bench; you can swipe from one cover story to the next.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Android on the Run!
facts: Residents of a {{Detroit}} suburb watched a chase after a police manhunt, with roadblocks and dozens of police interviews, flushed out a fugitive. The rogue AX400 model is thought to be suffering from an extremely rare malfunction and took extreme measures to avoid the police, even dashing across a busy highway. Eyewitness statements are inconclusive, there is no official report, and no {{CyberLife}} spokesperson was available for comment.

media.title: Tech Addict: {{CyberLife}}’s ‘Fortune Teller’ Computer
facts: {{CyberLife}} has unveiled a quantum supercomputer capable of “exaflops”, a billion billion operations per second. It will calculate the probability of mass-extinction events, such as aggressive alien invasions or global disasters like meteors or superviruses, so that humanity can anticipate and prepare for them.

media.title: Tech Addict: Android Astronauts to Explore Io
facts: NASA has launched a crew of five androids on a three-year journey to Io, one of Jupiter’s moons: the first all-machine crew. NASA’s director calls androids an extraordinary asset for the conquest of space, because cosmic radiation destroys human DNA. No return journey is planned; the androids will work on Io for several months before the extreme conditions destroy them.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s three magazine nodes, READ “ON THE RUN”, READ “FORTUNE TELLER” and READ “ANDROID ASTRONAUTS”: covers of one magazine on a bench on the platform (wiki: “on a bench right after Markus gets off the train”; PowerPyx: “before going down the escalator”, “Swipe right to change cover topics”). Android Astronauts to Explore Io (Tech Addict #13) is always there. Android on the Run! (Detroit Today #32) appears only if Kara and Alice were pursued by Connor in On the Run (wiki); CyberLife’s ‘Fortune Teller’ Computer (Tech Addict #15) appears otherwise. The pursuit is read from On the Run’s flag (`chase`), set whenever the highway chase began, including when it ended with Kara and Alice dead on the highway; a PowerPyx reader’s unconfirmed list puts that case and KARA & ALICE VANISHED under Fortune Teller, but the wiki’s condition is the pursuit itself. Article facts are condensed from the wiki’s magazine pages; NASA’s director, CyberLife’s Director of Futurology and the suburb (Camden) are left unnamed. Corrected from the earlier version of this scene: the article mentions no child, the “extremely rare malfunction” is not a CyberLife statement (no spokesperson was available), and the chapter is in daylight (04:30 PM), not at night. No public-opinion effect: no source gives one.
