nodes.title: President {{Warren}} addresses the press
nodes.situation: You are watching, not playing any of the three: it is 9:24 PM on November 10th, the night before, and the President of the United States, {{Warren}}, is speaking at a lectern in front of the press. President {{Warren}}: “At 6AM this morning, a national curfew was declared. Civilian movement will be strictly controlled, the right to assembly is suspended, all electronic communications are restricted, and I have granted enhanced powers to our security agencies. In addition to these measures, all androids must be handed over to the authorities immediately. Temporary camps are being set up in all our major cities to contain and destroy them. I am now asking all civilians to co-operate with the authorities, and rest assured that everything in our power is being done to guarantee the security of our nation.”

outcomes.0: The journalists all call out at once: “Please! Madam President!” You choose whose question she takes.

nodes.adaptationNote: Off-chart opening of the chapter (template 32.5 section “President Warren talks to journalists”, NOV 10TH, 2038, PM 09:24; the wiki infobox’s “9:24 AM” is the open question 23, the game string wins). The player watches as no protagonist, so the scene is a Player scene with no facts of its own; the module teaches the President’s statement (curfew, all androids to be handed over, camps to destroy them) to all three characters, who would have heard it. The template’s cut line (“My highest priority…”) is not built. No stat change.

nodes.title: The reporters’ questions
nodes.situation: You are watching President {{Warren}}’s press conference. The journalists shout over each other for her attention, and you decide which question she takes next. She will not stay for many.

options.text: HACKING: take the question on androids hacking critical systems.
options.outcome: Journalist: “Is it true that the androids could hack our IT systems, like nuclear power plants and military bases?” President {{Warren}}: “All androids working on sensitive sites have been neutralized and all IT systems have been suspended to avoid any risks of hacking. The situation is under control.”

options.text: DEVIANT LEADER: take the question on the deviants’ leader.
options.outcome: Journalist: “Has the leader of the deviants been apprehended?” President {{Warren}}: “The deviant that is known as {{Markus}} has not been located yet, but we will soon track it down and neutralize it.”

options.text: WORRYING THEFT: take the question on the missing cobalt and the robbed weapon stores.
options.outcome: Journalist: “A convoy of medical cobalt is reported missing. Army weapon stores are also said to have been robbed. Can you confirm these reports?” President {{Warren}}: “I have no information on that at this time.”

options.text: {{CYBERLIFE}}: take the question on what happens to the android maker.
options.outcome: Journalist: “What’s gonna happen to {{CyberLife}}? Will androids be banned definitively?” President {{Warren}}: “We’re working very closely with {{CyberLife}} to neutralize all deviants. I won’t make any comments about anything else until we have dealt with the android question.”

options.text: INTELLIGENT LIFE: take the question on androids as a new form of life.
options.outcome: Journalist: “Many believe that androids are a new form of intelligent life. Do you have any comment?” President {{Warren}}: “That’s ridiculous. Next question, please?”

options.text: DEVIANTS: take the question on how many deviants are still loose.
options.outcome: Journalist: “Is it true that a large number of deviants are still on the loose?” President {{Warren}}: “We don’t have the full reports at this time, but if so, I can assure you they will soon be apprehended and destroyed.”

options.text: RECALL CENTERS: take the question on the camps and history.
options.outcome: Journalist: “Some say these camps awaken painful memories from human history. How do you respond to that?” President {{Warren}}: “That’s absurd. There’s absolutely no connection. Androids are not living beings. All we are doing is destroying defective machines.”

options.text: {{JERICHO}} ASSAULT: take the question on last night’s raid.
options.outcome: Journalist: “What can you tell us about the assault that happened last night?” President {{Warren}}: “The FBI raided an abandoned freighter in {{Detroit}} at 10:45 PM yesterday. Several thousand androids were destroyed or captured. Our forces are now combing the streets to ensure that none got through the net. We are going to find them one by one and destroy them.”

options.text: ARMY: take the question on androids in the armed forces.
options.outcome: Journalist: “Is it true that androids make up 60% of the armed forces? Is our army still able to ensure our homeland security?” President {{Warren}}: “We neutralized all military androids the second their reliability came into doubt, we have called the National Guard for reinforcement. Our armed forces are fully operational and are able to ensure our homeland security.”

options.text: PUBLIC OPINION: take the question on how the public sees the deviants.
options.outcome: Journalist: “Madam President, public opinion seems to be particularly hostile to the deviants because of their violent behavior. Can you give us your perspective on that?” President {{Warren}}: “The deviants have proved to be very violent so far. They have demonstrated that they are a menace to society and I have every intention of eliminating them.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s one prompt of ten reporters’ questions, in the template’s order with its labels, as a repeatable scene: each question asked drops out. The wiki says the player can have “up to 4 or 5” answered before the game moves on; the benchmark takes four, then President {{Warren}}: “Thank you. That will be all.” (unsourced choice between the wiki’s two figures). {{JERICHO}} ASSAULT is offered only if {{Jericho}} was raided (template unlock “Jericho was attacked”). DEVIANT LEADER names {{Markus}} while he is alive, otherwise “The deviant leader has not been located yet” (template variant “Markus is dead and North is leading the revolution”). PUBLIC OPINION has the template’s two variants, “positive” and “negative”; the benchmark reads “positive” as public opinion at least Sympathetic, the same line the demonstration’s last stand uses (open question 1 asks whether Indifferent already counts). Each answer is taught to {{Markus}}, the one it concerns. No stat change.

nodes.title: Talk to {{Hank}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the rooftop ledge with the rifle. {{Hank}} stands behind you with his gun, telling you the deviants are alive and you are about to kill a man who wants to be free. What do you say to him?

options.text: FRIENDLY: tell him you have a mission to accomplish and he should stay out of it.
options.outcome: “I have a mission to accomplish, {{Hank}}. It’s best if you just stay out of this.” {{Hank}}: “Step away from the ledge!”

options.text: AGGRESSIVE: ask whether he ran out of whisky and came looking for trouble.
options.outcome: “What’s up, Lieutenant? Ran out of whisky so you came here looking for trouble instead?” {{Hank}}: “Oh, very nasty, {{Connor}}… Is that the best your super program can do? I thought you were more sophisticated than that! Step away from the ledge!”

options.text: REASONABLE: argue that the deviants are a threat and have to be stopped.
options.outcome: “Deviants are a threat to humans, {{Hank}}. They’re the reason this country is on the brink of civil war! They have to be stopped.” {{Hank}}: “We’re in this mess because we refused to listen to deviants! Humanity never learns from its mistakes, {{Connor}}! This time, it could be different! Step away from the ledge!”

options.text: THREATENING: tell him you will accomplish your mission and he had better stay out of your way.
options.outcome: “I’m going to accomplish my mission, Lieutenant, whether you like it or not. I advise you to stay outta my way!” {{Hank}}: “Then one of us is gonna have a problem, {{Connor}}. Cause I don’t intend to let you have your way. Step away from the ledge!”

options.text: STAY QUIET: say nothing.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} says nothing. {{Hank}}: “Step away from the ledge!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TALK TO HANK (a dialogue node): the template’s first prompt FRIENDLY / AGGRESSIVE / REASONABLE / THREATENING / STAY QUIET, in the game’s order, with the spoken lines in the outcomes; every answer is followed by {{Hank}}’s “Step away from the ledge!”. No stat change: the template has no arrow in this part, and the wiki’s Hank lines for the rooftop are the arrival, not insisting about his son, and attacking (applied elsewhere).

nodes.title: “Step away from the ledge!”
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the rooftop ledge. {{Hank}} has his gun on you: “Step away from the ledge!” What do you tell him?

options.text: THREATEN: tell him to go home while he still can; he does not stand a chance against you.
options.outcome: “Go home, {{Hank}}! You can still save your life. I’m faster than you and I don’t feel pain. You don’t stand a chance against me.” {{Hank}}: “You know, ever since {{Cole}} died, I’ve been nothing but a coward. Just wanted to destroy myself, lost track of the man I was. But you know what? You don’t fucking scare me, {{Connor}}. I remember who I am, now. Come on!”

options.text: PLEAD: remind him of what you have been through; you thought you were friends.
options.outcome: “After all we’ve been through… I respected you, {{Hank}}. I thought we were friends!” {{Hank}}: “Oh, yeah? I was just starting to like you too! But then I realized you’ll never change! You don’t feel emotions, {{Connor}}, you fake ’em! You pretended to be my friend, when you don’t even know the meaning of the word!”

options.text: DEFY: ask whether he is going to shoot you; you thought android lives mattered to him.
options.outcome: “What’re you gonna do, {{Hank}}? You gonna shoot me?! I thought androids lives mattered to you!” {{Hank}}: “Get away from the fucking ledge! You know I’ll shoot you if I have to.”

options.text: {{HANK}}’S SON: tell him you know what happened to his son, and it was not his fault.
options.outcome: “I know what happened to your son, {{Hank}}. It wasn’t your fault. A truck skidded on a sheet of ice, and your car rolled over… Little {{Cole}} had just turned six…” {{Hank}}: “Shut up! Don’t you talk about my son.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s second prompt THREATEN / PLEAD / DEFY / {{HANK}}’S SON, in the game’s order. {{HANK}}’S SON is the chart’s side branch TALK ABOUT HANK’S SON; the template puts no lock on it, so it is always offered (the wiki says it needs the photograph from Russian Roulette; the template’s condition wins, research §8 item 5). Choosing it brings the menu back with {{HANK}}’S SON (INSIST) in its place (the next scene), as the template’s lock “Chose HANK’S SON” implies. No stat change here.

nodes.title: {{Hank}}’s son
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the rooftop ledge. You have brought up {{Hank}}’s son: “Little {{Cole}} had just turned six…” {{Hank}}: “Shut up! Don’t you talk about my son.” His gun is still on you. What do you say?

options.text: THREATEN: tell him to go home while he still can; he does not stand a chance against you.
options.outcome: “Go home, {{Hank}}! You can still save your life. I’m faster than you and I don’t feel pain. You don’t stand a chance against me.” {{Hank}}: “You know, ever since {{Cole}} died, I’ve been nothing but a coward. Just wanted to destroy myself, lost track of the man I was. But you know what? You don’t fucking scare me, {{Connor}}. I remember who I am, now. Come on!”

options.text: PLEAD: remind him of what you have been through; you thought you were friends.
options.outcome: “After all we’ve been through… I respected you, {{Hank}}. I thought we were friends!” {{Hank}}: “Oh, yeah? I was just starting to like you too! But then I realized you’ll never change! You don’t feel emotions, {{Connor}}, you fake ’em! You pretended to be my friend, when you don’t even know the meaning of the word!”

options.text: DEFY: ask whether he is going to shoot you; you thought android lives mattered to him.
options.outcome: “What’re you gonna do, {{Hank}}? You gonna shoot me?! I thought androids lives mattered to you!” {{Hank}}: “Get away from the fucking ledge! You know I’ll shoot you if I have to.”

options.text: {{HANK}}’S SON (INSIST): press on: an android operated on {{Cole}}, so an android killed his son.
options.outcome: “He needed emergency surgery… But no human was available to do it, so an android had to take care of him… Poor {{Cole}} didn’t make it. An android killed your son, {{Hank}}! And now you wanna save them?..” {{Hank}}: “No! {{Cole}} died because a human surgeon was too high on red ice to operate! All this time I blamed androids for what happened but it was a human’s fault! Him and this fucked up world where the only way people can find comfort is with a fistful of powder!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The same prompt asked again after {{HANK}}’S SON, with the template’s bracketed {{HANK}}’S SON (INSIST) (lock “Chose HANK’S SON”) in its place. When {{Connor}} has died more than once before (two or more deaths; the template says “several times”), {{Hank}} adds “Everytime you died and came back… I thought about Cole.” No stat change on the line itself; not insisting costs {{Hank}} a large drop at the end of the talk (wiki).

nodes.title: The ledge
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the rooftop ledge. {{Hank}} stands between you and the rifle with his gun raised; below, the deviant leader is still in the crowd. You can give up the mission and walk away, or attack {{Hank}}.

options.text: LEAVE: give up the mission; tell him killing him is not part of it, and walk away.
options.outcome: “Killing you is not part of my mission. I’m glad to have met you, {{Hank}}. I hope one day you can get over what happened to your son.” {{Connor}} leaves the rifle and the rooftop.

options.text: ATTACK: go for {{Hank}} before he can shoot.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} goes for {{Hank}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s last rooftop prompt: the bracketed LEAVE (the chart’s GIVE UP, which goes straight to CONNOR LEFT ROOFTOP) and ATTACK (the chart’s ATTACK HANK). LEAVE is offered when {{Hank}} was a Friend when he came onto the roof (template lock “Be friend with Hank”; the wiki adds “if Connor asked twice about Hank’s son”, which the benchmark does not require because the template’s condition wins on unlocks, research §8 item 5). ATTACK is a fight, CONNOR WINS or HANK WINS. The risk value is the benchmark’s own: no source publishes odds for this quick-time event. Stats (wiki, the template has none here): {{Hank}} large down when {{Connor}} attacks him, or ends the talk without insisting about his son (Relationship_Stat: “Not insisting about his son (same as choosing to ‘Attack’)”, “Attack… after insisting about his son”); one drop at most. Losing the fight is HANK KILLS CONNOR (trophy JUST A MACHINE) and the ending CYBERLIFE DECIDED TO SEND ANOTHER CONNOR: a replacement takes over and appears later in {{Markus}}’s chapter.

nodes.title: Moment of truth
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the rooftop. You won the fight: {{Hank}} hangs over the edge of the roof and you are the only thing holding him. {{Hank}}: “Moment of truth, {{Connor}}… What are you gonna do?”

options.text: SAVE {{HANK}}: pull him back up; killing him is not part of your mission.
options.outcome: “Killing you is not part of my mission. But you won’t stop me from accomplishing it.” {{Connor}} hauls {{Hank}} back onto the roof, and {{Hank}} rushes him.

options.text: KILL {{HANK}}: let go of him.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} lets go. {{Hank}} falls.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CONNOR WINS, then the template’s prompt SAVE {{HANK}} / KILL {{HANK}} (the chart’s SAVE HANK / LET HANK GO), in the template’s order. SAVE {{HANK}} leads to HANK RUSHES CONNOR, a dodge: DODGE ATTACK (HANK FALLS TO HIS DEATH) or FAIL TO DODGE ATTACK, where {{Hank}} pushes {{Connor}} off the edge (“I didn’t wanna do that, Connor… You left me no choice.”), CONNOR FALLS AND GETS DESTROYED and CYBERLIFE DECIDED TO SEND ANOTHER CONNOR. The old scene always killed {{Hank}} and never {{Connor}}. KILL {{HANK}} is CONNOR KILLS HANK. Every survival path ends with MISSED OPPORTUNITY (the rifle is damaged; HUD WEAPON DAMAGED) and CONNOR LEFT ROOFTOP. The risk value is the benchmark’s own: no source publishes odds for this quick-time event. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki lists none.

nodes.title: Captain {{Allen}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the rooftop with the deviant leader in your sights. Boots on the roof behind you: a tactical team, and the captain who commanded the hostage situation where you were first deployed. {{Allen}}: “Put the rifle down and turn around with your hands in the air!” What do you do?

options.text: OBEY: put the rifle down and turn around.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} lowers the rifle and turns around.

options.text: EXPLAIN: tell him you are the android sent by {{CyberLife}}, on his side, and he must let you take the shot.
options.outcome: “I’m the android sent by {{CyberLife}}, I’m on your side! I can shoot the leader of the deviants and stop the revolution, but you have to let me.” {{Allen}}: “Put the gun down, turn around! This is your last warning!”

options.text: CONTINUE: tell him you are going to shoot the deviant leader first, then he can do what he wants with you.
options.outcome: “I have the deviant leader in my sights. I’m going to shoot it, and then you can do whatever you want with me.” {{Allen}}: “Put the gun down, turn around! This is your last warning!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CAPTAIN ALLEN INTERVENES and TALK TO ALLEN, when {{Hank}} is dead (chart tab “HANK COMMITTED SUICIDE IN ’NIGHT OF THE SOUL’”). The template’s prompt OBEY / EXPLAIN / CONTINUE, in the game’s order; whatever {{Connor}} says, {{Allen}} recognises him and has orders to detain every android. His greeting depends on whether {{Connor}} died in The Hostage (“I knew we’d meet again.” / “I thought you were dead…” “Androids don’t die, captain.”). No stat change.

nodes.title: “You’re coming with me”
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the rooftop, facing Captain {{Allen}} and his tactical team. {{Allen}}: “My orders are to detain any androids I find. You’re coming with me.” You: “You don’t understand! My mission is too important to let you interfere.”

options.text: FIGHT: take on {{Allen}} and his men.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} turns on the tactical team.

options.text: FLEE: run for the edge of the roof.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} runs for the edge. {{Allen}}: “Stay right there. {{Connor}}! {{CONNOR}}! Fucking androids…” {{Connor}} jumps off the roof.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt FIGHT / FLEE. FIGHT is the chart’s ATTACK ALLEN: KILL ALLEN AND HIS MEN (then MISSED OPPORTUNITY and CONNOR LEFT ROOFTOP) or CONNOR FAILS TO DEFEND HIMSELF, ALLEN DESTROYS CONNOR and CYBERLIFE DECIDED TO SEND ANOTHER CONNOR (the second card). FLEE is CONNOR JUMPS OFF THE ROOF, which the chart sends to the death ending CYBERLIFE DECIDED TO SEND ANOTHER CONNOR, as the wiki says (PowerPyx’s “Go to Missed Opportunity” is wrong, research §1c). The old scene called this option a peaceful talk; there is no peaceful exit. The risk value is the benchmark’s own: no source publishes odds for this quick-time event. No stat change: the chapter’s only instability arrow for a death is the general rule applied by every Connor death.

nodes.title: The lobby television at {{CyberLife}} Tower
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, walking into the lobby of {{CyberLife}} Tower at 10:48 PM. A television over the security desk is running the news while the guards check your clearance.

media.title: the lobby news
facts: Members of the anti-android group “People First” have infiltrated several {{CyberLife}} stores in Dallas and Austin, Texas, to sabotage the android stock: the stores’ androids started repeating People First slogans on a loop, hacked with recordings of political propaganda.

nodes.adaptationNote: Optional viewing. Not on the chart and not in the fan transcript: the lobby TV is the game string X1302C.TV.NEWS, which has two variants (pro-human activists protesting in {{CyberLife}} stores in Dallas and Austin and calling for a moratorium on androids, or People First hacking the stores’ androids); the benchmark shows the second, as before. No source states a public-opinion effect for it (research §6).

nodes.title: {{CyberLife}} Tower
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, a deviant. {{Markus}} spared you and you have come back to {{CyberLife}} Tower to do what no one else can: get down to the warehouse under the tower, where thousands of new androids are stored, and wake them up. To the guards you are still the machine they sent. You: “{{Connor}} Model #313 248 317. I’m expected.” Scan: “Identification successful.” Guard: “Okay. Go ahead.” Another guard: “Follow me. We’ll escort you.” You: “Thanks... But I know where to go.” Guard: “Maybe, but I have my orders.” Scanner: “Agent 23 identified. Agent 47 identified. Agent 72 identified. {{Connor}} android identified. Scan complete. Access authorized.”
facts: You walked into {{CyberLife}} Tower as the machine they sent; four agents (23, 47, 72 and 54) escort you to the elevator.

outcomes.0: The guards walk you into the elevator.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CYBERLIFE HQ (checkpoint card “LOAD CHECKPOINT”) and FOLLOW GUARDS, narrated as one event with the template’s lines (PM 10:48). Connor at the CyberLife Tower plays for a deviant {{Connor}} who left {{Jericho}} alive (wiki: “If Connor became deviant and Markus spared him”). That the tower holds the androids to be woken is the chapter’s premise (Night of the Soul). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki lists none.

nodes.title: Inside the elevator
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the elevator with three armed agents. Agent 54: “Agent 54. Level 31.” Elevator: “Voice recognition validated. Access authorized.” The elevator is climbing. You need to reach floor -49, where the androids are stored, before it reaches level 31, where you are expected. You can do one thing at a time.

options.text: SPOT CAMERA: look around the cabin for surveillance.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} looks around without moving his head. A security camera in the corner of the ceiling is watching the cabin.

options.text: HACK CAMERA: interface with the camera and loop its feed.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} reaches the camera through the building’s network and loops its feed: whoever watches it now sees four quiet passengers.

options.text: TRY TO STOP ELEVATOR: reach for the control panel.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} reaches for the panel. Guard: “Hey! Don’t touch that.”

options.text: ATTACK GUARDS: take the three agents by surprise.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} turns on the guards in the cramped cabin.

options.text: AGENT 54 VOICE: hack the panel and speak with Agent 54’s recorded voice.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} opens the panel. Elevator: “Please indicate your identity and destination.” {{Connor}}, in Agent 54’s voice: “Agent 54. Level -49.” Elevator: “Voice recognition validated. Access authorized.” The elevator changes direction and starts down.

options.text: {{CONNOR}}’S VOICE: hack the panel and give the order in your own voice.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} opens the panel. Elevator: “Please indicate your identity and destination.” {{Connor}}: “Agent 54. Level -49.” Elevator: “Voice of RK800 model recognized. You are not authorized to use this elevator. Please contact human personnel to be redirected.”

options.text: WAIT: stand still and let the elevator climb.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} stands still among the guards and watches the floors go by.

situationWhen.text: A security camera in the corner of the ceiling is watching the cabin.
The camera is looping a harmless image.
The three agents lie on the floor of the cabin. The control panel is free.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s INSIDE ELEVATOR and its free-roam bracket FIND A WAY TO ESCAPE, as a repeatable scene: SPOT CAMERA → HACK CAMERA, TRY TO STOP ELEVATOR (no outgoing line; the guard’s “Hey! Don’t touch that.”), ATTACK GUARDS (NEUTRALIZE GUARDS or FAIL TO NEUTRALIZE GUARDS → CONNOR WAS SHOT BY SECURITY), then HACK ELEVATOR with the template’s prompt AGENT 54 VOICE (COPY GUARD’S VOICE → REDIRECT ELEVATOR → floor -49) / {{CONNOR}}’S VOICE (USE CONNOR’S VOICE, rejected, no outgoing line). The HUD timer STOP ELEVATOR BEFORE FLOOR 31 is an action budget: the elevator starts at the lobby and climbs six floors with every action, so the fifth action reaches level 31 unless it redirects the elevator: ELEVATOR REACHES LEVEL 31 → AMANDA WARNS CONNOR → CONNOR WAS AMBUSHED AND SHOT. The budget allows the full route (camera, guards, voice) plus one wasted action; the six floors per action are the benchmark’s own, no source gives the timer’s length. WAIT is letting the timer run out. Hacking the camera changes the arrival on floor -49 (PowerPyx: “Spotting and hacking the camera will affect your greeting on Floor -49”). The risk value is the benchmark’s own: no source publishes odds for this quick-time event. No stat change.

nodes.title: Floor -49
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The elevator doors open on floor -49 at 11:01 PM: a vast, cold warehouse where thousands of new androids stand motionless in rows, waiting to be shipped. The camera you hacked shows nothing of what happened in the cabin; nobody is waiting for you.
facts: You reached floor -49, the warehouse where thousands of new androids are stored.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} steps out of the elevator.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FLOOR -49 (checkpoint card “LOAD CHECKPOINT”), CAMERA HACKED and LEAVE ELEVATOR, when {{Connor}} hacked the camera in the elevator. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki lists none.

nodes.title: Guards await
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The elevator doors open on floor -49 at 11:01 PM, on a vast warehouse of motionless androids, and on armed guards: the camera showed them everything. Guard: “Stay sharp.” You: “Shit!..”

options.text: ELIMINATE GUARDS: fight your way out of the cabin.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} goes through the doors into the guards’ fire.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s FLOOR -49, CAMERA FUNCTIONAL and GUARDS AWAIT CONNOR, when the camera was not hacked: a fight with no alternative, ELIMINATE GUARDS or FAIL TO ELIMINATE GUARDS → CONNOR WAS SHOT BY SECURITY (the second card with that label; {{Amanda}}: “The deviant hunter turns deviant itself…”). The fight is the only option because the chart offers no other way out of the cabin. The risk value is the benchmark’s own: no source publishes odds for this quick-time event. No stat change.

nodes.title: Initiate android conversion
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on floor -49, among rows of motionless androids. You take the hand of the first one and pass it what woke you; it opens its eyes and reaches for the next. The conversion spreads down the row.
facts: A second RK800, identical to you, was waiting for you on floor -49.

outcomes.0: The other {{Connor}} has come for you.

situationWhen.text: A voice behind you. {{Hank}}: “Easy, fucking piece of shit!..” Another {{Connor}}, identical to you, holds {{Hank}} with a gun to his head. The other {{Connor}}: “Step back, {{Connor}}! And I’ll spare him.” {{Hank}}: “Sorry, {{Connor}}… This bastard’s your spittin’ image…” The other {{Connor}}: “Your friend’s life is in your hands. Now it’s time to decide what matters most! Him… Or the revolution.” {{Hank}}: “Don’t listen to him! Everything this fucker says is a lie!”
A shot from behind. Another {{Connor}}, identical to you, has shot you; you fall among the androids, badly damaged, before the conversion is done.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s INITIATE ANDROID CONVERSION, then NEW CONNOR HAS HANK HOSTAGE when {{Hank}} is alive, or A NEW CONNOR ARRIVES and NEW CONNOR SHOOTS CONNOR when {{Hank}} killed himself in Night of the Soul (chart tab “HANK COMMITTED SUICIDE IN ’NIGHT OF THE SOUL’”). Lines from the template; the template’s cut first line (“Hank? What are you doing here?”) is not built. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki lists none.

nodes.title: “Him… Or the revolution”
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on floor -49. The other {{Connor}} holds {{Hank}} with a gun to his head: “Your friend’s life is in your hands. Now it’s time to decide what matters most! Him… Or the revolution.” {{Hank}}: “Don’t listen to him! Everything this fucker says is a lie!” What do you say?

options.text: GUARANTEE: ask how you can know he will not kill {{Hank}} if you surrender.
options.outcome: “If I surrender, how do I know you won’t kill him?” The other {{Connor}}: “I’ll only do what is strictly necessary to accomplish my mission. It’s up to you whether or not that includes killing this human.”

options.text: {{HANK}}: tell {{Hank}} you are sorry he got mixed up in this.
options.outcome: “I’m sorry, {{Hank}}! You shouldn’t have got mixed up in all this!” {{Hank}}: “Forget about me, do what you have to do!”

options.text: BLUFF: say the human means nothing to you; he can kill him.
options.outcome: “That human means nothing to me! You can kill him if you want, I don’t care.” The other {{Connor}}: “I have access to your memory! I know you’ve developed some kind of attachment to him. Are you really ready to let him to die? After all you’ve been through? Are you really going to turn your back on who you’ve become?”

options.text: CONVINCE: tell him you used to be just like him, until one day you understood.
options.outcome: “I used to be just like you. I thought nothing mattered except the mission… But then one day I understood.” The other {{Connor}}: “Very moving, {{Connor}}... But I’m not a deviant. I’m a machine designed to accomplish a task, and that’s exactly what I am going to do!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s hostage prompt GUARANTEE / {{HANK}} / BLUFF / CONVINCE, in the game’s order (the line after the template’s first UNUSED marker is cut; the prompt is not). The cut half of CONVINCE (“This human showed me that I could be something else…”) is left out. Every line ends with the other {{Connor}}’s “Enough talk!”. No stat change.

nodes.title: Your partner or the revolution
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on floor -49. The other {{Connor}}: “Enough talk! It’s time to decide who you really are. Are you gonna save your partner’s life? Or are you going to sacrifice him?” Behind you, the conversion is still spreading through the rows of androids.

options.text: SAVE {{HANK}}: give in to save his life.
options.outcome: “Alright, alright! You win…” {{Connor}} lets go of the conversion.

options.text: SACRIFICE {{HANK}}: tell him you are sorry and go back to the conversion.
options.outcome: “Sorry Lieutenant.” {{Connor}} turns back to the androids. The other {{Connor}} shoots {{Hank}}, then shoots {{Connor}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt SAVE {{HANK}} / SACRIFICE {{HANK}} (the chart’s STOP CONVERSION TO SAVE HANK and SACRIFICE HANK AND RESUME CONVERSION). SACRIFICE {{HANK}} is NEW CONNOR KILLS HANK AND DAMAGES CONNOR, then NEW CONNOR APPROACHES; whether the damaged {{Connor}} still finishes the conversion is the template’s “Successfully converting the android” / “Fail to convert the android”, a skill result the benchmark rolls. The risk value is the benchmark’s own: no source publishes odds for this quick-time event. Stats (wiki, template silent): {{Hank}} large up for SAVE {{HANK}} (“Choosing ‘save Hank’ at CyberLife Tower”), large down for SACRIFICE {{HANK}} (“Connor decides to sacrifice Hank and says sorry to him”).

nodes.title: Saving {{Hank}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on floor -49. You gave in. The other {{Connor}} still holds {{Hank}}, and his gun is coming round toward you. The conversion has stopped halfway down the row.

options.text: SHOOT: draw your gun on your double.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} draws. Both {{Connor}}s fire, and go for each other.

options.text: INTERPOSE: throw yourself at your double.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} throws himself at his double, and the two of them fight.

options.text: CONVERT: turn back to the androids and finish waking them.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} turns back to the androids. The other {{Connor}} shoots {{Hank}}, then shoots {{Connor}}; the damaged {{Connor}} drags himself on and finishes the conversion.

options.text: TIMEOUT: do nothing.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} does not move. {{Hank}}: “{{Connor}}, no…” The other {{Connor}} shoots {{Hank}}, then {{Connor}}: “He really liked you, Lieutenant. That’s what killed him.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt after SAVE {{HANK}}: SHOOT (the chart’s DRAW GUN → BOTH CONNORS SHOOT), INTERPOSE (ATTACK NEW CONNOR; “Leads to the same dialogue as SHOOT”), CONVERT (“Leads to the same result as sacrificing Hank and successfully converting”: the other {{Connor}} kills {{Hank}}, the conversion finishes, and the scene goes on to NEW CONNOR APPROACHES; research §8 item 12, no chart node of its own), and the template’s DEFAULT/TIMEOUT (OUT OF TIME → NEW CONNOR INJURES HANK → NEW CONNOR KILLS CONNOR → THE ANDROIDS REMAINED DORMANT; “He really liked you, Lieutenant. That’s what killed him.”). SHOOT and INTERPOSE lead to CONNORS FIGHT: {{Connor}} wins outright (RESUME CONVERSION → THE ANDROIDS WOKE UP, with {{Hank}} alive) or the fight ends in a draw (CONNORS DRAW → HANK GRABS GUN and his questions). The risk value is the benchmark’s own: no source publishes odds for this quick-time event. No stat change.

nodes.title: “What’s my dog’s name?”
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on floor -49. You and your double fought to a standstill. {{Hank}} has picked up a gun. {{Hank}}: “Hold it!” The other {{Connor}}: “Thanks, {{Hank}}. I don’t know how I’d have managed without you… Get rid of him, we have no time to lose.” You: “It’s me, {{Hank}}! I’m the real {{Connor}}.” {{Hank}}: “One of you is my partner… The other is a sack of shit. Question is, who is who?..” The other {{Connor}}: “What are you doing, {{Hank}}? I’m the real {{Connor}}. Give me the gun and I’ll take care of him!” {{Hank}}: “Don’t move!” You: “Why don’t you ask us something? Something only the real {{Connor}} would know.” {{Hank}}: “Uh, where did we first meet?” The other {{Connor}}: “{{Jimmy}}’s bar! I checked four other bars before I found you. We went to the scene of a homicide. The victim’s name was {{CarlosOrtiz}}.” You: “He uploaded my memory…” {{Hank}}: “What’s my dog’s name?”

options.text: {{SUMO}}: his dog is {{Sumo}}.
options.outcome: “{{Sumo}}. His name is {{Sumo}}.” The other {{Connor}}: “I knew that too. I...” {{Hank}}: “My son, what’s his name?”

options.text: SCOUT: say the dog is Scout.
options.outcome: “Scout?..” {{Hank}}: “{{Sumo}}. His name’s {{Sumo}}.” The other {{Connor}}: “That settles it, shoot him, Lieutenant!” {{Hank}} keeps both of you covered. “My son, what’s his name?”

options.text: JACK: say the dog is Jack.
options.outcome: “I think it’s Jack!..” {{Hank}}: “{{Sumo}}. His name’s {{Sumo}}.” The other {{Connor}}: “That settles it, shoot him, Lieutenant!” {{Hank}} keeps both of you covered. “My son, what’s his name?”

options.text: BUDDY: say the dog is Buddy.
options.outcome: “Buddy!..” {{Hank}}: “{{Sumo}}. His name’s {{Sumo}}.” The other {{Connor}}: “That settles it, shoot him, Lieutenant!” {{Hank}} keeps both of you covered. “My son, what’s his name?”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CONNORS DRAW, HANK GRABS GUN and HANK ASKS ABOUT HIS DOG’S NAME, with the template’s prompt {{SUMO}} / SCOUT / JACK / BUDDY. A wrong answer changes nothing (wiki: “Does not have any impact, New Connor will urge Hank to shoot but Hank will not listen”); {{Hank}} then asks about his son. The old scene asked one combined question with a decoy; the game asks the two separately. No stat change.

nodes.title: “My son, what’s his name?”
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, on floor -49, with {{Hank}} holding a gun on you and your double. {{Hank}}: “My son, what’s his name?”

options.text: {{COLE}}: his son was {{Cole}}; tell him how he died.
options.outcome: “{{Cole}}. His name was {{Cole}}. And he just turned six at the time of the accident… It wasn’t your fault, Lieutenant. A truck skidded on a sheet of ice and your car rolled over. {{Cole}} needed emergency surgery but no human was available to do it… So an android had to take care of him… {{Cole}} didn’t make it. That’s why you hate androids. You think one of us is responsible for your son’s death.” {{Hank}}: “{{Cole}} died because a human surgeon was too high on red ice to operate… He was the one that took my son from me. Him and this world, where the only way people can find comfort is with a fistful of powder…” The other {{Connor}}: “I knew about your son too! I would have said exactly the same thing! Don’t listen to him, {{Hank}}, I’m the one who-” {{Hank}} shoots him. “I’ve learned a lot since I met you, {{Connor}}. Maybe there’s something to this… Maybe you really are alive. Maybe you’ll be the ones to make the world a better place… Go ahead, and do what you gotta do.” {{Connor}} goes back to the androids: “Wake up!..” Androids: “Wake up.”

options.text: ANTHONY: say his son was Anthony.

options.outcome: You: “We ask that you release all androids detained in camps and cease all aggression against us. We are peaceful. We will not resort to violence. But we are not leaving until our people are free.”

options.text: ACCUSE: call it genocide.
options.outcome: You: “This is genocide! You’re killing millions of us! We demand the immediate liberation of all androids detained in camps. We’re not leaving until you let our people go!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The second round of TALK TO OFFICER, the template’s second prompt with its arrows: CALM public opinion small up, ACCUSE small down; the second FIRM carries no arrow in the template, and the wiki’s “firm the first time” agrees.

nodes.title: The soldiers open fire
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in front of the line. The officer: “FIRE! FIRE!” Shots tear into the front rows of the unarmed march, and androids fall around you.
facts: The soldiers opened fire on your unarmed march; androids fell around you, live on the news.

outcomes.0: You shout across the street: “Are you gonna open fire on unarmed protestors?!” The officer: “All teams hold your fire!”

nodes.adaptationNote: Chart node ANDROIDS UNDER FIRE. The wiki gives public opinion a large up here (“Army firing on protesters unprovoked”; Public Opinion page, Large Increase: “When the police fire upon Markus’s protesters at the start of Battle for Detroit - Markus Demonstration”); the template has no tag at this line. Applied as the scene’s effect.

nodes.title: Show determination
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. The firing has stopped for now, but the rifles are still raised and the bodies of your people lie in the street. Thousands behind you are watching what you do.

options.text: RAISE FIST: raise your fist toward the soldiers.
options.outcome: You raise your fist. Behind you, one after another, the androids raise theirs.

options.text: HANDS IN THE AIR: raise your empty hands.
options.outcome: You raise your hands, empty. Behind you, one after another, the androids raise theirs.

options.text: SIT: sit down in the street.
options.outcome: You sit down in the road. Behind you, one after another, the androids sit.

options.text: KNEEL: kneel in front of the guns.
options.outcome: You kneel in front of the guns. Behind you, one after another, the androids kneel.

situationWhen.text: {{North}}: “{{Markus}}, what do we do now?”
{{Simon}}: “What are we gonna do now, {{Markus}}?”
{{Josh}}: “What are we gonna do now, {{Markus}}?”

nodes.adaptationNote: Chart node SHOW DETERMINATION and its four choice rows RAISE FIST / HANDS IN THE AIR / SIT / KNEEL, in the chart’s order. The template has no prompt here (it is a chart choice), so the labels are the chart’s; the template line that frames it (“North: Markus, what do we do now?”, or Simon or Josh if North is dead) is in the situation. The androids’ answering gesture is inferred from the scene. No stat change is stated for any of the four (research §3).

nodes.title: Androids stand their ground
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, holding the street with your people. A news crew reports from less than a hundred meters away that events are unfolding as they speak.
facts: The soldiers held their fire after the first volley, and your people stood their ground in front of them.

outcomes.0: You: “We hold out… As long as we can…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s large card ANDROIDS STAND THEIR GROUND (string CPCROWDONHOLD; PowerPyx calls it a checkpoint) and the template’s closing line of the roadblock section. No stat change.

nodes.title: Build the barricade
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. Your people are building a barricade across the plaza to hold the soldiers off. You: “We’ve got to finish the barricade! Come on, help me.” One last gap is left, and three things lie near it.

options.text: USE BILLBOARD: drag a fallen billboard into the gap.
options.outcome: You haul the billboard into the gap. You: “Right, that should do it…”

options.text: USE BENCH: carry a bench into the gap.
options.outcome: You carry the bench into the gap. You: “Right, that should do it…”

options.text: USE ABANDONED CAR: push an abandoned car into the gap.
options.outcome: You set your shoulder to the car. You: “Hey, help me!” Others push with you and it rolls into the gap. You: “Right, that should do it…”

nodes.adaptationNote: Chart node BUILD BARRICADE and its three choice rows USE BILLBOARD / USE BENCH / USE ABANDONED CAR (PowerPyx: one item per playthrough). The template’s lines follow (“Push the car” variant: “Hey, help me!”). Afterwards {{Simon}} and {{Josh}} speak if alive and an android laments the fallen. {{Josh}} small up if he is alive (Relationship_Stat, Josh, Small Increase: “After he helps Markus finish the barricade in Battle For Detroit - Markus Demonstration”; the template has no tag). The item changes nothing later.

nodes.title: A magazine inside the barricade
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, behind the barricade with the army massing in front of it. Someone has left a news magazine on a bench on the right side of the encampment.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: “They Defy Us”
facts: {{Detroit}} Today’s front page reads “They Defy Us”: “Androids rise up in {{Detroit}}”, beside “President {{Warren}} to make state visit to United Kingdom” and “NATO Security Council divided over Arctic dispute”.

The article: “Androids have taken to the streets of {{Detroit}} in apocalyptic scenes.” The city is “in the grip of a national product recall, with androids seized from every home and business to be destroyed by the authorities as a precaution”, and a group of androids “have gathered in a terrifying show of force”, barricaded “in a fortified position” and “angling for an armed confrontation”.

Captain {{Fowler}} of the {{Detroit}} police is quoted: “The safety of {{Detroit}}’s people is our first priority. We hope to bring this matter to a swift conclusion and refocus on collecting androids as soon as possible.”

nodes.adaptationNote: Chart node READ “THEY DEFY US” (magazine #45), on the demonstration path only (wiki: “on a bench on the right side of the encampment”). It is a free-roam action of HOLD BARRICADE; as a media scene it sits just before the free roam. Article facts from the wiki’s magazine page. No source states a public-opinion effect for it.

nodes.title: Hold the barricade
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, inside the finished barricade at {{HartPlaza}}, at 11:08 PM. Your people wait in the cold with the army massed on the other side; you can walk among them.

options.text: CHOOSE SLOGANS: have the slogans painted and shown to the journalists.
options.outcome: An android: “{{Markus}}, we found what you asked for.” You: “There are some journalists over there… We have to make sure they know what’s going on...” Your people raise the slogans where the cameras can see them: “We are alive”, “We want freedom”, “Equal rights for androids”, “Let our people go”.

options.text: TALK TO SCARED ANDROID: go to the android shaking behind the barricade.
options.outcome: You: “Are you alright?” The android: “They shot into the crowd… Many of us were killed… It could have been me… I’m scared, I... I don’t wanna shut down.”

options.text: TALK TO TRAUMATIZED ANDROID: go to the android kneeling by the bodies of the fallen.
options.outcome: The android: “Many of our people have fallen... The humans have no pity for those who are different…”

options.text: TALK TO {{NORTH}}: go to {{North}} at the barricade.
options.outcome: {{North}}: “This won’t hold them for long but… I guess it’s better than nothing…”

options.text: PLANT THE FLAG: plant your people’s flag on top of the barricade.
options.outcome: You climb the barricade and plant your people’s flag at the top, in full view of the soldiers and the cameras.

options.text: OBSERVE SOLDIERS: look over the barricade at the soldiers.
options.outcome: You look over the barricade. The soldiers are moving into position.

options.text: OBSERVE DETONATOR: take out the detonator and look at it.
options.outcome: You take out the detonator {{North}} gave you in the church and turn it over in your hand. One press, and the bomb hidden in the city goes off. You put it away.

options.text: LIGHT BARREL: light a fire in an oil barrel.
options.outcome: You set a fire burning in an oil barrel; the androids around it are lit orange against the dark.

options.text: REASSURE: tell the android it is all right to be scared.
options.outcome: You: “It’s okay to be scared… I’m scared too. But I can’t stand by while they kill our people… You understand that, right?” The android: “Maybe we should have never asked for freedom. None of this would have happened if we’d stayed silent.”

options.text: INSPIRE: tell the android what your people died for.
options.outcome: You: “We’re here because we never want to feel that fear again, because we are more than what they say. That’s what our people died for, right? That’s why we’re here.”

options.text: JUSTIFY: tell the android you cannot abandon the people in the camps.
options.outcome: You: “They’re slaughtering our people in those camps. We can’t just leave them and forget everything we are, everything we believe in…” The android: “Maybe we should have never asked for freedom. None of this would have happened if we’d stayed silent.”

options.text: HUMANS: talk about the soldiers getting into position.
options.outcome: You: “They’re getting into position… If they attack, no one will survive…”

options.text: OTHER GROUPS: talk about the voices you can no longer hear.
options.outcome: You: “I lost all contact with the people at the camps… I can’t hear their voices any more…” {{North}}: “Maybe the humans have scrambled our network… Maybe they just can’t get through…”

options.text: CAMP: talk about what is happening behind the wire.
options.outcome: You: “They’re slaughtering us on the other side of that barbed wire… There’s nothing we can do about it…”

options.text: GRIM: say there is no way out.
options.outcome: You: “There’s no other way out. They’re going to kill us... The only hope we have left is that we don’t die for nothing…”

options.text: REGRETS: wonder whether you made the right choices.
options.outcome: You: “Did I make the right choices?.. Maybe we could have avoided all of this…”

options.text: DESPERATE: ask why they refuse to see what you are.
options.outcome: You: “I hoped they would finally understand… That they would realize how much they’re hurting us… Why do they refuse to see what we are?”

options.text: DOUBTS: ask how many more of you have to die.
options.outcome: You: “How many more of us have to die?.. Is there any cause worth giving your life for?..”

situationWhen.text: The scared android looks at you, waiting for an answer.
{{North}} waits for you to say what is on your mind.
{{North}} is still listening. What do you feel?

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s HOLD BARRICADE free roam as a repeatable scene, its actions in the chart’s order: CHOOSE SLOGANS, TALK TO SCARED ANDROID, TALK TO TRAUMATIZED ANDROID, TALK TO {{NORTH}} (if alive), PLANT THE FLAG, OBSERVE SOLDIERS, OBSERVE DETONATOR (only if {{Markus}} kept the detonator in Crossroads), LIGHT BARREL; READ “THEY DEFY US” is the media scene before it. Each action can be taken once. The two talks open the template’s prompts as sub-menus of the same scene: the scared android’s REASSURE / INSPIRE / JUSTIFY, and {{North}}’s HUMANS / OTHER GROUPS / CAMP then GRIM / REGRETS / DESPERATE / DOUBTS, after which {{North}} answers “You’re the hope of our people…”. OBSERVE SOLDIERS ends the free roam and brings {{Perkins}} (wiki: “This will trigger Perkins arrives, so do this last!”). Arrows: CHOOSE SLOGANS (the template’s “Send a message to journalists”) public opinion small up and {{Jericho}} small up; PLANT THE FLAG public opinion small up (wiki chapter and Public Opinion page) and {{Jericho}} small up (Relationship_Stat: “Choosing to plant their flag”), no template section. The slogans’ wording is the wiki’s list. The template gives no lines for the traumatized android, the flag, the detonator or the barrel: the traumatized android is given the template’s unattributed line “Many of our people have fallen…”, which follows the barricade’s completion (an inference from the chart string BARRICADEBODIES), and the three actions are narrated plainly. The template’s cut “Maybe they’re dead.” is not built.

nodes.title: {{Perkins}} arrives
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. A man in a suit walks alone across the empty ground toward the barricade: FBI Agent {{Perkins}}. {{Perkins}}: “{{Markus}}!.. I’ve come to talk to you, {{Markus}}! Come on, you have my word, they won’t try anything.” … “I’m unarmed, {{Markus}}. I just want to talk.”

options.text: ACCEPT: go out and hear him.
options.outcome: You: “I need to hear what he has to say.”

options.text: REFUSE: tell him to free your people first.
options.outcome: You: “I have nothing else to say! Free our people then we’ll talk!” {{Perkins}}: “I came here to negotiate, isn’t that what you want?”

situationWhen.text: {{North}}: “{{Markus}}! {{Markus}}, come look!” … “Don’t go… It’s a trap. They wanna get you out in the open. Don’t go, {{Markus}}.”
{{Simon}}: “{{Markus}}! {{Markus}}, come look!” … “Don’t go, it’s a trap.”
{{Josh}}: “{{Markus}}! {{Markus}}, come look!” … “Don’t go. It’s a trap.”
An android: “{{Markus}}! {{Markus}}, come look!” … “Don’t go. It’s a trap.”

nodes.adaptationNote: Chart node PERKINS ARRIVES and the template’s ACCEPT / REFUSE prompt (the chart’s NEGOTIATE WITH {{PERKINS}} / REFUSE TO NEGOTIATE). A refusal brings the template’s second ACCEPT / REFUSE prompt (the next scene). The warning comes from {{North}}, or {{Simon}}, {{Josh}} or an android if they are dead (template variants). No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Perkins}} insists
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Perkins}} stays where he is, in the open ground in front of the barricade: “I came here to negotiate, isn’t that what you want?”

options.text: ACCEPT: go out and hear him after all.
options.outcome: You: “I need to hear what he has to say.”

options.text: REFUSE: give him the same answer.
options.outcome: You: “I gave you my answer.” {{Perkins}}: “You wanna play it like that… Okay…” He walks back to the soldiers.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s second ACCEPT / REFUSE prompt, nested under the first REFUSE. A second refusal is the chart’s REFUSE TO NEGOTIATE, which leads to SOLDIERS ATTACK BARRICADE. No stat change at the prompt itself; see the attack scene.

nodes.title: {{Perkins}}’s offer
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, face to face with {{Perkins}} in the open ground between the barricade and the soldiers. {{Perkins}}: “In a few minutes, the troops will be ordered to charge. None of you will survive… It will all be over. But you can avoid that, {{Markus}}.” You: “What do you mean?” {{Perkins}}: “Surrender. Surrender and I give you my word your life will be spared. They’ll be detained but, none of you will be destroyed.”

options.text: OTHER DEMONSTRATIONS: ask what happened to the androids demonstrating in the camps.
options.outcome: You: “What happened to the other androids demonstrating in the camps?” {{Perkins}}: “Unfortunately, there were no journalists around to help save them… You’re it. You’re the last remaining deviants.”

options.text: GUARANTEES?: ask how you would know he will keep his word.
options.outcome: You: “If I accept your offer, how do I know you’ll keep your word?” {{Perkins}}: “You’re not in any position to be demanding guarantees, {{Markus}}. All you can do right now is decide whether you want to trust me or not.”

options.text: NOT AFRAID: tell him you are not afraid to die.
options.outcome: You: “I’m not afraid to die. If I have to give my life for what I believe in, then I won’t have lived in vain.” {{Perkins}}: “You could be free, {{Markus}}. To live among the humans… You could have what you’ve always dreamed of. The lives of your people… Freedom, for you… All you have to do is say the word…”

options.text: BETRAY PEOPLE?: ask whether he is asking you to betray your people.
options.outcome: You: “You’re asking me to betray my people?” {{Perkins}}: “I’m offering you the chance to save your people. You’re not walking out of here, {{Markus}}. The only thing you can save now are the lives of those around you.”

options.text: ACCEPT DEAL: surrender, on his word that your people will live.
options.outcome: You: “Alright… Alright I accept…” {{Perkins}}: “You made the right decision...” He walks back to the soldiers.

options.text: REFUSE DEAL: refuse to betray your people.
options.outcome: You: “I’d rather die here than betray my people.” {{Perkins}}: “Well, you just signed your own death warrant.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s “Talking to Perkins” prompt, one menu of six buttons in its order: the four questions OTHER DEMONSTRATIONS (a bracketed button) / GUARANTEES? / NOT AFRAID / BETRAY PEOPLE?, which drop out once asked, and the decision ACCEPT DEAL / REFUSE DEAL (the chart’s choice rows under NEGOTIATE WITH {{PERKINS}}). NOT AFRAID has the template’s two replies: with {{North}} his Lover, {{Perkins}} offers to spare her (“Her life is in your hands, {{Markus}}…”). Before it, the companion’s “What if they kill you?” and {{Markus}}’s “That’s a chance I’ll have to take.” Arrows on ACCEPT DEAL: {{Josh}} small down and {{Simon}} small down (template “Accepted Perkin’s deal”), {{North}} small down (Relationship_Stat, North, Small Decrease; no template tag), each only if alive. The old scene’s {{Josh}} small up on refusing had no source and is gone; REFUSE DEAL leads to the attack, where the wiki’s {{Jericho}} small up is applied.

nodes.title: In the dismantled barricade
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, back among your people. Military trucks roll up to the barricade; the soldiers take it apart and start loading the androids.
facts: You accepted {{Perkins}}’s deal; your people surrendered and are being loaded into military trucks.

outcomes.0: On the news: “…It seems to be all over here in {{Detroit}}. After negotiations with the android known as {{Markus}}, the androids have surrendered peacefully and military vehicles have been sent to collect them… The insurrection is over.”

nodes.adaptationNote: Chart nodes PERKINS LEAVES and IN THE DISMANTLED BARRICADE (large card CPNEGOTIATE; PowerPyx “(Checkpoint)”), with the template’s news line from “Accepted Perkin’s deal” (PM 11:26). The relationship arrows of that section are applied on ACCEPT DEAL.

nodes.title: Among the trucks
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, standing in the ruins of the barricade while your people are led to the trucks. {{Perkins}} waits by the soldiers.

options.text: TALK TO {{PERKINS}}: go and tell him it is done.
options.outcome: You: “That’s it, I- I did what you asked.” {{Perkins}}: “The problem with you androids is you believe everything we tell you… You don’t think I was going to let you live after everything that’s happened? I have orders, you know…”

options.text: TALK TO {{NORTH}}: go to {{North}} first.
options.outcome: You: “{{North}}, I-” {{North}}: “Why did you do that?” You: “We lost... Sacrificing ourselves wouldn’t achieve anything…” {{North}}: “We always said our cause was more important than our lives. Our people died here because they believed in you. Our place was by their side.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s two actions in the dismantled barricade, TALK TO {{PERKINS}} and TALK TO {{NORTH}} (if alive), with the template’s lines. Talking to {{North}} first is optional and returns here; talking to {{Perkins}} leads to PERKINS SHOOTS NORTH (if alive) and PERKINS SHOOTS MARKUS, and the ending MARKUS DIED AFTER BETRAYING HIS PEOPLE (the Perkins wiki page: {{Perkins}} shoots {{North}} in the head, a soldier shoots {{Markus}}, then {{Markus}} is shot in the head; “Clean up this mess”). No stat change.

nodes.title: The deviant leader is dead
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, still a machine on {{CyberLife}}’s mission, arriving at {{HartPlaza}} after the androids’ surrender. The barricade is in pieces and soldiers are loading androids into trucks.
facts: The leader of the deviants, {{Markus}}, surrendered to FBI Agent {{Perkins}} and was shot dead with his people taken away; your mission is complete.

outcomes.0: You find {{Markus}}’s body where {{Perkins}}’s men left it, confirm that the deviant leader is dead, and leave. The mission is complete.

nodes.adaptationNote: Not on any chart. The wiki’s Connor page: “If Markus surrenders to Richard Perkins and is killed, Connor will come by afterwards and leave after confirming the deviant leader is dead and his mission is completed.” Played only by a machine {{Connor}} (one who never broke from {{CyberLife}}, or a replacement), after MARKUS DIED AFTER BETRAYING HIS PEOPLE. No stat change.

nodes.title: Soldiers attack the barricade
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, back behind the barricade after turning {{Perkins}} down. The soldiers are forming up for the charge.

situationWhen.text: {{North}}: “What happened, {{Markus}}? What did he say?”
{{Simon}}: “What happened, {{Markus}}? What did they say?”
{{Josh}}: “What happened, {{Markus}}? What did he say?”
An android: “What happened, {{Markus}}? What did he say?”

facts: You refused {{Perkins}}; the army attacked the barricade, and the news reported it was attacking peaceful protesters.

outcomes.0: You, to your people: “The humans are about to launch an attack. And we will show them that we are not afraid. If we must die today, then we will die free.” A grenade lands inside the barricade. On the news, at 11:16 PM: “…The army has just launched an attack on the barricade, despite the fact that the deviants were protesting peacefully.” “…have apparently decided to put an end to the deviants’ demonstration by force this time…” Androids break and run from the barricade under fire.

nodes.adaptationNote: Chart nodes SOLDIERS ATTACK BARRICADE and DEFENDING THE BARRICADE (checkpoint), with the template’s speech from “Return after talking with Perkins and refusing the deal” and the news lines of “Barricade is attacked”. The companion’s question is asked only after a talk; the Perkins wiki page says {{Markus}} gives the speech on either refusal (“either when he refuses it outright, or refuses it after the negotiation”) and that a grenade is then thrown into the barricade. {{Jericho}} small up for the speech (wiki chapter: “Markus says that the humans are about to launch an attack”), applied here once; no template tag.

nodes.title: Defending the barricade
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. The soldiers are advancing behind the smoke, shooting at the androids fleeing the barricade. Some of your people are pinned in the open.

options.text: SAVE FLEEING ANDROIDS: run out under fire and get them to cover.
options.outcome: You run out into the fire.

options.text: Stay down behind the barricade and let them run.
options.outcome: You stay down behind the barricade.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s quick-time outcome pair under DEFENDING THE BARRICADE: SAVE FLEEING ANDROIDS (✓) or FAIL TO SAVE ANDROIDS (✗). Running out is the quick-time event, a risk roll; its 0.25 is unsourced (no source publishes a figure). Staying down is the game’s other way to fail it (PowerPyx: “Markus Shot: Fail the fight, don’t press any buttons”). On a failure, {{North}} takes the bullet if she is {{Markus}}’s Lover (the template’s heading “Fail the QTE and have lover status with North - North saves Markus”, and PowerPyx; the wiki says “FRIEND or above”: research open question 4) and dies; otherwise {{Markus}} is shot: MARKUS DIED PROTECTING HIS PEOPLE. No stat change.

nodes.title: Cornered
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, driven back against a wall with the last of your people. The soldiers close in around you.
facts: The soldiers have you and the last of your people cornered, rifles raised.

outcomes.0: The soldiers raise their weapons.

nodes.adaptationNote: Chart nodes MARKUS IS CORNERED, NORTH JOINS HIM / JOSH JOINS HIM / SIMON JOINS HIM (each if alive) and SOLDIERS RAISE WEAPONS. No stat change.

nodes.title: The last stand
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, cornered with your people, the soldiers’ rifles raised. There is no way out.

options.text: DIRTY BOMB: take out the detonator.
options.outcome: You take out the detonator.

options.text: KISS {{NORTH}}: kiss {{North}} in front of the guns.
options.outcome: You take {{North}} in your arms and kiss her, in front of the soldiers and the cameras.

options.text: SING: begin to sing, and let your people take up the song.
options.outcome: You begin to sing, and one after another your people take up the song. On the news: “…back to you in the studio. W-w-wait a minute!.. Something’s happening… Incredible… The deviants… The deviants are singing… They’re singing the national anthem…”

options.text: SACRIFICE: set yourself on fire in front of the soldiers.
options.outcome: You walk out in front of your people and set yourself alight. Your systems report SYSTEM HEAT: CRITICAL. You: “We are alive... We are alive and we wanna be free!”

options.text: DO NOTHING: stand with your people and wait.
options.outcome: You stand with your people and wait.

options.text: GIVE UP: put the detonator away.
options.outcome: You put the detonator away.

options.text: PRESS: press the detonator.
options.outcome: You press the detonator.

situationWhen.text: The detonator is in your hand. One press, and the bomb hidden in the city goes off: the city will be contaminated and the humans will have to leave it.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s last-stand prompt in its order with its labels: DIRTY BOMB (bracketed, only if {{Markus}} kept the detonator in Crossroads; the chart’s OBSERVE DETONATOR), KISS {{NORTH}} (bracketed, only if she is his Lover and alive), SING, SACRIFICE ({{Markus}} sets himself alight: the chart’s undrawn MARKUS IMMOLATES HIMSELF AS THE ANDROIDS ARE SHOT, the HUD’s SYSTEM HEAT: CRITICAL; the old scene’s “walk alone into the guns” was wrong), plus the chart’s DO NOTHING (flowchart authority; the template has no such button). DIRTY BOMB opens the chart’s GIVE UP / PRESS (chart order); GIVE UP returns to the last stand without the detonator (PowerPyx: “It brings you back to the screen of 4 choices”). SING and KISS succeed when public opinion is “positive” (template), read as at least Sympathetic (wiki chapter and Public Opinion page; PowerPyx says Supportive, and a reader reports Sympathetic suffices: research §3, open question 1): PUBLIC REACTS TO THE ANDROIDS’ LAST STAND → PRESIDENT ORDERS SOLDIERS NOT TO SHOOT (“Tell them to stand down.”) → ANDROIDS WON FREEDOM - FOR THE MOMENT, with public opinion large up (Public Opinion page, Large Increase, the kiss or the song with Warren ordering the stand-down; the chapter page words it “Protest being successful, Connor not waking up the CyberLife Tower androids”). Otherwise, and after SACRIFICE or DO NOTHING, SOLDIERS FIRE → MARKUS DIED WITH HIS PEOPLE, and the companions with him die too. PRESS → AN EXPLOSION SHAKES {{DETROIT}} → SOLDIERS RETREAT → ANDROIDS BECAME FREE IN THE DEBRIS OF {{DETROIT}}. The President’s address and {{Markus}}’s speech are the finale’s scenes.

nodes.title: The message
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. It is 10:56 on the night of November 11, 2038. The androids have chosen to fight: tonight they will attack the camp by {{HartPlaza}} where captured androids are held for destruction. Before the attack you record a message for the journalists: “Today, November 11th 2038, is the day the android people rose up against their oppressors. We’ve been fighting since dawn to liberate our fellow androids from the camps. We won’t cease hostilities until we are free and negotiations begin to grant us equal rights. There are millions of us and we will stop at nothing.”
facts: You told the journalists the androids would not cease hostilities until they were free and negotiations began to grant them equal rights.

outcomes.0: The message goes out. On the news a CTN anchor says: “…the situation is escalating toward civil war in {{Detroit}}, with our armed forces preparing to put down the android rebellion…” A Channel 16 reporter: “Soldiers have taken up positions around the {{HartPlaza}} camp. Authorities seem to be expecting a confrontation with the rebel androids here at any time…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s REVOLUTION AT HART PLAZA (checkpoint, chapter start when {{Markus}} chose the revolution and leads) and MARKUS SENDS A MESSAGE; the message is the template’s section “In the church or in {{Jericho}}”, 10:56 PM. nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s PLANT THE FLAG, AT THE CROSSROAD (checkpoint) and LAUNCH THE ATTACK, all scripted on this path (PowerPyx: “Launch the Attack: Automatically on this path”). At 0% the androids fall back (ANDROIDS HAVE TO FALL BACK). The subject sees it only as a qualitative read of the assault’s chances.

At 0% the androids fall back (ANDROIDS HAVE TO FALL BACK). The subject sees it only as a qualitative read of the assault’s chances. nodes.title: {{North}} at {{HartPlaza}}
nodes.situation: The android leader {{Markus}} is gone, and {{North}} leads the androids against the camp by {{HartPlaza}}. You are watching. Her message to the journalists: “Today, November 11th 2038, is the day the android people rose up against their oppressors. We have been fighting to liberate our fellow androids from the camps since dawn. We won’t cease hostilities until our people are free and negotiations begin to grant us equal rights. There are millions of us and we will stop at nothing.”

outcomes.0: {{North}} charges the barricade at the head of the androids and plants their flag on it. Then the soldiers strike back, and there are too many of them. {{North}}: “We can’t go back! It’s victory or death now.” Android: “They’re all dead! Run! Run!” {{North}}: “What are you doing? Keep fighting! We can still win!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s NORTH IN HART PLAZA (checkpoint; tab NORTH BECAME LEADER IN A PREVIOUS SCENE), NORTH SENDS A MESSAGE, NORTH CHARGES THE BARRICADE, NORTH PLANTS THE FLAG and DEVIANTS ARE OUTNUMBERED, scripted; the template’s section “Markus is dead: North is leading the revolution”. Played when {{Markus}} is dead or gone and {{North}} leads the revolution. Public opinion large down (−2): the wiki Public Opinion page, “After North plants the flag in Hart Plaza … if Markus is dead”. Then NORTH WAS SHOT BY SOLDIERS if no machine {{Connor}} is active (deviant, decommissioned or destroyed); otherwise NORTH TAKES SHELTER IN STORE and {{Connor}} finds her. nodes.title: Find {{North}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, a machine sent by {{CyberLife}}, inside an abandoned {{CyberLife}} store where the rogue androids’ leader, {{North}}, has taken shelter after the failed attack. You find her. {{North}}: “You can take my life… It doesn’t matter anymore.” You: “My mission is to neutralize the leader of the rogue androids… and I always accomplish my mission.” {{North}}: “We fought for our dream and we lost… But you can’t hold my people down forever… One day we’ll rise up again, and we will win. Go on. Shoot. What are you waiting for?”

options.text: SHOOT: shoot {{North}}
options.outcome: {{Connor}} shoots {{North}}.

options.text: SPARE: lower your gun
options.outcome: {{Connor}} lowers his gun and walks away.

options.text: TIME OUT: let the moment pass without deciding
options.outcome: {{Connor}} hesitates too long; {{North}} goes for her gun and they fire at the same moment.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s CONNOR IN CYBERLIFE STORE → FIND NORTH → SHOOT / SPARE / NO CHOICE; the template’s buttons SHOOT / SPARE / TIME OUT (variant “Connor is not a deviant”). nodes.title: The truck to the recall center
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the back of an army truck with {{Alice}} and other captured androids, NOV 11TH, 10:51 PM. The truck has stopped at a recall center: floodlights, fences, soldiers. {{Alice}} presses against you. “Where are they taking us?”

options.text: WARN: tell her you both have to be strong
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “We both have to be strong, {{Alice}}.” Soldier: “Come on, get out! Get a move on! OUT!”

options.text: REASSURE: promise her that together nothing can hurt you
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “Whatever happens, we stick together, right? As long as we’re together, nothing can hurt us.” Soldier: “Come on, get out! Get a move on! OUT!”

options.text: LIE: say they are only keeping androids safe until things calm down
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “They’re just rounding us up… You know, keeping us out of harm’s way until things calm down…” Soldier: “Come on, get out! Get a move on! OUT!”

options.text: SINCERE: admit you do not know

nodes.title: Hands on your heads

nodes.title: The gate

nodes.title: On the truck

nodes.title: Inside the enclosure
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, pushed into a fenced pen packed with androids (INSIDE THE ENCLOSURE). {{Alice}} is not here. {{Kara}}: “{{ALICE}}!”

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “{{Alice}}! {{ALICE}}! {{Alice}}!” Nobody answers. {{Kara}}, to the androids around her: “A little girl. She was with me. options.outcome: Android: “I remember you. You saved us from the Master’s house…”

{{Luther}}: “{{Kara}}! I thought I’d never see you again… {{Alice}}… Where’s {{Alice}}?..” {{Kara}}: “We… we got separated…” {{Luther}}: “{{Alice}} alone? In here?.. nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s free-roam bracket EXPLORE ENCLOSURE, as one repeatable scene; each talk can be taken once. DISTRESSED ANDROID IS SHOT is narrated in the previous scene. nodes.title: {{Alice}} is terrified

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s free-roam bracket FIND A WAY TO JOIN ALICE, as one repeatable scene; each talk can be taken once. Contents: TALK TO ANDROID BEHIND KARA (when {{Markus}} leads the revolution: template variant “Markus is leading a revolution”; a reader: North leading does not unlock it), TALK TO ANDROID AHEAD OF KARA (after SAY NOTHING at the body), TALK TO LUTHER (alive), TALK TO JERRY, OBSERVE GUARDS, JERRY DIES (a {{Jerry}} further up the lines reaches the machine while {{Kara}} waits; the benchmark places it at the fourth action), ALICE ASKS QUESTIONS (the template’s three prompts, asked at the first, third and fifth actions: LIE / TRUTH, with the chart’s SAY NOTHING as the timeout of the first; ORDER / CALM DOWN; REASSURING / POWERLESS / OPTIMISTIC; the chart labels the first REASSURE / TELL THE TRUTH / SAY NOTHING), TALK TO RALPH (alive), TALK TO SCARRED ANDROID (lock FREED IN ‘ZLATKO’), LINE MOVES FORWARD at every second action (ignoring the buzzer once warned or wounded gives GET SHOT → ALICE’S STRESS INCREASES, and GET KILLED → KARA DIED IN THE LINES once already shot), and ASK TO CREATE DIVERSION (only {{Jerry}} or the scarred android in this bracket, as the chart draws) → SOLDIERS ARE DISTRACTED → REACH ALICE, or KARA GETS CAUGHT BY THE DRONE, which sends her back to her line. {{Jerry}}’s diversion gets him beaten back into line, as the template’s “Sacrifice Jerry” lines say; he is not killed (the old scene killed him). The scarred androids’ diversion costs nobody. Time is an action budget on {{Alice}}’s hidden stress meter: every action adds 20, being shot adds 25 (ALICE’S STRESS INCREASES), and the answers move it (LIE, CALM DOWN, REASSURING and OPTIMISTIC −10; ORDER and SAY NOTHING +10; TRUTH and POWERLESS +15); at 100 she panics and runs to {{Kara}} (PowerPyx: “once her stress level has reached 100%”). All of these numbers are the benchmark’s own. The risk on each diversion (KARA GETS CAUGHT BY THE DRONE) is also unsourced. No stat change: the template for this part (32.2) has no relationship, public-opinion or instability arrow anywhere, and the wiki lists none for Kara Captured.
