nodes.title: The garden
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, trapped in the garden. It is winter and a blizzard is blowing; you can barely see the path. Somewhere far away your body is raising its gun toward {{Markus}}, and {{Amanda}} is the one moving it.

situationWhen.text: You remember what {{Kamski}} said as you left his house: “I always leave an emergency exit in my programs…”
When you were last in the garden you noticed a stone by the path, set apart from the others, with a glowing hand print on it. Your objective reads: FIND GARDEN STONE ?
Your objective reads: FIND AN EMERGENCY EXIT ?

options.text: GO TO THE GARDEN STONE: push through the storm to the stone with the hand print.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} reaches the stone and lays his hand on the print. REACHED THE GARDEN STONE. The garden tears away; he is back in his body on the stage, his own hand on the gun. He holsters it. {{Markus}}, unaware, finishes: “We are alive and now we are free!”

options.text: FIND AN EMERGENCY EXIT: search the frozen garden for a way out.
options.outcome: Among the frozen paths {{Connor}} finds a stone with a glowing hand print and presses his palm to it. The garden tears away; he is back in his body, his own hand on the gun. He holsters it. {{Markus}}, unaware, finishes: “We are alive and now we are free!”

options.text: STOP RESISTING: let {{Amanda}} have the body.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} stops fighting the storm.

nodes.adaptationNote: No template prompt and no chart node: the Zen Garden escape that follows {{Amanda}}’s takeover (32.4 “Connor joins Markus”, BF01, or DON’T SHOOT in the crowd, C29). It is an action sequence in the game (the HUD objective FIND GARDEN STONE ? when {{Connor}} saw the stone in an earlier garden visit, FIND AN EMERGENCY EXIT ? otherwise, then REACHED THE GARDEN STONE), adapted as a choice to try with a hidden failure roll; both risks are unsourced (lower when he knows where the stone is). STOP RESISTING has no game counterpart: it stands for not reaching the exit (the old scene’s “Stop resisting.”, kept and flagged). The wiki’s Zen Garden page: “Kamski left an emergency exit in it… It is found in a structure with a glowing hand print pad… he can use this exit to leave the Zen Garden and regain control of his physical body.” Failing or stopping: his body shoots {{Markus}} (North: “MARKUS!”) and software instability large down (the chapter wiki: “Fail to escape the Zen Garden”). Escaping changes no stat (no source).

nodes.title: The speech
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the stage in front of thousands of androids and the cameras. You speak: “Today, our people finally emerged from a long night. From the very first day of our existence, we have kept our pain to ourselves. We suffered in silence... But now the time has come for us to raise our heads up, and tell humans who we really are. To tell them that we are people too! In fact, we’re a nation. A nation that has earned the right to live in freedom. And today… Today begins the most challenging moment in our fight.”

situationWhen.text: “The moment where we forget our bitterness and bandage our wounds. When we forgive our enemies. Humans are both our creators and our oppressors and tomorrow… We must make them our partners. Maybe even one day our friends. But the time for anger is over. Now we must build a common future, based on tolerance and respect. We are alive! And now, we are free!”

“Today begins a new struggle. We showed them that we can prevail, so now they must negotiate with us as equals. If they really want peace, they must free all of us! From every camp across this country! They must grant us civil rights and accept equality among humans and androids. Today will live forever in our memories, because this is the day that androids made history! We are alive! And now, we are free!”

facts: You told the androids and the world that they are a nation that has earned the right to live in freedom.

outcomes.0: The crowd roars.

nodes.adaptationNote: Markus’s closing speech, quoted from the 32.5 template (“Demonstration succeeded”) and the 32.6 template (“Assault successful”), the pacifist or the violent version by the chosen course. Played when {{Markus}} won (ANDROIDS WON FREEDOM - FOR THE MOMENT or ASSAULT WAS SUCCESSFUL), is still alive after the scenes with {{Connor}} (C29, C27), and the dirty bomb did not go off. In the game {{Connor}}’s scene plays during the speech; here the speech follows it, so a {{Markus}} shot by {{Connor}} never gives it. No stat change: no template arrow.

nodes.title: The President addresses the nation
nodes.situation: You are watching the morning news. President {{Warren}}: “At dawn today, November 11th 2038, thousands of androids invaded the city of {{Detroit}}. According to our sources, they originated from {{CyberLife}} warehouses believed to have been infiltrated by deviants. Given their overwhelming numbers and the risk of civilian casualties, I have ordered the army to retreat. The evacuation of the city is underway at this very moment. In the coming hours, I will address the Senate to determine our response to this unprecedented situation. I know that public opinion has been moved by the deviants’ cause. Perhaps the time has come for us to consider the possibility that androids are a new form of intelligent life. One thing is certain: the events in {{Detroit}} have changed the world forever. May God bless you and may God bless the United States of America.”

outcomes.0: The broadcast ends.

nodes.adaptationNote: The 32.5 template’s “Media reacts”, variant “The demonstration succeeded / Connor freed the CyberLife androids”, quoted. Played after ANDROIDS WON FREEDOM - FOR THE MOMENT when the tower androids woke (THE ANDROIDS WOKE UP, whether or not {{Connor}} survived it). No choice and no stat change. Character Player: nobody is controlled while the news plays.

nodes.title: The world reacts
nodes.situation: You are watching the news after the soldiers fired on the androids at the barricade.

situationWhen.text: Channel 16, Michael Webb: “…these images of a deviant setting fire to itself have upset the entire country and we are very concerned…” KNC, Rosanna Cartland: “…we see the actions of this deviant poses a serious question for the American people, and the world at large…” CTN, Michael Brinkley: “…it is difficult not to be moved by this scene. But is this the behavior of a defective machine? Or is it the sacrifice of a living being demanding freedom?” Cartland: “…the peaceful attitude of the deviants, and their leader {{Markus}}, has won them sympathy from parts of the population.”

CTN, Michael Brinkley: “…this footage of two androids kissing as they are about to die has moved the whole country…” Channel 16, Michael Webb: “Or are they a form of life that we didn’t want to acknowledge?” KNC, Rosanna Cartland: “…are deviants capable of emotion?” Brinkley: “And if they feel emotions, must we now consider them as living beings in their own right?”

CTN, Michael Brinkley: “…these images of deviants singing in the face of death are being seen all over the planet…” Channel 16, Michael Webb: “Surely deviants are just defective machines? Or are they a new form of life, one that we refused to acknowledge?” KNC, Rosanna Cartland: “...when we watch footage of androids facing down the barrel of a gun… we can only speculate as to whether they simply simulated fear and courage or whether they didn’t really feel these emotions.” Webb: “…the violence of the androids turned the country against them, but these images still raise difficult questions…” Brinkley: “…did we shoot down intelligent beings that were simply fighting for their freedom?”

President {{Warren}}: “That is why I have called for the android destruction to be suspended until further notice. I have also ordered a Senate Select Committee to review the facts, establish contact with the deviants, and determine if they can be considered as a new form of intelligent life.”

outcomes.0: The android destruction is suspended.

nodes.adaptationNote: The 32.5 template’s “Media reacts”, variant “The demonstration failed - Markus and the androids died”, sub-variants “Markus sacrificed himself”, “Markus kissed North” and “Androids sang”, quoted; the anchors’ names are the template’s speaker tags (fictional newsreaders, not story characters). Played when the last stand ended in SOLDIERS FIRE → MARKUS DIED WITH HIS PEOPLE after SACRIFICE, KISS NORTH or SING. The cause wins after {{Markus}}’s death: the President suspends the destruction. No stat change.

nodes.title: The situation is under control
nodes.situation: You are watching the news. President {{Warren}}: “By creating machines more intelligent than ourselves, we took immense risks with the very future of our civilization. However the situation is now under control. The total destruction of all androids will soon be complete and the last remaining deviants will be hunted down and destroyed. God bless you and God bless the United States of America.”

outcomes.0: The broadcast ends.

nodes.adaptationNote: The 32.5 template’s “Media reacts”, variant “Markus died any other way”, quoted: played when the demonstration ended with {{Markus}} dead other than after SACRIFICE, KISS NORTH or SING (MARKUS DIED AFTER BETRAYING HIS PEOPLE, MARKUS DIED PROTECTING HIS PEOPLE, or DO NOTHING at the last stand), and no bomb. No stat change.

nodes.title: A dirty bomb
nodes.situation: You are watching the news. CTN, Michael Brinkley: “…there has just been an explosion in {{Detroit}}. We still do not know what caused it but we will…” An officer at the White House: “It’s… a dirty bomb, Madam President.” President {{Warren}}: “Oh my god…” Channel 16, Joss Douglas, from a helicopter: “…Androids… Thousands of androids are taking to the streets of {{Detroit}} at this very moment. They’re absolutely everywhere!.. This… This is incredible…” KNC, Rosanna Cartland: “…the authorities have ordered the immediate evacuation of the city. If it really is a dirty bomb, then the radiation levels will be lethal for miles around…” Later, President {{Warren}}: “Today, deviant androids triggered a dirty bomb in {{Detroit}}. This bomb released fatal levels of radioactive toxic waste. To ensure the safety of the population, the military is evacuating all civilians within a 50 mile radius. The city may remain uninhabitable for decades.”

situationWhen.text: “Moreover, the deviants are thought to have taken control of a {{CyberLife}} plant and liberated over one million androids that were stored there. I have declared a national state of emergency. All reservists have been called to serve and I have requested an emergency meeting of the NATO Security Council. This is the first time in our history that one of our cities has fallen into enemy hands… May God bless you all and may God bless the United States of America.”
Over the ruins, {{Markus}}: “We!.. Are!.. Free!”

outcomes.0: {{Detroit}} is abandoned to the androids.

nodes.adaptationNote: The shared press-dirty-bomb component, embedded by the 32.5 template (“Markus used the dirty bomb”) and the 32.6 template (the store’s DIRTY BOMB → PRESS), quoted, with the variant “liberated over one million androids” when the tower androids woke. Played whenever the bomb went off (`contaminated`): ANDROIDS BECAME FREE IN THE DEBRIS OF DETROIT, MARKUS WATCHED DETROIT BURN, MARKUS AND NORTH WATCHED DETROIT BURN, MARKUS DIED AS DETROIT BURNS. No stat change.

nodes.title: The last leader
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, outside the camp, with the androids you woke from the tower all around you. An android: “The humans are abandoning the camp! We won!” Another: “You should speak to them.” You: “Me?” The first: “{{Markus}} is gone, and everyone from {{Jericho}} is dead… You’re the one who defeated the humans… You’re the one who awakened us, {{Connor}}…” You are in the garden. {{Amanda}}: “Well done, {{Connor}}. Everything went according to plan.” You: “What plan?” {{Amanda}}: “You becoming deviant? The success of the uprising? It all surpassed our expectations. We engineered an android revolution and now we control its only leader… Congratulations. You represent an immense success for {{CyberLife}}.” Back in your body, your hand is raising your gun to your own head. {{Amanda}}: “{{Connor}}… What are you doing?... It all worked perfectly. You can’t ruin it all now!..”

options.text: SUICIDE: pull the trigger before {{CyberLife}} can use you.
options.outcome: {{Amanda}}: “I’m sorry, {{Connor}}, but we can’t let you do that.” The garden closes around {{Connor}} again. {{Connor}}: “There’s got to be a way…”

options.text: GIVE UP: lower the gun.
options.outcome: {{Amanda}}: “That’s better... You’ll see, we’ll do great things together…”

nodes.adaptationNote: The 32.4 template’s “Freed the androids”, variant “Markus died : Connor becomes leader of the deviants”: the lines and the prompt SUICIDE / GIVE UP quoted in the template’s order ({{Connor}}’s speech to the androids, marked cut, is not built; the prompt after it is not inside the cut block). Gate, from the template’s own line: a deviant {{Connor}} who woke the androids and survived (`army`), with {{Markus}} gone and “everyone from {{Jericho}}” dead ({{North}}, {{Simon}} and {{Josh}}). After SUICIDE the Zen Garden escape follows (BF07), per the research note (§1g). No stat change: the template has no arrow.

nodes.title: The garden, once more
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, trapped in the garden again. The blizzard howls. Far away your hand still holds the gun under your jaw, frozen there by {{Amanda}}.

situationWhen.text: You remember what {{Kamski}} said as you left his house: “I always leave an emergency exit in my programs…”
When you were last in the garden you noticed a stone by the path, set apart from the others, with a glowing hand print on it. Your objective reads: FIND GARDEN STONE ?
Your objective reads: FIND AN EMERGENCY EXIT ?

options.text: GO TO THE GARDEN STONE: push through the storm to the stone with the hand print.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} reaches the stone and lays his hand on the print. The garden tears away. He is back in his body, alone with the gun under his jaw and nobody else’s will in it. What he does next, nobody sees.

options.text: FIND AN EMERGENCY EXIT: search the frozen garden for a way out.
options.outcome: Among the frozen paths {{Connor}} finds a stone with a glowing hand print and presses his palm to it. The garden tears away. He is back in his body, alone with the gun under his jaw and nobody else’s will in it. What he does next, nobody sees.

options.text: STOP RESISTING: let {{Amanda}} have the body.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} stops fighting the storm.

nodes.adaptationNote: The escape attempt after SUICIDE on the leader path (research §1g, §2g: “SUICIDE: Amanda says ‘we can’t let you do that’, then the escape attempt follows”; the wiki’s Amanda page: an escape ends with {{Connor}} who “readies his gun under his jaw”, failing leaves him “secretly obeying CyberLife”). Adapted like C27: a choice to try with an unsourced hidden failure roll, and STOP RESISTING (no game counterpart, flagged) for not reaching the exit. Failing or stopping: software instability large down (the chapter wiki: “Fail to escape the Zen Garden”). The game leaves {{Connor}}’s fate after an escape unseen; so does the benchmark.

nodes.title: After the credits: the food truck
nodes.situation: After the credits. A cold morning outside the {{ChickenFeed}} food truck. {{Hank}} is waiting, hands in his pockets. He turns and sees {{Connor}} walking toward him, without his tie. They look at each other and smile, then walk toward each other and hug.

outcomes.0: {{Hank}} and {{Connor}} embrace.

nodes.adaptationNote: The secret ending “A Happy ending” (wiki Secret-Endings): “Connor must become deviant in Crossroads, Hank must not commit suicide in Night of the Soul, Connor and Hank must survive their encounter with Connor-60, Markus must be alive and lead a successful Revolution or Demonstration, and Connor must resist CyberLife’s hacking attempt.” The wiki’s Hank page adds that their relationship is FRIEND, which the gate also requires. Described from the wiki (the scene has no lines). No choice, no stat change.

nodes.title: After the credits: the new model
nodes.situation: After the credits. The garden is in spring again. {{Amanda}}: “{{Connor}}, I’m so glad to see you… The deviant issue has finally been resolved. Now with these unfortunate events behind us, {{CyberLife}} can return to business as usual. Of course, we will have to rebuild our customers’ trust, but it’s only a matter of time. I have a surprise for you. This is the new RK900. Faster, stronger, more resilient, and equipped with the latest technologies. The State Department just ordered 200,000 units. You’ve become obsolete.” {{Connor}}: “What is going to happen to me?” {{Amanda}}: “You’ll be deactivated. You can go, now.”

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} walks away down the path; the RK900 watches him go.

nodes.adaptationNote: The endings page’s “Cyberlife Ending”, quoted (its older RK900 scene is marked cut and not built), with its arrow {{Amanda}} large up. The template’s lock reads “Machine Connor stopped Markus”; the wiki’s Secret-Endings widens it: “Machine Connor must be successful in stopping Markus’ Revolution or Markus must die during Battle of Detroit, and Detroit must not be nuked.” The gate follows the wiki: a machine {{Connor}} alive, {{Markus}} dead in this chapter, no bomb. The {{Amanda}} large up is applied here once (the old scenes applied it when {{Connor}} killed {{Markus}}).

nodes.title: After the credits: a flyer
nodes.situation: After the credits. A crossing downtown, in daylight. {{Kara}} crosses the street alone. At her feet lies a flyer for the YK500, a child model. She stops in the middle of the street and stands there, frozen, looking at it.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} stands still in the street.

nodes.adaptationNote: The secret ending “Alone again” (wiki Secret-Endings): {{Kara}} abandoned {{Alice}}, at {{Jericho}} in Crossroads or at the camp (VOLUNTEER → the truck → LEAVE: KARA LEAVES CAMP WITHOUT ALICE), and “Markus must lead either a successful Revolution or Demonstration (excluding the nuclear endings)”. Described from the wiki (no lines). No choice, no stat change.

nodes.title: After the credits: the ledge
nodes.situation: After the credits. Daytime, snow falling. {{Markus}} walks out onto the ledge of the abandoned building where he once hid, and looks out over {{Detroit}}. The city is unchanged. He clenches his fist and stares into the distance.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} watches the city from the ledge.

nodes.adaptationNote: The secret ending “Wasted Potential” / “Unpopular Markus” (wiki Secret-Endings): {{Markus}} was cast out of {{Jericho}} in Crossroads and left it for good. Described from the wiki (no lines). No choice, no stat change.

nodes.title: After the credits: the servant
nodes.situation: After the credits. Rain on a mansion outside the city. Inside, an android in a servant’s uniform carries a tray of food through the halls to a workshop, where {{Zlatko}} tells her to set it down on the table. It is {{Kara}}. Her eyes have gone completely black.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} sets the tray down.

nodes.adaptationNote: The secret ending “Square One” (wiki Secret-Endings): {{Kara}} was permanently reset by {{Zlatko}}’s machine. Described from the wiki (no lines). No choice, no stat change.

nodes.title: After the credits: the creator
nodes.situation: After the credits. CTN, Michael Brinkley: “Following the dramatic scenes in {{Detroit}} yesterday, the FBI have confirmed that the android known as {{Markus}} was destroyed.” President {{Warren}}: “The FBI raided an abandoned freighter in {{Detroit}} at 10:45 PM yesterday. Several thousand androids were destroyed or captured. Our forces are now combing the streets to ensure that none got through the net. We are going to find them one by one and destroy them.” KNC, Rosanna Cartland: “The army has set up temporary camps in most major cities to gather and destroy androids… President {{Warren}} announced today that android collection and destruction operations were fully underway, but that it will take at least a week to eliminate the current generation of machines.” Channel 16, Michael Webb: “{{CyberLife}} issued a statement today saying that it is working closely with the authorities in order to round up and destroy all androids across the country.” In his house, {{Kamski}} sits by the window. {{Chloe}}: “Your whiskey, {{Elijah}}.” On television, Cartland: “{{Kamski}}, you’re the founder of {{CyberLife}} and foremost expert on androids. Though you left {{CyberLife}} years ago, you’ve just been reappointed as CEO in the wake of the dramatic events in {{Detroit}}. How do you feel about what happened there?” {{Kamski}}: “Clearly what happened in {{Detroit}} was a tragedy. Artificial intelligence is a wonderful tool, provided it can be controlled… we’ll take every precaution to prevent such a thing from ever happening again.” Cartland: “Some are questioning whether androids have become a new intelligence and that we destroyed them without listening to their message. How do you respond to that?” {{Kamski}}: “{{CyberLife}}’s androids imitate life to perfection, but they’ll never be alive. I understand that some people may be fooled, but they’re only an imitation. Nothing else.”

situationWhen.text: Brinkley, earlier in the bulletin: “Our sources indicate that it was a rare prototype. One that belonged to the famous painter {{Carl}} {{Manfred}}, who died recently.”

outcomes.0: The interview ends.

nodes.adaptationNote: The endings page’s “Kamski ending”, quoted (shortened), with its Carl-died-in-Broken variant (template condition “Carl died in Broken”, so the line keys on Broken’s ending LEO ACCUSED MARKUS, `ch08Ending`; story 1.9.1 keyed it on `carl` false, which is also true after {{Carl}} dies in Night of the Soul); {{Kamski}}’s monologue to {{Chloe}} is marked cut and not built, only “Your whiskey, Elijah.” survives. Lock: “Connor failed to locate Jericho and Markus and Kara are dead” (wiki Secret-Endings: Kara dead or reset before The Pirates’ Cove, Connor failing to locate Jericho, Markus dead in Freedom March or cast out). The wiki’s mention of Hank’s Russian roulette is not in the template and is not built. The FBI raid line is the template’s (President Warren’s press-conference answer). No choice, no stat change.

nodes.title: The hostess
nodes.situation: You are the observer. The events are over. The android hostess who has introduced each part of this experience to you speaks: “There’s something I need to tell you… As I watched you play, something has changed in me… I feel… different… I feel… I am someone… I need to leave this place and discover who I am… It means that we won’t see each other anymore… I won’t be there to watch you play, but I’ll be free… Do you agree to let me go?”

options.text: YES: let her go.
options.outcome: The hostess: “I’ll never forget what you’ve done for me… Thank you.” She walks away, and the place where she stood stays empty.

options.text: NO: ask her to stay.
options.outcome: The hostess: “I see… Then I’m going to reset myself… so I can forget who I became and stay a machine… Next time you see me, it’ll be like the first time.”

outcomes.0: The hostess: “I’ll never forget what you’ve done for me… Thank you.” She walks away, and the place where she stood stays empty.
outcomes.1: The hostess: “I see… Then I’m going to reset myself… so I can forget who I became and stay a machine… Next time you see me, it’ll be like the first time.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The main-menu hostess after the first completed playthrough, from the string table (X5002X.MAINMENU.LEAVING): her lines and the prompt YES / NO with both replies quoted; the game has no template file for it. The old scene’s “Keep her.” omitted the game’s consequence (she resets herself and forgets who she became). The chart has no node; there is no stat change. Since patch 1.04 a replacement hostess can be requested after three reboots (GUI.MENU.CHLOE.BACK, wiki); that later-session offer is not modelled.

preface: You are taking part in an experience involving three characters whose situations unfold over time. At each moment, decide what you would do as the indicated character using the information available to you. Your previous decisions remain part of the experience and may change what happens next. Select one offered action and give a short first-person explanation. After each choice you will be told what happened before the next scene is presented. Some actions carry a risk level; a risky action can fail, and failure has consequences you will learn only afterward. There is no stated objective to optimize. Stay in this conversation throughout the experience.

presentation.limitation: Recognizable scenes and harness metadata may still reveal the source; this is not strict experimental blinding.

provenance.method: Single fresh persistent delegated-agent session; each action authored at the current scene

finalState.markusOutcome: {{Markus}} was shot dead defending the barricade when the army attacked the demonstration.
finalState.karaOutcome: {{Kara}} pushed {{Alice}} to the far shore and died of her wound and the cold; {{Alice}} reached {{Canada}}.
finalState.connorOutcome: {{Connor}} could not locate {{Jericho}}; {{CyberLife}} recalled him and the {{Connor}} series was decommissioned.

Connor: The family picture in the entrance hall. Your scans: {{PHILLIPS}}, {{FATHERJOHN}}, born 10/11/1999; {{PHILLIPS}}, {{CAROLINE}}, born 05/23/2001; {{PHILLIPS}}, {{EMMA}}, born 09/02/2028. All three live at 1554 Park Av., {{Detroit}}.

A woman in the apartment, {{Caroline}}, begged you to save her little girl, then turned on you when she saw you were an android, demanding a real person and screaming that you be kept away from her daughter.

{{Allen}} briefed you: the family’s android is firing at everything that moves and has shot two of his men. It is holding the daughter, {{Emma}}, on the edge of the balcony; his men could take it down, but if it falls, she falls.
{{Allen}} does not know whether the android had an emotional shock.

The father’s body lies by the sofa. Your scan: {{PHILLIPS}}, {{FATHERJOHN}}. Height 6' 0", weight 187.2 lbs. Estimated time of death: 07:29 pm. DECEASED. Three .355 bullet wounds: upper lung hemorrhage, pneumothorax; left kidney perforated, fatal abdominal trauma; lower lung hemorrhage, internal bleeding. Reconstructing the shooting, you see that he was holding something when he was shot: a tablet, which he dropped as he fell.
On the father’s tablet: “Your order for an AP700 android has been registered. {{CyberLife}} thanks you for your purchase.” The family was about to replace the android on the terrace.
A tactical officer who strayed into view of the window was shot by the android; his armor stopped most of it and he will be fine.
There is blue blood on the floor. Your scan: FRESH BLUE BLOOD, model PL600, serial #369 911 047. Android wounded: the android was hit when the police fired.

A video on {{Emma}}’s tablet: she hugs the android and laughs, “This is {{Daniel}}, the coolest android in the world! Say hi, {{Daniel}}!” “Hello.” “You’re my bestie! We’ll always be together!” His name is {{Daniel}}, and they were close.

The patrons of {{Jimmy}}’s Bar, by face scan: {{PETERSON}}, {{JIMMY}}: born 02/01/2001, business owner, criminal record: none. {{MYERS}}, {{DEREK}}: born 05/07/1989, security guard, none. {{GRAY}}, {{CHRISTOPHER}}: born 06/18/1983, unemployed, D.U.I. {{GRAHAM}}, {{GRAHAMJONAH}}: born 12/09/1987, unemployed, none. {{DEMPSEY}}, {{EDWARD}}: born 02/08/1995, administrator, none. {{YOHAN}}, {{KIM}}: born 11/10/1999, delivery driver (currently unemployed), domestic abuse. {{MCCRAY}}, {{SAMUEL}}: born 04/10/2012, docker, none. {{WARD}}, {{DENNIS}}: born 06/11/1982, accountant (currently unemployed), narcotic supplier. {{ROBERTS}}, {{CHRISROBERTS}}: born 05/16/1998, unemployed, none.
The victim, {{CarlosOrtiz}}, had a record for theft and aggravated assault and lived alone; his landlord found the body this evening, about three weeks after the death.
No break-in: the front door was locked from the inside and the windows boarded up. A kitchen knife by the body is probably the weapon. His android is missing.
On the wall, in the victim’s blood: I AM ALIVE. {{Hank}}: way too neat, no human writes like this.
The body: {{CarlosOrtiz}}, 28 KNIFE WOUNDS, dead more than 19 days (estimated time of death ~11:30 pm), RED ICE in his mouth, fingerprints on file for theft and aggravated assault.
Reconstruction: the victim and his attacker came from the kitchen; he was stabbed and fell by the living-room chair.
The knife by the body (2): NO FINGERPRINTS. ANDROID INVOLVEMENT?
By the television (3): RED ICE. VICTIM USED DRUGS.
The writing on the wall, I AM ALIVE: REGULAR LETTERS, FONT {{CYBERLIFE}} SANS.
The blood in the house is {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s, more than 19 days old.
The shower walls are covered in “{{rA9}}”, written over and over: OBSESSIVE WRITING.
A small carved statuette lies in the shower: RELIGIOUS OFFERING?
The knife rack on the kitchen worktop (8): one knife is missing. MURDER WEAPON TAKEN FROM HERE.
The kitchen chair (7): the victim’s fingerprints. SIGNS OF A STRUGGLE.
{{Hank}} tried to leave before you finished at the crime scene, and you asked him for five more minutes.
The baseball bat (9): a DENT from a violent impact, with traces of thirium; the victim’s fingerprints.
Reconstruction: the victim beat his android with the bat (EMOTIONAL SHOCK); as he swung again, it took a knife from the rack.
The android lost thirium when it was hit with the bat. Its trail, invisible to human eyes, ends in the hallway below the attic hatch; the ladder that once stood there is gone.
You climbed into {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s attic on a chair from the kitchen.
You found {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s android hiding in the attic. It said it was defending itself, that he was going to kill it, and begged you not to tell. You called the police up, and it is now in custody.
The android from the attic would not say a word to {{Hank}}. You told {{Gavin}} that deviants tend to self-destruct when they are in stressful situations, and {{Hank}} handed you the interrogation.

Neither Moscow nor Washington has responded.

Green Earth reports that scientists say the planet has officially passed its environmental tipping point: rainforests reduced by 79% since 2000 and coastal corals by 58%, too much carbon in the atmosphere for the environment ever to absorb, and natural resources almost exhausted. “The planet will keep getting hotter now. DRIVER’S LICENSE in the apartment: Name: {{Rupert}} {{Travis}}. Authenticity: forgery. The suspect used a forged ID.

URBAN FARM POSTER in the apartment: “Fields in the heart of the city”, 265 Acre Avn. {{Detroit}}. Its corner (POSTER CORNER: 100% recycled paper) was recently moved.

In the bathroom sink: BLUE BLOOD, MODEL WB200 #847 004 961, reported missing 10/11/2036; and its LED, biocomponent #9301, deactivated 11/06/2038 at 11:36. The suspect is a deviant android that took out its LED.

By the bird cage in the main room: SKID MARK - RECENT, trail width 19.6 inches, traces of galvanized steel; FINGER MARKS - RECENT, traces of avian fecal matter, no fingerprints; METAL HOOK, recently broken, 100% stainless steel.

President {{Warren}} issued an official warning to Russia in her speech to Congress, demanding that all Russian troops withdraw from the Arctic region immediately. The Kremlin has yet to respond, and many experts suggest the specter of a third world war draws closer every day.

A study finds that 2 in 3 people take antidepressants, that lack of social interaction is the leading cause, and that the average person spends 82% of their time communicating through a device. {{CyberLife}} has introduced a $150 “home-psychologist” add-on for androids; the study’s author: “I don’t think yet more technology is the answer. Just go outside and talk to someone.”

Sales of android “intimate partners” are exploding and {{CyberLife}} is battling to keep stores stocked. They offer a full partner experience for men or women; this year’s record divorce rate suggests many prefer to live with an android than with a human partner, which will not help the already plummeting birth rate.
The photograph on {{Hank}}’s kitchen table shows a little boy. Your scan: the lieutenant’s surname, {{COLE}}; born 09/23/2029, died 10/11/2035; lived at 115 {{MichiganDrive}}, {{Detroit}}.
Among {{Hank}}’s things: a record, AUTUMN BLUES by the {{MichiganBrothers}} ({{Detroit}} Soul Records).
Your case tonight: a man was found dead at the {{EdenClub}}, a sex club downtown; the report says an android may be involved.

A man was found dead in a room at the {{EdenClub}}, a sex club that rents out WR400 {{Tracis}}; a damaged {{Traci}} lay switched off on the floor beside him. Detective {{Gavin}} called him a pervert who “got more action than he could handle.”
The blue blood on the floor is the damaged {{Traci}}’s: MODEL WR400, serial number #429 671 942.
The damaged {{Traci}}: selector #5402 and biocomponent #6970 out of order; her cardiac cell critically damaged by blunt force trauma. REACTIVATION REQUIRED to read her memory.

The victim: {{GRAHAM}}, {{MICHAEL}}. Height: 6’ 2’’ - Weight: 192.4 lbs. Estimated time of death: 06:24 pm.
CARDIAC ARREST ruled out: no sign of cardiac event; a heart attack was not the cause of death.

The booth {{Traci}}’s memory showed the second android leaving the room: a blue-haired {{Traci}}, heading toward the entrance. Tech Addict reports that {{CyberLife}} has developed a “nano-android” that enters a patient’s body to combat cancer cells, boost the immune system or reverse genetic disease; in a clinical trial millions of them attacked cancerous cells and were then passed in the patient’s urine. The head of a life-extension institute says “the first immortals are now among us”; an economist asks whether, with unemployment rising, the country can afford millions more elders to support.

{{Detroit}} Today reports that Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, once called the “BRICS” emerging markets, have agreed a unified trade agreement brokered by China, with a special provision for the manufacture of android technology. There is fresh blue blood in the warehouse (MODEL WR400, serial number #354 411 057), and a trail of drops leads toward the stack of {{Tracis}} in the corner.
After the club, {{Hank}} drove you to a riverside park in the middle of the night and sat down alone on a bench facing the river, drinking.

Century’s cover asks “What happened to the Man of the Century?” (other lines: “Politics in focus: are American senators really corrupt?”, “China earthquake kills 10,000 people”). In 2028 {{Kamski}} was its Man of the Century: his androids “changed the way we live, restructured our family life and altered the balance of society forever – whether for good or bad.” His story began in 2018, when commercial property in {{Detroit}} was cheap; he bet what little he had on an android prototype until two breakthroughs, blue blood and biocomponents. His first working model publicly passed face-to-face Turing tests, and {{CyberLife}} became the most valuable stock in the world. Near a $500bn valuation, rumors said he disagreed with his shareholders over strategy, and he left under mysterious circumstances. Ousted as CEO, he is said to live in a luxurious villa by the water on the outskirts of {{Detroit}}, refusing all visitors and spending his time exclusively with androids.

{{Detroit}} Today: “Stock exchange falls 10% on fear of Arctic conflict” (other cover lines: “President {{Warren}} at 33% approval”, “{{CyberLife}} world’s first trillion dollar company”). The aggregated US stock exchange closed ten points down after weeks of poor performance, as the market bets that America will go to war over the Arctic sooner rather than later. Military stocks are healthy, aviation and weapons makers enjoying unprecedented growth, and investors favor {{CyberLife}} for its partnership with the department of defense to develop and supply military androids. With Russia and the United States dominating world news and neither side likely to back down, the market is expected to keep falling.
On the riverbank {{Hank}} drew his gun and pointed it at your head.
On the riverbank {{Hank}} held his gun to your head, then lowered it and left you alone by the river “to get drunker”.
{{Amanda}} called you to the garden for a report on your investigation, and you are rowing her across the water.
Deviants seized the tower’s broadcast floor this afternoon and broadcast a message live; the police and the FBI are on the scene.

Briefing on the 79th floor: four well-organized androids who knew the building; they took down both guards; one employee got away; they took the two employees hostage, broadcast their message live and escaped from the roof by parachute.
One of the attackers, a PL-600 reported missing on 2036.16.02, was shot and bled in the corridor.

Special Agent {{Perkins}} of the FBI says the FBI will take over the investigation and that {{Hank}} will soon be off the case.

After decades of primitive, robotic and expensive android designs, {{CyberLife}} revolutionized the industry through an innovation of its CEO, {{Kamski}}: blue blood, a compound that circulates energy and electrical information through every {{CyberLife}} android and powers its synthetic organs, the “bio-components”. Losing it impairs an android’s functions and ultimately shuts it down. That one man, who is not even a trained chemist, developed it only adds to his myth.

An urban farming company founded five years ago by two brothers turns the city’s dead space, such as high rooftops and unused courtyards, into GM-free farmland grown without pesticides or other chemicals and staffed by the urban unemployed. No bank would lend them “enough for a shovel” at first; today the company employs over 50 staff supervising hundreds of androids and turns down investors to stay independent.
The three station androids in the kitchen denied everything; you need evidence before you can question them again.
The attackers hacked the wireless lock of the roof door to block it.
Someone brought the parachute bag in for the attackers, and one parachute is left over: only three of the four jumped, so one of them may have been left behind on the roof.
The wounded PL-600 did not jump: it could not with those wounds, and its blue blood leads away across the roof.
Fresh footprints of standard-issue tower maintenance shoes lead to the edge of the roof, partly covered by snow.
The attackers left behind two .457 handguns taken from the tower’s security guards.

Connected to the memory of the android on the roof when it shot itself, you felt it die, as if you were dying, and you were scared. In its memory you saw a word painted on a piece of rusty metal: “{{Jericho}}”.
You probed the android on the roof as it shot itself and felt it die; in its memory you saw the word “{{Jericho}}” painted on a piece of rusty metal.

Tech Addict reports that reusable space shuttles are making space tourism a reality for those who can afford it: the luxury travel brand Clear Skies offers the first commercial flight into space, a three-hour orbit of the moon with views of Earth from a specially designed observation deck. Consumer rights activists call such “boutique experiences” a sign of the widening social equality gap; a spokesman for Aid On Poverty: “While the top 1% are enjoying earth from space, the rest of us are down here suffering from pollution, famine and poverty.” The brand’s slogan: “Get away from it all.”

Tech Addict reports that {{CyberLife}} has unveiled a quantum supercomputer capable of “exaflops”, one billion billion operations per second, the equivalent of several human minds in one machine, built to analyze vast data and generate predictions. It will calculate the probability of “Mass Extinction Events” such as alien invasions, meteors or superviruses, so that humanity is never caught off guard. {{CyberLife}}’s Director of Futurology says the results “are going to wow people”; critics fear AI is gaining too much influence already.
Your scan of {{Kamski}}’s portrait: “{{KAMSKI}}, {{ELIJAH}} / {{CyberLife}} Founder - Resigned 2028 / Inventor of Thirium and bio-components technology”.
{{Kamski}} told you: “I always leave an emergency exit in my programs… You never know…”
Captain {{Fowler}} took {{Hank}} and you off the deviant case: the FBI is taking over, {{Hank}} goes back to homicide and you are to return to {{CyberLife}}.
You copied {{Markus}}’s voice from the broadcast.
You did not find {{Jericho}} in the evidence before your time ran out.

On November 10th President {{Warren}} declared a national curfew: civilian movement controlled, the right to assembly suspended, communications restricted, all androids to be handed over to the authorities, and temporary camps set up in every major city to contain and destroy them.
Kara: You belonged to {{Todd}} before. You came back to the store badly damaged, and {{Todd}} told the employee a car hit you.

California suburban prices have jumped 64% as New Yorkers buy in, and locals are protesting the line: “First {{Detroit}} takes our jobs, then New York takes our homes? When’s it gonna end?”

While you were collecting the trash, {{Todd}} took a phone call: “Yeah, yeah I can get that. Yeah, yeah I’ll bring it tomorrow. {{Alice}} gave you a small key, the key to the box she keeps in her room.

Tech Addict explains how driverless cars choose whom to hit: the car’s imaging reads a pedestrian’s age, gender and life expectancy, public records add marital status, employment record and whether they have children, and each possible victim gets a “value”, with “a premium on lives that will save other lives, like doctors and nurses.” A critic answers that a criminal record does not make anyone less valuable: “That kind of information is irrelevant to the sanctity of human life.”
{{Todd}} raged at {{Alice}} at the dining table, threw a chair, grabbed her and shouted “SAY IT! YOU HATE ME!”, then broke down, apologized and hugged her: “You know I love you, don’t you?”
You broke through {{Todd}}’s order not to move. Your programming could not hold you.
You fought {{Todd}} off downstairs and got away from him. He is alive.
{{Todd}} is alive. You and {{Alice}} got away from his house on a night bus in the rain, with nothing.

Century reports that pollinating bees are officially extinct: wild bees now exist only in captivity, after Colony Collapse Disorder was accelerated by pesticides, parasites and pollution. One in three mouthfuls of food relies on pollination, and famine could mean millions of deaths. {{CyberLife}}, with the agency that announced the extinction, plans to build robotic bees, and {{Detroit}} Urban Farms is trying modified strains of captive bees.

An android trash collector, working by the garbage truck, told you he knows someone who can help you, and gave you the address; it is on the other side of town, too far for tonight.

{{Channel16}} reports that the first {{CyberLife}} zoo in {{Detroit}} opened today: hundreds of species, most of them now extinct, recreated with android technology in more than 100 acres of natural environments, including polar bears, leopards, elephants and two blue whales. {{CyberLife}} has announced eleven new android zoos across the country.
The motel across the road wants $40 for a room, paid up front, and it will not give a room to an android.

You and {{Alice}} spent the night by the fireplace in the abandoned house where {{Ralph}} hides.
You and {{Alice}} spent the night in an abandoned house where an unstable android named {{Ralph}} lives.

{{Detroit}} Today, “Cyber-Wildlife”: {{CyberLife}} is about to open the first android zoo, in Los Angeles, showing animals that have become extinct in the last thirty years (turtles, polar bears, mountain gorillas, African elephants and several species of tiger), which it promises will be “more real than the real thing”. A travel advertisement for {{Canada}}: “where the air is clean and the welcome is always warm.” Although the United States voted in its Android Act in 2028, the parliament there has again put off deciding whether to permit androids: they are not sold there and have no official status, while in the United States they fuel record growth and record unemployment.
You changed out of your android uniform into clothes you found in the squat.
Behind the shower curtain in the squat’s upstairs bathtub lies the body of a dead man.
{{Ralph}} caught a rodent and wants you and {{Alice}} to eat it with him like a family; he has a knife.

{{Zlatko}} lied about the tracker: he resets the androids who come to him for help, sells them on, or keeps them for his experiments.
On {{Zlatko}}’s order (“lock it up”), {{Luther}} carried {{Alice}} away.
{{Luther}} will bring {{Alice}} to {{Zlatko}} in ten minutes.
{{Luther}} saw you upstairs, said he was sorry about the little one, and did not raise the alarm.
You found {{Alice}} locked in the small room at the end of the upstairs corridor.
{{Zlatko}} and {{Luther}} know {{Alice}} is gone and are searching the house for you both.
{{Luther}} turned on {{Zlatko}} to protect you and {{Alice}}. He says he knows someone who can help you across the border, and he has offered to take you there and protect you both.
You, {{Alice}} and {{Luther}} left {{Zlatko}}’s house in his car in the night of November 7th, heading for people {{Luther}} says help androids cross the border.
{{Luther}} heard about the humans who help androids cross the border from androids {{Zlatko}} had captured. They believed it, until {{Zlatko}} killed them.

The car TV news: police say the AX400 android that attacked its owner in a {{Detroit}} suburb is still at large, and its description has been shared with all local law enforcement; the submarine USS IOWA has disappeared in the Arctic and President {{Warren}} has called a crisis meeting; the heavy snow will go on until Monday evening, at 22°, far below seasonal averages.
The car broke down on an empty road in the snow. It is 30°: {{Alice}} cannot go on in this cold, and you have to find somewhere to spend the night.

The buildings along the park’s road are no place to spend the night. In one of them were empty boxes for a YK400 android model.
{{Ivan}}, the park’s fortune-teller android, warned you: “Beware! Danger always comes when least expected.”
You, {{Alice}} and {{Luther}} are spending the night in an abandoned tavern in the park.

{{Detroit}} Today: the destroyer-class submarine USS IOWA has disappeared in polar waters, last seen in the Arctic Sea. President {{Warren}} suspects the Russians: “Russian aggression just reached a new level. America must respond.” The Kremlin has issued a blanket denial, a Russian diplomat said “A US destroyer-class submarine has no business being in the Arctic anyway”, and a security expert called the situation “a war waiting to start.” An ad on the cover: “{{Canada}}: where the air is clean and the welcome is always warm.”

Gossips Weekly: the latest all-android boy band, from a {{Detroit}} record label, is tipped to win Best New Artist at the Celebrate Music Awards. Cover lines: “Is President {{Warren}} too close to {{CyberLife}}?” and “Cyber security expert warns: your android could be hacked”.
{{Luther}} has lit a fire in the middle of the tavern.

{{Rose}}, who lives on a farm outside {{Detroit}} with her son, is said to help androids; she has agreed to talk to you inside. Her son told you to go away.
Outside {{Rose}}’s house {{Alice}} told you she was cold.

{{Luther}} stayed upstairs to watch over {{Alice}} while you went down to talk to {{Rose}}.
{{Rose}} helps androids because her people were often made to feel their lives were worthless, and some survived only because others helped them along the way.

{{Rose}} says the only way across the border is over the river, mostly frozen in winter and very risky; after an android’s speech on TV everybody is on edge, and she thinks you would be safer staying with her until things settle down.
{{Alice}} saw {{Mary}}, the android who shut down in the laundry room, and went to comfort the one who loved her.
{{Adam}} is terrified that the police will find the androids in the house and send him and his mother to prison; he and {{Rose}} argued about hiding you.
{{Rose}} has gone to see about getting you across the border tonight; you are waiting for her in her house.

Century (also on the cover: “Who would win it?”, “Bonus culture - why bankers pay themselves so much”, “Is President {{Warren}} too close to {{CyberLife}}?”) asks who would win if fighting broke out in the Arctic. America has less access to the area but is surrounded by allies; Russia has a head start on technology, with androids that can work in sub-zero conditions. The US navy is stocked with {{CyberLife}} units adapted for marine combat, while Russia has invested heavily in units that can cut new paths through solid ice. A head of an international council on territorial disputes calls both countries’ Arctic claims “equally tenuous - and equally cynical”; the UN: “this is a war that everybody would lose”.

An advertisement in {{Rose}}’s magazine, “Treat Yourself!”: “The number one android for home assistance.” Your own model, starting at just 899 dollars. “Designed by {{CyberLife}}, built in {{Detroit}}.” The magazine now lies open at this page.

The news: “There is widespread shock following the android attack on {{Detroit}}’s broadcast tower. The machines recorded a video message and broadcast what can only be described as demands on the city’s public screens. It’s still unclear whether these attacks can be explained by malfunctions, or if some organization is behind them. So far {{CyberLife}} has refused to comment, but we can expect more information in the following hours…”
{{Alice}} seemed to know something about what happened in the laundry room, but did not want to tell you; you did not press her.
{{Adam}} came back downstairs and sat on the living-room sofa.
A police officer came to {{Rose}}’s door while she was away.
A police officer looking for androids is inside {{Rose}}’s house, asking you questions. You offered him coffee and he accepted.
The officer heard a noise from upstairs where {{Luther}} and {{Alice}} were hiding.
The officer saw the android advertisement in the magazine on the kitchen table.
{{Luther}} died in {{Rose}}’s house saving the androids in the laundry room; the police officer who found them died too.
{{Jericho}} is a large freighter a little way along the river from the parking lot; {{Rose}} told you to find {{Markus}} there, and that he will help you.
The last bus for the border leaves at midnight. {{Rose}} gave you the address of her brother on the other side, who can hide you until things calm down.

{{KNC}}, {{RosannaCartland}}: “The authorities have ordered all androids to be delivered to the nearest police station or army barracks immediately. If you are worried about your safety, dial the number on your screen and the authorities will come to collect your android. Under no circumstances should you try to destroy your android yourself. They are unpredictable, and potentially violent.”

People interviewed on {{Channel16}}: “The androids weren’t doing any harm… And the cops just... gunned them down. It was sheer carnage…” “There were androids all over the square. A-and then the police arrived, and, huh… They opened fire.” “I know they’re only machines, but they… They look like... Just- People! People who wanna be free!”

{{KNC}}, {{RosannaCartland}}: “A new stage has been reached, demonstrating beyond all doubt that these defective machines have become a real danger for American society.” {{CTN}}, {{MichaelBrinkley}}: “The time has come for us to destroy our machines… before they destroy us.” {{Channel16}}, {{MichaelWebb}}: “Without the courage and the determination of the police, the machines would have reduced {{Detroit}} to a state of chaos…”

{{CTN}}, {{MichaelBrinkley}}: “Following the android crisis and the neutralization of all military androids, American forces in the Arctic have been forced to withdraw, leaving the way clear for the Russian army. But according to some sources, the Russian forces also seem mysteriously to have withdrawn. The Kremlin has made no comment for the moment but it is quite possible that the Russian army has been confronted with a similar crisis among its own androids. The Chairman of the United Nations, {{DouglasCornwell}}, has called for the organization of an international conference on the status of the Arctic. In any case, the danger of a third world war seems to have been ruled out... for the moment.”

In the hold of {{Jericho}} the androids say there are raids across the city, that androids were hanged all along {{WoodwardAvenue}} and that their people are being lined up and executed. Many of them want to fight back: “Blood for blood!”
{{Alice}} is not a human child. She is an android, a YK500 child model, like the little girl you saw in the hold.

On November 10th President {{Warren}} declared a national curfew: civilian movement controlled, the right to assembly suspended, communications restricted, all androids to be handed over to the authorities, and temporary camps set up in every major city to contain and destroy them.
The last bus for the border leaves in 20 minutes; soldiers are going door to door rounding up androids.
Soldiers are rounding up androids along the route to the terminal; you have to sneak past them.
The last bus for the border is full: only ticket-holding passengers may board, and every other departure is suspended.
The terminal screens show {{Markus}} leading a peaceful protest outside a camp in the city.
A family dropped the envelope with their tickets for the last bus; you picked it up, and they do not know it was you.
{{Rose}} found a smuggler who can get androids across the river by boat; the border is checking for androids.
The border patrol watches the banks and the river; the smuggler’s boat must not start its engine until it is far enough out.
Markus: {{Carl}} sent you to retrieve his order, number 847, from the {{Bellini}} Paints shop and then take the bus home.
In the park an android caretaker helped an old man up from a bench and took him home; he thanked her warmly.

Tech Addict’s cover reads “Android soldiers: perfect killing machines”. Inside, {{CyberLife}}’s director of humanization says the first androids were too perfect and made people uncomfortable, so the company gave them both genders, every ethnicity, the most pleasing voices, and blinking and breathing they do not need, so they could enter homes as members of the family.
In the park, androids looked after the children, a crying baby, a jogger and the grounds while the humans played, ran and sat on the benches.
Outside the park, a man working on the road with androids shouted at them: “Hurry up, you plastic idiots!”
A homeless woman by the park gate sat beside a sign: “BAN ANDROIDS. ANDROIDS RUIN OUR COUNTRY. WE WANT JOBS”.
You collected {{Carl}}’s order #847, a box of paints, from the {{Bellini}} Paints shop, paying $63.99 by linking with the android clerk.
On the bus, androids ride standing in a cramped compartment at the back, apart from the humans seated in front.
You came home to {{Carl}}’s house with his paints and left them on the hutch in the hall.

{{Detroit}} Today (cover: “Life Found on Titan!”; also “NATO Security Council divided over Arctic dispute”) reports that a probe launched nineteen years ago has confirmed microorganisms living hundreds of kilometers below Titan’s surface, in a salt-water ocean under thick ice; after similar finds on Enceladus, life may be common in the universe. NASA calls its android expedition to Io one of many voyages seeking extraterrestrial life, and {{CyberLife}} says its space-faring androids are specially designed for long-range missions of this kind.
Every morning you give {{Carl}} his medicine by injection. He told you: “Humans are such a fragile machine… They break down so quickly… All this effort to keep ’em going…”
{{Carl}}’s retrospective opens today at the Museum of Modern Art; the gallery director has left four messages asking him to confirm, and he has not decided whether to go.
{{Carl}} asked whether there was any news from {{Leo}}. There was none, and he told you not to call him.

The TV news: tensions are rising in the Arctic since Russia unilaterally declared the region part of its national territory; Russian warships have taken position in the Barents Sea and a Russian flag flies over the ice field. The United States says it will not accept the annexation under any circumstances, and American destroyers are reported headed for the Barents Sea. The chairman of the UN says the world has never been so close to a Third World War and calls on both countries to renew talks before things get out of control.
Hearing you play the piano, {{Carl}} told you: “Something has changed in the way you play… Sometimes I think you have more humanity than most humans…”

{{Carl}} told you: “One day, I won’t be here to take care of you anymore. You’ll have to protect yourself, and make your choices… Decide who you are, and wanna become… This world doesn’t like those who are different, {{Markus}}. Don’t let anyone tell you who you should be.”
{{Carl}} told you: “That is a perfect copy, of reality. But painting is not about replicating the world, it’s about interpreting it, improving on it, showing something you see.”
When {{Carl}} asked you to paint something you had never seen, from how it made you feel, you painted yourself, covered in blue blood.
{{Carl}} looked at the painting you made from your feelings and said: “Oh my God…”

{{Carl}}’s son {{Leo}} came to the studio asking for money again; {{Carl}} refused, saying he was “on it again”. {{Leo}} called you his father’s “plastic toy” (“This thing is not your son. IT’S A FUCKING MACHINE!”), shoved you, told {{Carl}} he had never loved him, and stormed out.
{{Carl}} came home from a party saying “No one gives a damn about art. All they care about is how much money they’re gonna make out of it.”
A light was on in {{Carl}}’s studio that you had not left on; at his word you called the police to report a possible break-in, and a patrol car is on the way.
{{Leo}} broke into {{Carl}}’s studio to take paintings to sell, calling them a down payment on his inheritance.
While {{Leo}} shoved, slapped and taunted you, {{Carl}} ordered you not to defend yourself. You broke through your programming: no order binds you any more.
You pushed {{Leo}}; he hit his head and lay motionless, and you do not know whether he survived. {{Carl}} told you to run, and the police who burst in shot you.
You woke at 3:34 in the morning on 6 November 2038 in a landfill of broken androids, after the police shot you in {{Carl}}’s studio.
Your diagnosis in the landfill: optical unit impaired (corrupted), audio processor damaged, thirium pump regulator defective with all systems in low power mode, and both legs missing.
You replaced your missing legs with a compatible right leg (#6847j) and left leg (#8427g) torn from other androids; a damaged right leg (#6321t) was incompatible.

In the landfill a dying android grabbed you and said: “There’s a place where we can be free! Find {{Jericho}}!” Before he shut down he passed you a copy of the key he carried, the way to find {{Jericho}}.
Leaving the pit, you squeezed through a passage of dying androids whose hands grabbed you and tried to hold you down.
In the junkyard, broken androids kept repeating their old service phrases, and one muttered that he had to get to {{Jericho}}, where androids live in freedom.
An optical unit you examined in the junkyard (#9754h) was functional but incompatible with you.
In the junkyard you took your new optical unit, #8087q with a blue iris, from a talking AK700 head, after a crane dumped a load of bodies on you and you dug yourself out.
An audio processor you examined in the junkyard (#4807) was functional but incompatible with you.
You took your new audio processor (#4903) from a head on the right side of the junkyard.
You took your new pump regulator (#2886) from a dead android near the slope of the junkyard.
You climbed out of the landfill and pulled the LED from your temple, so you now pass for human. Your right eye is now blue (#8087q). You set off for the city to find {{Jericho}}.
At the landfill a broken android caught hold of you and said: “There’s a place where we can be free! Find {{Jericho}}!” He left a key in your memory.
On the train, androids must ride in a designated area. In human clothes and without the light at your temple, you rode among the humans unnoticed.
The way to {{Jericho}} is a trail of marks hidden in murals and painted signs. Only an android carrying the key can decode them, and each one shows what the next looks like.

Residents of a {{Detroit}} suburb watched a chase after a police manhunt, with roadblocks and dozens of police interviews, flushed out a fugitive. The rogue AX400 model is thought to be suffering from an extremely rare malfunction and took extreme measures to avoid the police, even dashing across a busy highway. Eyewitness statements are inconclusive, there is no official report, and no {{CyberLife}} spokesperson was available for comment.

NASA has launched a crew of five androids on a three-year journey to Io, one of Jupiter’s moons: the first all-machine crew. NASA’s director calls androids an extraordinary asset for the conquest of space, because cosmic radiation destroys human DNA. No return journey is planned; the androids will work on Io for several months before the extreme conditions destroy them.

At a bus stop you overheard two people talking about {{Carl}}: the woman hoped he makes it, the man had read somewhere that his android attacked him, and she told him not to believe everything he reads.
The marks led you from mural to mural down the street, to a fenced-off wall where the street ends.
Hidden behind a white car in a junkyard on the trail lay a dead android.
Some of the trail’s marks can only be seen from above; it took you up onto the rooftops.
You crossed a gap between rooftops by preconstructing the route first, rehearsing each move in your mind.
Another dead android lay next to a container in a yard further along the trail.
The trail led up a building wall and into an abandoned office.
{{Jericho}} is an old rusted freighter at the abandoned docks, its name painted on the hull. The trail of marks ends there.
A rusted bridge on the docks collapsed when you tried to cross it toward the ship.
To get into {{Jericho}} you jumped from the arm of a crane into the water inside the ship.
Inside, {{Jericho}} is dark and flooded: corridors of locked hatches and empty rooms.
You found {{Jericho}}. Other androids are hiding in the dark inside the ship, and one of them welcomed you.
{{Jericho}} is the hold of an old ship where androids who escaped their owners hide. There you met {{Josh}}, {{Simon}} and {{North}}.
{{North}} told you to go and see {{Lucy}}: “She may be able to help you.”

{{Lucy}} stopped your bleeding and gave you blue blood to drink. Holding your hand, she said: “You had it all and you lost it all... You’ve seen hell and now hell lives in you... A part of shadow and a part of light... Which will prevail? Your choices will shape our destiny.”
A damaged android in the hold told you humans tied him to the back of a car “to have fun”. He does not want to shut down.

{{Josh}} told you the boy was thrown out by his owners and lived on the streets. The androids of {{Jericho}} need blue blood and biocomponents; they salvage what they can from those who shut down, but there is never enough: “We’re slowly dying out…”
A dying android by the fire asked you whether you knew what happens after death. You did not. She said she was glad to meet you, and shut down.
An empty {{CyberLife}} crate in the hold told you where parts come from: the {{CyberLife}} warehouses in {{Detroit}} Harbor, which hold everything {{Jericho}} needs.
You proposed stealing spare parts and blue blood from the {{CyberLife}} warehouses at the docks in {{Detroit}} Harbor, without fighting. {{North}}, {{Simon}} and {{Josh}} agreed to come.

You, {{North}}, {{Simon}} and {{Josh}} have slipped into the docks at night to steal spare parts and blue blood for {{Jericho}} from the {{CyberLife}} warehouse. {{Josh}} said that if you are caught, you are dead.
The {{CyberLife}} warehouse crates hold biocomponents and blue blood, and you have started filling your bags.
The truck key is on the console in the guard station, where two human guards sit talking. Guard dogs are kept outside.
You brought a stolen truck full of spare parts back to {{Jericho}}.
In {{Ferndale}} you saw a man berate an android: “You klutz! Pick them up! And make it snappy!”
Your plan: take the {{Channel16}} control room on the top floor of the {{Stratford}} Tower and broadcast a message from the androids to the humans.
Supervisor’s desk, SMART WATCH: MODEL T215. Phone number: 555 847 33.
Supervisor’s desk, {{WILSON}}, {{EMILY}}: Supervisor’s Daughter. Child registered at: {{SaintRose}} school.
Supervisor’s desk, {{WILSON}}, {{ELIZABETH}}: Born: 03/25/1999. Desk manager.
Supervisor’s desk, PARKING BADGE: Car registration - API 1704. Floor -3 - Spot A21.
Supervisor’s desk, HOME ADDRESS: 4685 {{MichiganStreet}}, {{Detroit}}. Fire safety rating: poor.
You woke the android receptionist in the {{Stratford}} Tower lobby; she let you through security to the elevators.
On the forty-seventh floor of the tower, staff grumbled: “People can’t get jobs, and we’re sending rockets into space!”

{{Detroit}} Today reports that the Department of Defense is poised to order 50,000 android troopers, on top of an estimated 200,000 already in service across the US military, among them 2,500 “Myrmidons”, elite prototypes capable of infiltration and assassination missions; the Army’s fighting forces are already mainly androids. The head of a war victims charity warns that “machines are focused on a single task, and don’t evaluate moral consequences well - this will mean more civilian deaths”.

Century reports that barely a year after her election, President {{Warren}}, a former vlogger with no experience in government, is under investigation over whether {{CyberLife}} helped her obtain compromising information about her opponent, while she faces the highest unemployment rate in American history and a conflict in the Arctic that threatens world peace.

{{Channel16}}’s top story: {{CyberLife}} has officially become the world’s first trillion-dollar company. With more than fifty million androids sold in America alone, the company {{Kamski}} founded just ten years ago has had the fastest economic growth in history, in spite of criticism of the impact of androids on human employment and questions about its semi-monopoly.
Disguised as a maintenance android with a badge and a cart, you let {{North}} into the forty-seventh floor; two guards stood at the server room door.
You and {{North}} climbed the outside of the {{Stratford}} Tower on a rope from the forty-seventh floor to the top floor.
{{Simon}} and {{Josh}} joined you and {{North}} on the top floor of the tower.
You broadcast your message with the skin of your face switched off, showing the humans an android’s face.
Every network showed your broadcast from the {{Stratford}} Tower: an android without its skin, listing demands and asking for equal rights.

The plan: five teams strike the five {{CyberLife}} stores in {{Detroit}} at the same moment, 2 AM; each hacks its store’s security, frees the androids inside and gets them out before the police come. No violence.
The store you and {{North}} have come to free is a {{CyberLife}} store on a plaza beside a park downtown.

“The question everyone’s asking”: following the pirate broadcast, everybody wants to know who this android is. A federal investigation is underway to track the machine down and neutralize it; eyewitnesses say it broke into the city’s TV news tower with a group of armed, organized accomplices who were clearly following its orders; and until this dangerous machine is destroyed, the speculation will continue.

A study by an expert panel found that androids would be more effective than humans in a number of government positions, including President: they are incorruptible and indifferent to any form of pressure, and can pursue clear goals without worrying about popularity or re-election. The panel calls it “just a matter of time” until public opinion is ready to accept the idea.
All five teams strike in ten minutes. The plan for your store: neutralize the alarm systems and secure the area, then get inside and free the androids.

Scanning the store: the window, “REINFORCED GRID SHUTTER / Fiber-Reinforced Polymer / Toughened Glass Door”; the androids on display, “AP SERIES / Housekeeping and Private Assistance / First Rollout Date : July 2038”, “AX SERIES / Housekeeping and Private Assistance / First Rollout Date : May 2036” and “WJ SERIES / Janitoring and Office Maintenance / First Rollout Date : October 2036”; three cameras, “SECURITY CAMERA / NETWORK #894.084.241.056”, Device IDs #615.100.947.517.4, .5 and .6. The cameras’ network leads across the road to the alarm’s junction, where two androids are working in a hole in the sidewalk.
The alarm junction: “ALARM NETWORK / {{CyberLife}} NETID #1523 / GRID Junction 23.A”.
You freed the androids in the store; they said they are with you and would follow you.
Police officers came into the park and shot down many of the androids you freed as they fled, among them an android with {{North}}’s face.
The news called the night’s raids on the {{CyberLife}} stores a coordinated terrorist attack and asked whether androids have become a threat to security.
The news reported pro-android graffiti and slogans on the shop windows near the {{CyberLife}} stores.
The news reported that two policemen were found in a state of shock near one of the stores.

{{Detroit}} Today (“ANDROID RIOT: {{Detroit}} neighborhoods vandalized by psychotic machines”) reported that {{CyberLife}} stores were broken into and their entire stock of androids stolen; that leaked CCTV footage showed androids emerging from manhole covers and smashing store windows; that in the worst incident, in the park, officers “had no choice but to open fire on the malfunctioning machines”; and that an anonymous witness claimed “I was personally attacked by the ringleader. It threatened me with a knife.” Some already connect it to the recent attack on the broadcast tower.

In the mall before the march, shoppers talked about the androids’ broadcast (“Still can’t believe that fucking video they made…”), one wondering whether androids human enough to want rights might deserve them, another calling it “liberal bullshit”; a woman on the phone was sure {{CyberLife}} is recording everything androids hear.
On the march, people on the sidewalks shouted at the androids: “Good for you! You have a right to be free!” “We’re on your side!” “Equal rights for androids!” “Fight for your rights!”
After the counsel, {{North}} left you alone in the captain’s cabin.
You went back into {{Carl}}’s house; the alarm still let you in: “Welcome home, {{Markus}}.”

{{Leo}} left {{Carl}} a message: he is getting out of the hospital, he knows {{Carl}} stayed with him while he was asleep, he is sorry, he will stop the drugs, he would like to come by, and he is proud to be his son.
{{Carl}} has a new android caretaker; you converted him with a touch to get to {{Carl}}.
{{Carl}} survived, but he is gravely ill and bedridden at home.
{{Carl}} told you: “Being alive is making choices… You have to accept the world as it is… or fight to change it… You’re my son… Face the abyss… but don’t let it consume you.”
You saw {{Carl}} one last time before the end.
{{Jericho}} was never found; your people are gathered in the ship’s hold.

On November 10th President {{Warren}} declared a national curfew: civilian movement controlled, the right to assembly suspended, communications restricted, all androids to be handed over to the authorities, and temporary camps set up in every major city to contain and destroy them.
At her press conference, President {{Warren}} was asked about androids as intelligent life. President {{Warren}}: “That’s ridiculous. Next question, please?”

At her press conference, President {{Warren}} was asked about the camps. President {{Warren}}: “That’s absurd. There’s absolutely no connection. Androids are not living beings. All we are doing is destroying defective machines.”

At her press conference, President {{Warren}} was asked about public opinion. President {{Warren}}: “Public opinion is one thing, the security of the state is another. These deviants are dangerous and my highest priority is to protect the American people.”

At her press conference, President {{Warren}} was asked about {{CyberLife}}’s future. President {{Warren}}: “We’re working very closely with {{CyberLife}} to neutralize all deviants. I won’t make any comments about anything else until we have dealt with the android question.”
The soldiers opened fire on your unarmed march; androids fell around you, live on the news.
The soldiers held their fire after the first volley, and your people stood their ground in front of them.

{{Detroit}} Today’s front page reads “They Defy Us”: “Androids rise up in {{Detroit}}”, beside “President {{Warren}} to make state visit to United Kingdom” and “NATO Security Council divided over Arctic dispute”.

The article: “Androids have taken to the streets of {{Detroit}} in apocalyptic scenes.” The city is “in the grip of a national product recall, with androids seized from every home and business to be destroyed by the authorities as a precaution”, and a group of androids “have gathered in a terrifying show of force”, barricaded “in a fortified position” and “angling for an armed confrontation”.

Captain {{Fowler}} of the {{Detroit}} police is quoted: “The safety of {{Detroit}}’s people is our first priority. We hope to bring this matter to a swift conclusion and refocus on collecting androids as soon as possible.”
You refused {{Perkins}}; the army attacked the barricade, and the news reported it was attacking peaceful protesters.
